songs.title: 'Take Up Thy Cross', the Savior Said
songs.author: Charles William Everest (1814-1877)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
"Take up thy cross," the Savior said,
"If thou wouldst My disciple be;
Deny thyself, the world forsake,
And humbly follow after Me."

[2]
Take up thy cross, let not its weight
Fill thy weak spirit with alarm;
His strength shall bear thy spirit up,
And brace thy heart and nerve thine arm.

[3]
Take up thy cross, nor heed the shame,
Nor let thy foolish pride rebel;
Thy Lord for thee the cross endured,
And saved thy soul from death and hell.

[4]
Take up thy cross then in His strength,
And calmly sin's wild deluge brave,
'Twill guide thee to a better home,
It points to glory o'er the grave.

[5]
Take up thy cross and follow Christ,
Nor think til death to lay it down;
For only those who bear the cross
May hope to wear the glorious crown.

[6]
To Thee, great Lord, the One in Three,
All praise forevermore ascend:
O grant us in our home to see
The heavenly life that knows no end.

songs.title: 'Tis Midnight and On Olive's Brow
songs.author: William Bingham Tappan (1794-1849)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
'Tis midnight, and on Olive's brow
The star is dimmed that lately shone;
'Tis midnight, in the garden now
The suff'ring Savior prays alone.

[2]
'Tis midnight, and from all removed
Immanuel wrestles, lone, with fears;
E'en the disciple whom He loved
Heeds not his Master's grief and tears.

[3]
'Tis midnight, from the heav'nly plains
Are borne the songs that angels know;
Unheard by mortals are the strains
That sweetly soothe the Savior's woe.

songs.title: 'Twas On That Dark, That Doleful Night
songs.author: Isaac Watts (1674-1748)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
'Twas on that dark, that doleful night
When pow'rs of earth and hell arose
Against the Son of God's delight,
And friends betrayed Him to His foes:

[2]
Before the mournful scene began,
He took the bread, and blessed, and brake:
What love through all His actions ran!
What wondrous words of grace He spake!

[3]
"This is My body, broke for sin;
Receive and eat the living food:"
Then took the cup, and blessed the wine;
"'Tis the new cov'nant in My blood."

[4]
For us His flesh with nails was torn,
He bore the scourge, He felt the thorn;
And justice poured upon His head
Its heavy vengeance in our stead.

[5]
For us His vital blood was spilt,
To buy the pardon of our guilt,
When, for black crimes of biggest size,
He gave His soul a sacrifice.

[6]
"Do this," He cried, "till time shall end,
In memory of your dying friend;
Meet at My table, and record
The love of your departed Lord."

[7]
Jesus, Thy feast we celebrate,
We show Thy death, we sing Thy name,
Till Thou return, and we shall eat
The marriage supper of the Lamb.

songs.title: A Child of The King
songs.author: Harriet Eugenia Peck Buell (1834-1910)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
My Father is rich in houses and lands,
He holdeth the wealth of the world in His hands!
Of rubies and diamonds of silver and gold
His coffers are full,- He has riches untold.

[1.2]
I'm a child of the King, a child of the King:
With Jesus my Savior I'm a child of the King.

[2]
My Father's own Son, the Savior of men,
Once wander'd o'er earth as the poorest of men,
But now He is reigning forever on high,
And will give me a home in heaven by and by.

[3.1]
I once was an outcast stranger on earth,
A sinner by choice, and an alien by birth!

[3.2]
But I've been adopted, my name's written down,-
An heir to a mansion, a robe, and
A crown.

[4.1]
A tent or a cottage, why should I care?
They're building a palace for me over there!
Tho' exiled from home, yet, still I may sing:

[4.2]
All glory to God,
I'm the child of a King.

songs.title: A Great and Mighty Wonder
songs.author: Germanus of Constantinople (634-734) (trad. John Mason Neale (1818-1866))
songs.composer: K�ln, 1599 from Altes Catholische Geistliche Kirchengeseng
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
A great and mighty wonder,
A full and holy cure:
The virgin bears the Infant
With virgin honor pure!

[1.2]
Repeat the hymn again:
"To God on high be glory
And peace on earth to men!"

[2]
The Word becomes incarnate and yet remains on high,
And cherubim sing anthems to shepherds from the sky.

[3]
While thus they sing your Monarch, those bright angelic bands,
Rejoice, ye vales and mountains, ye oceans, clap your hands.

[4]
Since all He comes to ransom, by all be He adored,
The Infant born in Bethl'em, the Savior and the Lord.

[5]
And idol forms shall perish, and error shall decay,
And Christ shall wield His scepter, our Lord and God for aye.

songs.title: A Lamb Goes Uncomplaining Forth
songs.author: Paul Gerhardt (1607-1676) (trad. composite)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
A Lamb goes uncomplaining forth,
The guilt of all men bearing;
And laden with the sins of earth,
None else the burden sharing!

[1.2]
Goes patient on, grow weak and faint,
To slaughter led without complaint,
That spotless life to offer;

[1.3]
Bears shame and stripes, and wounds and death,
Anguish and mockery, and saith,
"Willing all this I suffer."

[2.1]
This Lamb is Christ, the soul's great Friend,
The Lamb of God, our Savior;
Him God the Father chose to send
To gain for us His favor.

[2.2]
"Go forth, My Son," the Father saith,
"And free men from the fear of death,
From guilt and condemnation.

[2.3]
The wrath and stripes are hard to bear,
But by Thy Passion men shall share
The fruit of Thy salvation."

[3.1]
"Yea, Father, yea, most willingly
I'll bear what Thou commandest;
My will conforms to Thy decree,
I do what Thou demandest."

[3.2]
O wondrous Love, what hast Thou done!
The Father offers up His Son!
The Son, content, descendeth!
O Love, how strong Thou art to save!

[3.3]
Thou beddest Him within the grave
Whose word the mountains rendeth.

[4.1]
Thou lay'st Him, Love, upon the cross,
With nails and spear Him bruising;
Thou slay'st Him as a lamb, His loss
From soul and body oozing;

[4.2]
From body 'tis the crimson flood
Of precious sacrificial blood
From soul, the strength of anguish:

[4.3]
My gain it is; sweet Lamb to Thee
What can I give, whose love to me
For me doth make Thee languish?

[5.1]
Lord, all my life I'll cleave to Thee,
Thy love fore'er beholding,
Thee ever, as Thou ever me,
With loving arms enfolding.

[5.2]
Yea, Thou shalt be my Beaconlight,
To guide me safe through death's dark night.
And cheer my heart in sorrow;

[5.3]
Henceforth myself and all that's mine
To Thee, my Savior, I consign,
From whom all things I borrow.

[6.1]
From morn till eve my theme shall be
Thy mercy's wondrous measure;
To sacrifice myself for Thee
Shall be my aim and pleasure.

[6.2]
My stream of life shall ever be
A current flowing ceaselessly,
Thy constant praise outpouring.

[6.3]
I'll treasure in my memory,
O Lord, all Thou hast done for me,
Thy gracious love adoring.

[7.1]
Enlarge, my heart's own shrine, and swell,
To thee shall now be given
A treasure that doth far excel
The worth of earth and heaven.

[7.2]
Away with the Arabian gold,
With treasures of an earthly mold!
I've found a better jewel.

[7.3]
My priceless treasure, Lord my God,
Is Thy most holy, precious blood,
Which flowed from wounds so cruel.

[8.1]
This treasure ever I'll employ,
This every aid shall yield me;
In sorrow it shall be my joy,
In conflict it shall shield me;

[8.2]
In joy, the music of my feast,
And when all else has lost its zest,
This manna still shall feed me;
In thirst my drink; in want my food;

[8.3]
My company in solitude,
To comfort and to lead me.

[9.1]
Of death I am no more afraid,
New life from Thee is flowing;
Thy cross affords me cooling shade
When noonday's sun is glowing.

[9.2]
When by my grief I am oppressed,
On Thee my weary soul shall rest
Serenely as on pillows.

[9.3]
Thou art my Anchor when by woe
My bark is driven to and fro
On trouble's surging billows.

[10.1]
And when Thy glory I shall see
And taste Thy kingdom's pleasure,
Thy blood my royal robe shall be,
My joy beyond all measure.

[10.2]
When I appear before Thy throne,
Thy righteousness shall be my crown-
With these I need not hide me.

[10.3]
And there, in garments richly wrought
As Thine own bride, I shall be brought
To stand in joy beside Thee.

songs.title: A Mighty Fortress Is Our God
songs.author: Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. Frederic Henry Hedge (1805-1890))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
A mighty fortress is our God,
A bulwark never failing;
Our helper He, amid the flood
Of mortal ills prevailing:

[1.2]
For still our ancient foe
Doth seek to work us woe;

[1.3]
His craft and pow'r are great,
And, armed with cruel hate,
On earth is not his equal.

[2.1]
Did we in our own strength confide,
Our striving would be losing;
Were not the right Man on our side,
The Man of God's own choosing:

[2.2]
Dost ask who that may be?
Christ Jesus, it is He;

[2.3]
Lord Sabaoth, His name,
From age to age the same,
And He must win the battle.

[3.1]
And though this world, with devils filled,
Should threaten to undo us,
We will not fear, for God hath willed
His truth to triumph through us:

[3.2]
The Prince of Darkness grim,
We tremble not for him;

[3.3]
His rage we can endure,
For lo, his doom is sure,
One little word shall fell him.

[4.1]
That word above all earthly pow'rs,
No thanks to them, abideth;
The Spirit and the gifts are ours
Through Him who with us sideth:

[4.2]
Let goods and kindred go,
This mortal life also;
The body they may kill:

[4.3]
God's truth abideth still,
His kingdom is forever.

songs.title: Abide With Me
songs.author: Henry F. Lyte (1793-1847)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Abide with me; fast falls the eventide;
The darkness deepens; Lord with me abide.
When other helpers fail and comforts flee,
Help of the helpless, O abide with me.

[2]
Swift to its close ebbs out life's little day;
Earth's joys grow dim; its glories pass away;
Change and decay in all around I see;
O Thou who changest not, abide with me.

[3]
Not a brief glance I beg, a passing word;
But as Thou dwell'st with Thy disciples, Lord,
Familiar, condescending, patient, free.
Come not to sojourn, but abide with me.

[4]
Come not in terrors, as the King of kings,
But kind and good, with healing in Thy wings,
Tears for all woes, a heart for every plea?
Come, Friend of sinners, and thus bide with me.

[5]
Thou on my head in early youth didst smile;
And, though rebellious and perverse meanwhile,
Thou hast not left me, oft as I left Thee,
On to the close, O Lord, abide with me.

[6]
I need Thy presence every passing hour.
What but Thy grace can foil the tempter's power?
Who, like Thyself, my guide and stay can be?
Through cloud and sunshine, Lord, abide with me.

[7]
I fear no foe, with Thee at hand to bless;
Ills have no weight, and tears no bitterness.
Where is death's sting? Where, grave, thy victory?
I triumph still, if Thou abide with me.

[8]
Hold Thou Thy cross before my closing eyes;
Shine through the gloom and point me to the skies.
Heaven's morning breaks, and earth's vain shadows flee;
In life, in death, O Lord, abide with me.

songs.title: Abide, O Dearest Jesus
songs.author: Joshua Stegmann (1588-1632) (trad. August Crull (1845-1923))
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Abide, O dearest Jesus,
Among us with Thy grace,
That Satan may not harm us,
Nor we to sin give place.

[2]
Abide, O dear Redeemer,
Among us with Thy Word,
And thus now and hereafter
True peace and joy afford.

[3]
Abide with heav'nly brightness
Among us, precious Light;
Thy truth direct, and keep us
From error's gloomy night.

[4]
Abide with richest blessings
Among us, bounteous Lord;
Let us in grace and wisdom
Grow daily through Thy Word.

[5]
Abide with Thy protection
Among us, Lord, our Strength,
Lest world and Satan fell us
And overcome at length.

[6]
Abide, O faithful Savior, Among us with Thy love;
Grant steadfastness, and help us To reach our home above.

songs.title: All Creatures of Our God and King
songs.author: Francis of Assisi (1181/1182-1226) (trad. William Henry Draper (1855-1933))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
All creatures of our God and King Lift
Up your voice and with us sing,
Alleluia!
Alleluia!

[1.2]
Thou burning sun with golden beam,
Thou silver moon with softer gleam!
O praise Him!
O praise Him!

[1.3]
Alleluia!
Alleluia!
Alleluia!

[2.1]
Thou rushing wind that art so strong Ye
Clouds that sail in Heaven along,
O praise Him!
Alleluia!

[2.2]
Thou rising moon, in praise rejoice,
Ye lights of evening, find a voice!

[3.1]
Thou flowing water, pure and clear,
Make music for thy Lord to hear,
O praise Him!
Alleluia!

[3.2]
Thou fire so masterful and bright,
That givest man both warmth and light.

[4.1]
Dear mother earth, who day by day Unfoldest blessings on our way,
O praise Him!
Alleluia!

[4.2]
The flowers and fruits that in thee grow,
Let them His glory also show.

[5.1]
And all ye men of tender heart,
Forgiving others, take your part,
O sing ye!
Alleluia!

[5.2]
Ye who long pain and sorrow bear,
Praise God and on Him cast your care!

[6.1]
And thou most kind and gentle Death,
Waiting to hush our latest breath,
O praise Him! Alleluia!

[6.2]
Thou leadest home the child of God,
And Christ our Lord the way hath trod.

[7.1]
Let all things their Creator bless,
And worship Him in humbleness,
O praise Him! Alleluia!

[7.2]
Praise, praise the Father, praise the Son,
And praise the Spirit, Three in One!

songs.title: All Depends On Our Possessing
songs.author: unknown (trad. Catherine Winkworth (1827-1878))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
All depends on our possessing
God's abundant grace and blessing,
Though all earthly wealth depart.

[1.2]
He who trusts with faith unshaken
In His God is not forsaken
And e'er keeps a dauntless heart.

[2.1]
He who hitherto hath fed me
And to many joys hath led me,
Is and ever shall be mine.

[2.2]
He who did so gently school me,
He who still doth guide and rule me,
Will remain my Help divine.

[3.1]
Many spend their lives in fretting
Over trifles and in getting
Things that have no solid ground.

[3.2]
I shall strive to win a treasure
That will bring me lasting pleasure
And that now is seldom found.

[4.1]
When with sorrow I am stricken,
Hope my heart anew will quicken,
All my longing shall be stilled.

[4.2]
To His loving- kindness tender
Soul and body I surrender;
For in Him alone I build.

[5.1]
Well He knows what best to grant me;
All the longing hopes that haunt me,
Joy and sorrow, have their day.

[5.2]
I shall doubt His wisdom never,
As God wills, so be it ever,
I to Him commit my way.

[6.1]
If on earth my days He lengthen,
He my weary soul will strengthen;
All my trust in Him I place.

[6.2]
Earthly wealth is not abiding,
Like a stream away is gliding;
Safe I anchor in His grace.

songs.title: All Glory, Laud, and Honor
songs.author: Theodulf of Orleans (760-821) (trad. John Mason Neale (1818-1866))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
All glory, laud and honor,
To Thee, Redeemer, King,
To Whom the lips of children
Made sweet hosannas ring.

[1.2]
Thou art the King of Israel,
Thou David's royal Son,
Who in the Lord's Name comest,
The King and Blessed One.

[2]
The company of angels Are praising Thee on High,
And mortal men and all things Created make reply.

[3]
The people of the Hebrews With palms before Thee went;
Our prayer and praise and anthems Before Thee we present.

[4]
To Thee, before Thy passion,
They sang their hymns of praise;
To Thee, now high exalted,
Our melody we raise.

[5]
Thou didst accept their praises;
Accept the prayers we bring,
Who in all good delightest,
Thou good and gracious King.

songs.title: All Hail The Power Of Jesus' Name
songs.author: Edward Perronet (1726-1792)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
All hail the pow'r of Jesus' Name!
Let angels prostrate fall;
Bring forth the royal diadem,
And crown Him Lord of all.

[1.2]
Bring forth the royal diadem,
And crown Him Lord of all.

[2.1]
Let highborn seraphs tune the lyre,
And as they tune it, fall
Before His face Who tunes their choir,
And crown Him Lord of all.

[2.2]
Before His face Who tunes their choir,
And crown Him Lord of all.

[3.1]
Crown Him, ye morning stars of light,
Who fixed this floating ball;
Now hail the strength of Israel's might,
And crown Him Lord of all.

[3.2]
Now hail the strength of Israel's might,
And crown Him Lord of all.

[4.1]
Crown Him, ye martyrs of your God,
Who from His altar call;
Extol the Stem of Jesse's Rod,
And crown Him Lord of all.

[4.2]
Extol the Stem of Jesse's Rod,
And crown Him Lord of all.

[5.1]
Ye seed of Israel's chosen race,
Ye ransomed from the fall,
Hail Him Who saves you by His grace,
And crown Him Lord of all.

[5.2]
Hail Him Who saves you by His grace,
And crown Him Lord of all.

[6]
Hail Him, ye heirs of David's line, whom David Lord did call,
The God incarnate, Man divine, and crown Him Lord of all,
The God incarnate, Man divine, and crown Him Lord of all.

[7]
Sinners, whose love can ne'er forget the wormwood and the gall,
Go spread your trophies at His feet, and crown Him Lord of all.
Go spread your trophies at His feet, and crown Him Lord of all.

[8]
Let every tribe and every tongue before Him prostrate fall
And shout in universal song the crown�d Lord of all.
And shout in universal song the crown�d Lord of all.

songs.title: All My Heart This Night Rejoices
songs.author: Paul Gerhardt (1607-1676) (trad. Catherine Winkworth (1827-1878))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
All my heart this night rejoices,
As I hear,
Far and near,
Sweetest angel voices;

[1.2]
"Christ is born," their choirs are singing,
Till the air
Ev'rywhere
Now with joy is ringing.

[2.1]
For it dawns,- the promised morrow
Of His birth
Who the earth
Rescues from her sorrow.

[2.2]
God to wear our form descendeth,
Of His grace
To our race
Here His Son He lendeth:

[3.1]
Yea, so truly for us careth,
That His Son
All we've done
As our off'ring beareth;

[3.2]
As our Lamb who, dying for us,
Bears our load,
And to God
Doth in peace restore us.

[4.1]
Hark! a voice from yonder manger,
Soft and sweet,
Doth entreat,
"Flee from woe and danger;

[4.2]
Brethren come, from all doth grieve you
You are freed,
All you need
I will surely give you."

[5.1]
Come then, let us hasten yonder;
Here let all,
Great and small,
Kneel in awe and wonder.

[5.2]
Love Him who with love is yearning;
Hail the Star
That from far
Bright with hope is burning!

[6]
Ye who pine in weary sadness, Weep no more, For the door
Now is found of gladness. Cling to Him for He will guide you
Where no cross, Pain or loss, Can again betide you.

[7]
Hither come, ye heavy\- hearted, Who for sin Deep within,
Long and sore have smarted; For the poison'd wounds you're feeling
Help is near, One is here Mighty for their healing!

[8]
Hither come, ye poor and wretched; Know His will Is to fill
Every hand outstretched; Here are riches without measure,
Here forget All regret, Fill your hearts with treasure.

[9]
Blessed Savior, let me find Thee! Keep Thou me Close to Thee,
Cast me not behind Thee! Life of life, my heart Thou stillest,
Calm I rest On Thy breast, All this void Thou fillest.

[10]
Thee, dear Lord, with heed I'll cherish, Live to Thee, And with Thee
Dying, shall not perish; But shall dwell with Thee for ever,
Far on high In the joy That can alter never.

songs.title: All Praise to Jesus' Hallowed Name
songs.author: German, Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. Richard Massie (1800-1887))
songs.lyrics:
[1]
All praise to Jesus' hallowed Name Who of
Virgin pure became True man for us!
The angels sing As the glad news to earth they bring.
Hallelujah!

[2]
Th'Eternal Father's only Son For a manger leaves
His throne Disguised in our poor flesh and
Blood See now the everlasting Good.

[3]
He whom the world could not inwrap Yonder lies in Mary's lap;
He is become an infant small,
Who by His might upholdeth all.

[4]
Th'Eternal Light, come down from heav'n,
Hath to us new sunshine giv'n;
It shineth in the midst of night,
And maketh us the sons of light.

[5.1]
The Father's Son,
God ever- blest,
In the world became a guest;

[5.2]
He leads us from this vale of tears,
And makes us in his kingdom heirs.

[6]
He came to earth so mean and poor, Man to pity and restore,
And make us rich in heaven above, Equal with angels through his love.

[7]
All this He did to show His grace To our poor and sinful race;
For this let Christendom adore And praise His name for evermore.

songs.title: All Praise To Thee, My God, This Night
songs.author: Thomas Ken (1637-1711)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
All praise to Thee, my God, this night,
For all the blessings of the light!
Keep me, O keep me, King of kings,
Beneath Thine own almighty wings.

[2]
Forgive me, Lord, for Thy dear Son,
The ill that I this day have done,
That with the world, myself, and Thee,
I, ere I sleep, at peace may be.

[3]
Teach me to live, that I may dread
The grave as little as my bed.
Teach me to die, that so I may
Rise glorious at the judgment day.

[4]
O may my soul on Thee repose,
And with sweet sleep mine eyelids close,
Sleep that may me more vig'rous make
To serve my God when I awake.

[5]
When in the night I sleepless lie,
My soul with heav'nly thoughts supply;
Let no ill dreams disturb my rest,
No pow'rs of darkness me molest.

[6]
O when shall I, in endless day,
For ever chase dark sleep away,
And hymns divine with angels sing,
All praise to thee, eternal King?

[7]
Praise God, from Whom all blessings flow;
Praise Him, all creatures here below;
Praise Him above, ye heavenly host;
Praise Father, Son, and Holy Ghost.

songs.title: All Who Believe and Are Baptized
songs.author: Thomas Hansen Kingo (1634-1703) (trad. George Alfred Taylor Rygh (1860-1942))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
All who believe and are baptized
Shall see the Lord's salvation;
Baptized into the death of Christ,
They are a new creation.

[1.2]
Through Christ's redemption they shall stand
Among the glorious heav'nly band
Of every tribe and nation.

[2.1]
With one accord, O God, we pray:
Grant us thy Holy Spirit;
Look thou on our infirmity
Through Jesus' blood and merit.

[2.2]
Grant us to grow in grace each day
That by this sacrament we may
Eternal life inherit.

songs.title: Alleluia, Alleluia! Hearts to Heaven and Voices Raise
songs.author: Christopher Wordsworth (1807-1885)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Alleluia, alleluia!
Hearts to Heav'n and voices raise:
Sing to God a hymn of gladness,
Sing to God a hymn of praise.

[1.2]
He, who on the cross a Victim,
For the world's salvation bled,
Jesus Christ, the King of glory,
Now is risen from the dead.

[2.1]
Now the iron bars are broken,
Christ from death to life is born,
Glorious life, and life immortal,
On the holy Easter morn.

[2.2]
Christ has triumphed, and we conquer
By His mighty enterprise:
We with Him to life eternal
By His resurrection rise.

[3.1]
Christ is risen, Christ, the first fruits
Of the holy harvest field,
Which will all its full abundance
At His second coming yield:

[3.2]
Then the golden ears of harvest
Will their heads before Him wave,
Ripened by His glorious sunshine
From the furrows of the grave.

[4.1]
Christ is risen, we are risen!
Shed upon us heav'nly grace,
Rain and dew and gleams of glory
From the brightness of Thy face;

[4.2]
That we, with our hearts in Heaven,
Here on earth may fruitful be,
And by angel hands be gathered,
And be ever, Lord, with Thee.

[5.1]
Alleluia, alleluia!
Glory be to God on high;
Alleluia! to the Savior
Who has gained the victory;

[5.2]
Alleluia! to the Spirit,
Fount of love and sanctity:
Alleluia, alleluia!
To the Triune Majesty.

songs.title: Alleluia, Sing To Jesus!
songs.author: William Chatterton Dix (1837-1865)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Alleluia! sing to Jesus!
His the scepter, His the throne.
Alleluia! His the triumph,
His the victory alone.

[1.2]
Hark! the songs of peaceful Zion
Thunder like a mighty flood.
Jesus out of every nation
Has redeemed us by His blood.

[2.1]
Alleluia! not as orphans
Are we left in sorrow now;
Alleluia! He is near us,
Faith believes, nor questions how;

[2.2]
Though the cloud from sight received Him
When the forty days were o'er
Shall our hearts forget His promise,
"I am with you evermore"?

[3.1]
Alleluia! bread of angels,
Thou on earth our food, our stay;
Alleluia! here the sinful
Flee to Thee from day to day:

[3.2]
Intercessor, Friend of sinners,
Earth's Redeemer, plead for me,
Where the songs of all the sinless
Sweep across the crystal sea.

[4.1]
Alleluia!
King eternal,
Thee the Lord of lords we own;
Alleluia!

[4.2]
Born of Mary,
Earth Thy footstool,
Heaven Thy throne:

[4.3]
Thou within the veil hast entered, robed in
Flesh our great High Priest;
Thou on earth both priest and victim in the Eucharistic feast.

songs.title: Almighty God Your Word Is Cast
songs.author: John Cawood (1775-1852)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Almighty God, Your Word is cast
Like seed into the ground;
Now let the dew of Heav'n descend,
And righteous fruits abound.

[2]
Let not the foe of Christ and man
This holy seed remove,
But give it root in ev'ry heart
To bring forth fruits of love.

[3]
Let not the world's deceitful cares
The rising plant destroy.
But let it yield a hundredfold
The fruits of peace and joy.

[4]
Nor let Your Word so kindly sent
To raise us to Your throne
Return to You, and sadly tell
That we reject Your Son.

[5]
Oft as the precious seed is sown,
Your quick'ning grace bestow,
That all whose souls the truth receive,
Its saving power may know.

[6]
Great God, come down and on Your Word
Your mighty power bestow,
That all who hear the joyful sound,
Your saving grace may know.

songs.title: Amazing Grace
songs.author: John Newton (1725-1807)
songs.composer: James P. Carrell (1787-1854), David L. Clayton
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Amazing grace! How sweet the sound
That saved a wretch like me!
I once was lost, but now am found;
Was blind, but now I see.

[2]
'Twas grace that taught my heart to fear,
And grace my fears relieved;
How precious did that grace appear
The hour I first believed.

[3]
Through many dangers, toils and snares,
I have already come;
'Tis grace hath brought me safe thus far,
And grace will lead me home.

[4]
The Lord has promised good to me,
His Word my hope secures;
He will my Shield and Portion be,
As long as life endures.

[5]
Yea, when this flesh and heart shall fail,
And mortal life shall cease,
I shall possess, within the veil,
A life of joy and peace.

[6]
The earth shall soon dissolve like snow,
The sun forbear to shine;
But God, Who called me here below,
Shall be forever mine.

[7]
When we've been there ten thousand years,
Bright shining as the sun,
We've no less days to sing God's praise
Than when we'd first begun.

songs.title: And Can It Be
songs.author: Charles Wesley (1707-1788)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
And can it be that I should gain
An interest in the Savior's blood?
Died He for me, who caused His pain?
For me, who Him to death pursued?

[1.2]
Amazing love! How can it be,
That Thou, my God, shouldst die for me?

[2.1]
'Tis mystery all: th'Immortal dies:
Who can explore His strange design?
In vain the firstborn seraph tries
To sound the depths of love divine.

[2.2]
'Tis mercy all! Let earth adore,
Let angel minds inquire no more.

[3.1]
He left His Father's throne above
So free, so infinite His grace?
Emptied Himself of all but love,
And bled for Adam's helpless race:

[3.2]
'Tis mercy all, immense and free,
For O my God, it found out me!

[4.1]
Long my imprisoned spirit lay,
Fast bound in sin and nature's night;
Thine eye diffused a quick'ning ray?
I woke, the dungeon flamed with light;

[4.2]
My chains fell off, my heart was free,
I rose, went forth, and followed Thee.

[5.1]
Still the small inward voice I hear,
That whispers all my sins forgiv'n;
Still the atoning blood is near,
That quenched the wrath of hostile Heav'n.

[5.2]
I feel the life His wounds impart;
I feel the Savior in my heart.

[6]
No condemnation now I dread; Jesus, and all in Him, is mine;
Alive in Him, my living Head, And clothed in righteousness divine,
Bold I approach th'eternal throne, And claim the crown, through Christ my own.

songs.title: Angel Voices, Ever Singing
songs.author: Francis Pott (1832-1909)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Angel voices, ever singing,
Round Thy throne of light,
Angel harps, forever ringing,
Rest not day or night;

[1.2]
Thousands only live to bless Thee,
And confess Thee Lord of might.

[2.1]
Thou Who art beyond the farthest
Mortal eye can scan,
Can it be that Thou regardest
Songs of sinful man?

[2.2]
Can we feel that Thou art near us
And wilt hear us? Yea, we can.

[3.1]
Lord, we know Thy love rejoices
O'er each work of Thine;
Thou didst ears and hands and voices
For Thy praise combine;

[3.2]
Craftsman's art and music's measure
For Thy pleasure didst design.

[4.1]
Here, great God, today we offer
Of Thine own to Thee;

[4.2]
And for Thine acceptance proffer,
All unworthily,
Hearts and minds, and hands and voices,
In our choicest melody.

[5.1]
Honor, glory, might and merit,
Thine shall ever be,
Father, Son, and Holy Spirit,
Blessed Trinity;

[5.2]
Of the best that Thou hast given
Earth and Heaven render Thee.

songs.title: Angels From the Realms of Glory
songs.author: James Montgomery (1771-1854)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Angels from the realms of glory,
Wing your flight o'er all the earth;
Ye who sang creation's story
Now proclaim Messiah's birth.

[1.2]
Come and worship, come and worship,
Worship Christ, the newborn King.

[2]
Shepherds, in the field abiding,
Watching o'er your flocks by night,
God with us is now residing;
Yonder shines the infant light:

[3]
Sages, leave your contemplations,
Brighter visions beam afar;
Seek the great Desire of nations;
Ye have seen His natal star.

[4]
Saints, before the altar bending,
Watching long in hope and fear;
Suddenly the Lord, descending,
In His temple shall appear.

[5.1]
Sinners, wrung with true repentance,
Doomed for guilt to endless pains,
Justice now revokes the sentence,

[5.2]
Mercy calls you;
Break your chains.

[6]
Though an Infant now we view Him,
He shall fill His Father's throne,
Gather all the nations to Him;
Every knee shall then bow down:

[7]
All creation, join in praising
God, the Father, Spirit, Son,
Evermore your voices raising
To th'eternal Three in One.

songs.title: Angels We Have Heard On High
songs.author: French (trad. James Chadwick (1813-1882))
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Angels we have heard on high Sweetly singing o'er the plains,
And the mountains in reply Echoing their joyous strains.
Gloria, in excelsis Deo!
Gloria, in excelsis Deo!

[2]
Shepherds, why this jubilee?
Why your joyous strains prolong?
What the gladsome tidings be Which inspire your heav'nly song?

[3]
Come to Bethlehem and see Christ Whose birth the angels sing;
Come, adore on bended knee,
Christ the Lord, the newborn King.

[4.1]
See Him in a manger laid,
Whom the choirs of angels praise;

[4.2]
Mary,
Joseph, lend your aid,
While our hearts in love we raise.

songs.title: As With Gladness Men of Old
songs.author: William Chatterton Dix (1837-1865)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
As with gladness, men of old
Did the guiding star behold
As with joy they hailed its light
Leading onward, beaming bright

[1.2]
So, most glorious Lord, may we
Evermore be led to Thee.

[2.1]
As with joyful steps they sped
To that lowly manger bed
There to bend the knee before
Him whom Heav'n and earth adore;

[2.2]
So may we with willing feet
Ever seek Thy mercy seat.

[3.1]
As they offered gifts most rare
At that manger rude and bare;

[3.2]
So may we with holy joy,
Pure and free from sin's alloy,
All our costliest treasures bring,
Christ, to Thee, our heav'nly King.

[4.1]
Holy Jesus, ev'ry day
Keep us in the narrow way;

[4.2]
And, when earthly things are past,
Bring our ransomed souls at last
Where they need no star to guide,
Where no clouds Thy glory hide.

[5.1]
In the heav'nly country bright,
Need they no created light;
Thou its Light, its Joy, its Crown,
Thou its Sun which goes not down;

[5.2]
There forever may we sing
Alleluias to our King!

songs.title: Ascribe To the Lord Honor
songs.author: 'Bola Omodun. Ilori (1950-)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Ascribe to the Lord, honor,
And glory due His Name
Worship in His holiness,
Worthy is His pow'r and fame.

[2]
The Lord of glory thunders
O'er great and mighty seas;
His voice is so majestic,
It breaks cedar to pieces.

[3]
His voice like a mighty flash,
Shakes the desert of Kadesh,
It makes bare the thick forest No other voice is its match.

[4]
The Lord sits upon His throne,
That's set upon the flood.
He gives strength to His people,
Who put their trust in His word.

[5]
Ascribe to the Lord, honor,
And glory due His Name,
Worship Him in holiness
Worthy is His might and fame.

songs.title: At The Lamb's High Feast
songs.author: Latin (trad. Robert Campbell (1814-1868))
songs.lyrics:
[1]
At the Lamb's high feast we sing,
Praise to our victorious King,
Who has washed us in the tide Flowing from his pierc�d side;
Alleluia!

[2.1]
Praise we Him, whose love divine Gives His sacred blood for wine,
Gives His body for the feast,
Christ the Victim,

[2.2]
Christ the Priest.
Alleluia!

[3]
Where the Paschal blood is poured,
Death's dark angel sheathes his sword;
Israel's hosts triumphant go Through the wave that drowns the foe.
Alleluia!

[4.1]
Praise we Christ, whose blood was shed,
Paschal Victim,
Paschal Bread;

[4.2]
With sincerity and love Eat we Manna from above.
Alleluia!

[5.1]
Mighty Victim from the sky,
Hell's fierce pow'rs beneath Thee lie;
Thou hast conquered in the fight,

[5.2]
Thou hast brought us life and light;
Alleluia!

[6]
Now no more can death appall,
Now no more the grave enthrall;
Thou hast opened Paradise,
And in Thee Thy saints shall rise.

[7]
Paschal triumph, Easter joy,
This alone can sin destroy;
From sin's death do Thou set free
Souls reborn, O Lord, in Thee.

[8]
Hymns of glory and of praise,
Father, to Thee we raise;
Risen Lord, all praise to Thee,
Ever with the Spirit be.

songs.title: Author of All Life
songs.author: Brian James Dumont (1971-)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Author of all Life, our Father,
Breathe into our hearts again.
Stir our deadness, heal our weakness,
Crush our evil thoughts so vain.

[1.2]
Life Creator, life Redeemer,
Life Imparter, Source of Truth,
Teach us now to love each other,
Teach us Lord to love like You.

[2.1]
Hearts so hard, we hate each other,
Those in need we treat with scorn...
Old, unwise, or not my color,
Palsied limbs, or not yet born.

[2.2]
Life Creator, life Redeemer,
Life Imparter, Three in One,
Teach us Lord to see Your Image,
Teach us now to see the Son.

[3.1]
Christ now grants us life eternal,
To know You the one true God,
He the Way to see the Father,
He the One who felt the rod.

[3.2]
Life Creator, life Redeemer,
Life Imparter, Life conferred!
Let us sing of Your atonement,
Let all people hear Your Word!

songs.title: Awake My Soul, An Offering Bring
songs.author: Brian L. Penney (1951-)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Awake my soul, an off'ring bring
To Jesus our exalted King;
Sing to Him Who reigns above
Incarnate fount of grace and love;

[1.2]
Sing to Him Who reigns above
Incarnate fount of grace and love.

[2.1]
In awe we stand upon this ground,
His wisdom and His pow'r astound;
All His wonders we behold,
In heav'n and earth His story's told;

[2.2]
All His wonders we behold,
In heav'n and earth His story's told.

[3.1]
Then to this world, behold what grace!
He comes to rescue Adam's race;
Our Redeemer, our High Priest,
From sin and death He brings release;

[3.2]
Our Redeemer, our High Priest,
From sin and death He brings release.

[4.1]
Awake my soul, arise and sing,
Eternal praise to Christ our King;
In His Church, His Name confessed,
We worship Him among the blessed;

[4.2]
In His Church, His Name confessed,
We worship Him among the blessed.

songs.title: Awake, My Heart, With Gladness
songs.author: Paul Gerhardt (1607-1676) (trad. John Kelly (1833-1890))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Awake, my heart, with gladness,
See what today is done;
How after gloom and sadness,
Comes forth the glorious Sun.

[1.2]
My Savior there was laid
Where our bed must be made
When to the realms of light
Our spirit wings its flight.

[2.1]
They in the grave did sink Him,
The foe held jubilee;
Before he can bethink him,
Lo! Christ again is free.

[2.2]
And "Victory" He cries,
And waving tow'rds the skies
His banner, while the field
Is by the Hero held!

[3.1]
Upon the grave is standing
The Hero looking round;

[3.2]
The foe, no more withstanding,
His weapons on the ground
Throws down, his hellish pow'r
To Christ must he give o'er,

[3.3]
And to the Victor's bands
Must yield his feet and hands.

[4.1]
A sight it is to gladden;
And fill the heart with glee,

[4.2]
No more affright or sadden
Shall aught, or take from me
My trust or fortitude,

[4.3]
Or any precious good
The Savior bought for me
In sov'reign love and free.

[5.1]
Hell and its prince, the devil,
Of all their pow'rs are shorn;
Now I am safe from evil,
And sin I laugh to scorn.

[5.2]
Grim Death with all his might
Cannot my soul affright;
He is a pow'rless form,
Howe'er he rage and storm.

songs.title: Awake, My Soul, And With The Sun
songs.author: Thomas Ken (1637-1711)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Awake, my soul, and with the sun
Thy daily stage of duty run;
Shake off dull sloth, and joyful rise,
To pay thy morning sacrifice.

[2]
Thy precious time misspent, redeem,
Each present day thy last esteem,
Improve thy talent with due care;
For the great day thyself prepare.

[3]
By influence of Light divine
Let thy own light to others shine.
Reflect all Heaven's propitious ways
In ardent love, and cheerful praise.

[4]
In conversation be sincere;
Keep conscience as the noontide clear;
Think how all seeing God thy ways
And all thy secret thoughts surveys.

[5]
Wake, and lift up thyself, my heart,
And with the angels bear thy part,
Who all night long unwearied sing
High praise to the eternal King.

[6]
All praise to Thee, Who safe has kept
And hast refreshed me while I slept
Grant, Lord, when I from death shall wake
I may of endless light partake.

[7]
Heav'n is, dear Lord, where'er Thou art,
O never then from me depart;
For to my soul 'tis hell to be
But for one moment void of Thee.

[8]
Lord, I my vows to Thee renew;
Disperse my sins as morning dew.
Guard my first springs of thought and will,
And with Thyself my spirit fill.

[9]
Direct, control, suggest, this day,
All I design, or do, or say,
That all my powers, with all their might,
In Thy sole glory may unite.

[10]
I would not wake nor rise again
And Heaven itself I would disdain,
Wert Thou not there to be enjoyed,
And I in hymns to be employed.

[11]
Praise God, from Whom all blessings flow;
Praise Him, all creatures here below;
Praise Him above, ye heavenly host;
Praise Father, Son, and Holy Ghost.

songs.title: Away In A Manger
songs.author: anonymous, John T. MacFarland (1851-1913)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Away in a manger, no crib for a bed,
The little Lord Jesus laid down His sweet head.
The stars in the sky looked down where He lay,
The little Lord Jesus, asleep on the hay.

[2]
The cattle are lowing, the Baby awakes,
But little Lord Jesus, no crying He makes;
I love Thee, Lord Jesus, look down from the sky
And stay by my cradle til morning is nigh.

[3]
Be near me, Lord Jesus, I ask Thee to stay
Close by me forever, and love me, I pray;
Bless all the dear children in Thy tender care,
And fit us for Heaven to live with Thee there.

songs.title: Baptized Into Thy Name Most Holy
songs.author: Johann Jakob Rambach (1693-1735) (trad. Catherine Winkworth (1827-1878), August Crull (1845-1923))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Baptized into Thy Name most holy,
O Father, Son, and Holy Ghost,
I claim a place, though weak and lowly,
Among Thy seed, Thy chosen host.

[1.2]
Buried with Christ and dead to sin,
Thy Spirit now shall live within.

[2.1]
My loving Father, here doth take me
To be henceforth His child and heir;
My faithful Savior, now doth make me
The fruit of all His sorrows share;

[2.2]
My Comforter will comfort me
When darkest clouds around I see.

[3.1]
And I have vowed to fear and love Thee
And to obey Thee, Lord, alone;

[3.2]
I felt Thy Holy Spirit move me,
I dared to pledge myself Thine own,
Renouncing sin to keep the faith
And war with evil unto death.

[4.1]
My faithful God, Thou failest never,
Thy cov'nant surely will abide;
Oh, cast me not away forever
Should I transgress it on my side!

[4.2]
But if I fall hide not Thy face,
Restore Thy child, Lord, by Thy Grace.

[5.1]
Yes, all I am and love most dearly,
To Thee I offer now the whole;
O let me make my vows sincerely,
Take full possession of my soul!

[5.2]
Let naught within me, naught I own,
Serve any will save Thine alone.

songs.title: Be Still My Soul
songs.author: Katharina Amalia Dorothea von Schlegel (1697-1768) (trad. Jane Laurie Borthwick (1813-1897))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Be still, my soul: the Lord is on thy side.
Bear patiently the cross of grief or pain.
Leave to thy God to order and provide;
In every change, He faithful will remain.

[1.2]
Be still, my soul: thy best, thy heav'nly Friend
Through thorny ways leads to a joyful end.

[2.1]
Be still, my soul: thy God doth undertake
To guide the future, as He has the past.
Thy hope, thy confidence let nothing shake;
All now mysterious shall be bright at last.

[2.2]
Be still, my soul: the waves and winds still know
His voice Who ruled them while He dwelt below.

[3.1]
Be still, my soul: when dearest friends depart,
And all is darkened in the vale of tears,
Then shalt thou better know His love, His heart,
Who comes to soothe thy sorrow and thy fears.

[3.2]
Be still, my soul: thy Jesus can repay
From His own fullness all He takes away.

[4.1]
Be still, my soul: the hour is hast'ning on
When we shall be forever with the Lord.
When disappointment, grief and fear are gone,
Sorrow forgot, love's purest joys restored.

[4.2]
Be still, my soul: when change and tears are past
All safe and bless�d we shall meet at last.

[5.1]
Be still, my soul: begin the song of praise
On earth, believing, to Thy Lord on high;
Acknowledge Him in all thy words and ways,
So shall He view thee with a well pleased eye.

[5.2]
Be still, my soul: the Sun of life divine
Through passing clouds shall but more brightly shine.

songs.title: Be Thou My Vision
songs.author: Dallan Forgaill (8th Century) (trad. Mary Elizabeth Byrne (1880-1931), Eleanor Henrietta Hull (1860-1935))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Be Thou my Vision,
O Lord of my heart;
Naught be all else to me, save that Thou art.

[1.2]
Thou my best Thought, by day or by night,
Waking or sleeping,
Thy presence my light.

[2]
Be Thou my Wisdom, and Thou my true Word;
I ever with Thee and Thou with me, Lord;
Thou my great Father, and I Thy true son;
Thou in me dwelling, and I with Thee one.

[3]
Be Thou my battle Shield, Sword for the fight;
Be Thou my Dignity, Thou my Delight;
Thou my soul's Shelter, Thou my high Tower:
Raise Thou me heav'nward, O Pow'r of my pow'r.

[4]
Riches I heed not, nor man's empty praise,
Thou mine Inheritance, now and always:
Thou and Thou only, be first in my heart,
High King of Heaven, my Treasure Thou art.

[5]
High King of Heaven, my victory won,
May I reach Heav'ns joys, O bright Heaven's Sun!
Heart of my own heart, whatever befall,
Still be my Vision, O Ruler of all.

songs.title: Beautiful Savior
songs.author: German Jesuits (trad. Joseph August Seiss (1823-1904))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Beautiful Savior,
King of Creation
Son of God and Son of Man!

[1.2]
Truly I'd love Thee,
Truly I'd serve Thee,
Light of my soul, my joy, my crown.

[2.1]
Fair are the meadows,
Fair are the woodlands,
Robed in the flow'rs of blooming spring;

[2.2]
Jesus is fairer,
Jesus is purer,
He makes our sorr'wing spirit sing.

[3.1]
Fair is the sunshine,
Fair is the moonlight,
Bright the sparkling stars on high;

[3.2]
Jesus shines brighter,
Jesus shines purer
Than all the angels in the sky.

[4.1]
Beautiful Savior,
Lord of the nations,
Son of God and Son of Man!

[4.2]
Glory and honor,
Praise, adoration
Now and forevermore be Thine!

songs.title: Behold, A Host, Arrayed in White
songs.author: Hans Adolf Brorson (1694-1764) (trad. composite)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Behold a host, arrayed in white,
Like thousand snow clad mountains bright,
With palms they stand.

[1.2]
Who is this band
Before the throne of light?

[1.3]
Lo, these are they of glorious fame
Who from the great affliction came
And in the flood
Of Jesus' blood

[1.4]
Are cleansed from guilt and blame.
Now gathered in the holy place
Their voices they in worship raise,

[1.5]
Their anthems swell
Where God doth dwell,
Mid angels song of praise.

[2.1]
Despised and scorned, they sojourned here;
But now, how glorious they appear!

[2.2]
Those martyrs stand
A priestly band,
God's throne forever near.

[2.3]
So oft, in troubled days gone by,
In anguish they would weep and sigh.

[2.4]
At home above
The God of Love
For aye their tears shall dry.

[2.5]
They now enjoy their Sabbath rest,
The paschal banquet of the blest;

[2.6]
The Lamb, their Lord,
At festal board
Himself is Host and Guest.

[3.1]
Then hail, ye mighty legions, yea,
All hail! Now safe and blest for aye,
And praise the Lord,

[3.2]
Who with His Word
Sustained you on the way.
Ye did the joys of earth disdain,
Ye toiled and sowed in tears and pain.

[3.3]
Farewell, now bring
Your sheaves and sing
Salvation's glad refrain.

[3.4]
Swing high your palms, lift up your song,
Yea, make it myriad voices strong.

[3.5]
Eternally
Shall praise to Thee,
God, and the Lamb belong.

songs.title: Beneath The Cross Of Jesus
songs.author: Elizabeth Cecelia Douglas Clephane (1830-1869)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Beneath the cross of Jesus I fain would take my stand,
The shadow of a mighty rock within a weary land;

[1.2]
A home within the wilderness, a rest upon the way,
From the burning of the noontide heat, and
The burden of the day.

[2.1]
O safe and happy shelter,
O refuge tried and sweet,
O trysting place where Heaven's love
And Heaven's justice meet!

[2.2]
As to the holy patriarch
That wondrous dream was giv'n,
So seems my Savior's cross to me,
A ladder up to heav'n.

[3.1]
There lies beneath its shadow
But on the further side
The darkness of an awful grave
That gapes both deep and wide

[3.2]
And there between us stands the cross
Two arms outstretched to save
A watchman set to guard the way
From that eternal grave.

[4.1]
Upon that cross of Jesus
Mine eye at times can see
The very dying form of One
Who suffered there for me;

[4.2]
And from my stricken heart with tears
Two wonders I confess;
The wonders of redeeming love
And my unworthiness.

[5.1]
I take, O cross, thy shadow
For my abiding place;
I ask no other sunshine than
The sunshine of His face;

[5.2]
Content to let the world go by
To know no gain or loss,
My sinful self my only shame,
My glory all the cross.

songs.title: Blessed Assurance
songs.author: Fanny Jane Crosby (1820-1915)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Bless�d assurance, Jesus is mine!
O what a foretaste of glory divine!
Heir of salvation, purchase of God,
Born of His Spirit, washed in His blood.

[1.2]
This is my story, this is my song,
Praising my Savior, all the day long;
This is my story, this is my song,
Praising my Savior, all the day long.

[2]
Perfect submission, perfect delight,
Visions of rapture now burst on my sight;
Angels descending bring from above Echoes of mercy, whispers of love.

[3]
Perfect submission, all is at rest I in
My Savior am happy and blest,
Watching and waiting, looking above,
Filled with His goodness, lost in His love.

songs.title: Blessed Jesus at Thy Word
songs.author: Tobias Clausnitzer (1619-1684) (trad. Catherine Winkworth (1827-1878))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Blessed Jesus, at Thy Word
We are gathered all to hear Thee;

[1.2]
Let our hearts and souls be stirred
Now to seek and love and fear Thee,
By Thy teachings sweet and holy,
Drawn from earth to love Thee solely.

[2.1]
All our knowledge, sense, and sight
Lie in deepest darkness shrouded,
Til Thy Spirit breaks our night
With the beams of truth unclouded;

[2.2]
Thou alone to God canst win us;
Thou must work all good within us.

[3.1]
Glorious Lord, Thyself impart!
Light of light, from God proceeding,
Open Thou our ears and heart;
Help us by Thy Spirit's pleading;

[3.2]
Hear the cry Thy people raises;
Hear and bless our prayers and praises.

[4.1]
Father, Son, and Holy Ghost,
Praise to Thee and adoration!

[4.2]
Grant that we Thy Word may trust
And obtain true consolation,
While we here below must wander,
Till we sing Thy praises yonder.

songs.title: Blest Be The Tie That Binds
songs.author: John Fawcett (1740-1817)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Blest be the tie that binds
Our hearts in Christian love;
The fellowship of kindred minds
Is like to that above.

[2]
Before our Father's throne
We pour our ardent prayers;
Our fears, our hopes, our aims are one
Our comforts and our cares.

[3]
We share each other's woes,
Our mutual burdens bear;
And often for each other flows
The sympathizing tear.

[4]
When we asunder part,
It gives us inward pain;
But we shall still be joined in heart,
And hope to meet again.

[5]
This glorious hope revives
Our courage by the way;
While each in expectation lives,
And longs to see the day.

[6]
From sorrow, toil and pain,
And sin, we shall be free,
And perfect love and friendship reign
Through all eternity.

songs.title: Blind Bartimaeus
songs.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow (1807-1882)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Blind Bartimaeus at the gates
Of Jericho in darkness waits:
He hears the crowd; he hears a breath
Say "It is Christ of Nazareth!"

[1.2]
And calls in tones of agony,
"O Jesus, Jesus pity me!"

[2.1]
The thronging multitudes increase
"Blind Bartimaeus, hold thy peace!"
But still, above the noisy crowd,
The blind man's cry is shrill and loud:

[2.2]
Until they say, "He calleth thee;
Courage! arise! He calleth thee!"

[3.1]
Then saith the Christ, as silent stands
The crowd, "What wilt thou at My hands?"
And he replies, "O give me light!
Rabbi, restore the blind man's sight."

[3.2]
And Jesus answers, "Go thy way,
Thy faith, thy faith hath sav�d thee."

[4.1]
Ye that hath eyes and cannot see,
In darkness and in misery,
Recall those mighty voices three-
"O Jesus, Jesus pity me!"

[4.2]
"Courage! arise! He calleth thee!"
"Thy faith, thy faith hath sav�d thee."

songs.title: Breathe on Me, Breath of God
songs.author: Edwin Hatch (1835-1889)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Breathe on me, breath of God,
Fill me with life anew,
That I may love what Thou dost love,
And do what Thou wouldst do.

[2]
Breathe on me, breath of God,
Until my heart is pure,
Until with Thee I will one will,
To do and to endure.

[3]
Breathe on me, breath of God,
So shall I never die,
But live with Thee the perfect life
Of Thine eternity.

songs.title: Built on the Rock
songs.author: Nikolai Frederik Severin Grundtvig (1783-1872) (trad. Carl D�ving (1867-1937))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Built on the Rock the church doth stand,
Even when steeples are falling;
Crumbled have spires in every land,
Bells still are chiming and calling;

[1.2]
Calling the young and old to rest,
But above all the soul distressed,
Longing for rest everlasting.

[2.1]
Surely in temples made with hands,
God, the Most High, is not dwelling;
High above earth His temple stands,
All earthly temples excelling;

[2.2]
Yet He whom heav'ns cannot contain
Chose to abide on earth with men,
Built in our bodies His temple.

[3.1]
We are God's house of living stones,
Built for His own habitation;
He through baptismal grace us owns,
Heirs of His wondrous salvation;

[3.2]
Were we but two His Name to tell,
Yet He would deign with us to dwell,
With all His grace and His favor.

[4.1]
Now we may gather with our King;
Ev'n in the lowliest dwelling:
Praises to Him we there may bring,
His wondrous mercy foretelling;

[4.2]
Jesus His grace to us accords,
Spirit and life are all His words,
His truth doth hallow the temple.

[5.1]
Still we our earthly temples rear,
That we may herald His praises;

[5.2]
They are the homes where He draws near
And little children embraces,
Beautiful things in them are said,

[5.3]
God there with us His cov'nant made,
Making us heirs of His kingdom.

songs.title: By Grace I'm Saved
songs.author: Christian Ludwig Scheidt (1709-1761) (trad. Matthias Loy (1828-1915))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
By grace I'm saved- grace free and boundless!
My heart, believ'st thou this or not?
Why tremblest thou with terror groundless?
Has ever God a falsehood taught?

[1.2]
His Word is truethen this must be:
By grace there is a crown for thee.

[2.1]
By grace! our works are all rejected,
All claims of merit pass for naught;

[2.2]
The mighty Savior, long expected,
To us this blissful truth has brought,
That He by death redeems our race,
And we are saved alone by grace.

[3.1]
By grace! mark well this phrase's meaning,
When sin rolls sorrows o'er thy breast,
When Satan threats with pride o'erweening,
When troubled conscience sighs for rest:

[3.2]
What reason ne'er can comprehend
It pleases God by grace to send.

[4.1]
By grace His Son, on earth appearing,
Vouchsafed beneath thy woe to bend;
Hadst thou, damnation justly fearing,
Done aught to render Him thy friend?

[4.2]
Was't not that He thy welfare sought,
And but by grace deliv'rance wrought?

[5.1]
By grace! this ground of our salvation
As long as God is true endures:

[5.2]
What saints have penned by inspiration,
What God to our poor soul secures,
What all our faith must rest upon,
Is grace, free grace through His dear Son.

[6.1]
By grace! but think not, thou who livest
Securely on in godless ways,
That thou, though all are called, receivest
The promised rest that wakes our praise:

[6.2]
By grace none find in heaven a place
Who live in sin in hope of grace.

[7.1]
By grace! They who have heard this sentence
Must bid hypocrisy farewell;
For only after deep repentance
The soul what grace imports can tell;

[7.2]
To sin while grace a trifle seems,
To faith it bright with glory beams.

[8.1]
By grace the timid hearts that languish,
Find access to the Father's heart,
When conflicts fierce and bitter anguish
Bid all their joy and hopes depart.

[8.2]
Where, oftimes, should I strength obtain,
Bid grace my anchor not remain!

[9.1]
By grace! on this in death I'll rest me,
Rejoicing e'en though feeling naught;
I know my sin it oft oppressed me
But Him, too, who my soul hath bought:

[9.2]
My heart exults grief flees apace
Because my soul is saved by grace.

[10.1]
By grace! O sin and Satan hear it!
I bear my flag of faith in hand,
And pass, in spite of doubts, nor fear it,
The Red Sea to the promised land;

[10.2]
I hold the word my Savior taught
As certain, whether felt or not.

songs.title: Christ Arose
songs.author: Robert Lowry (1826-1899)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Low in the grave He lay Jesus my Savior!
Waiting the coming day- Jesus my Lord!
Up from the grave He arose,
With a mighty triumph o'er His He arose!

[1.2]
Foes;
He arose a Victor from the dark domain,
And He lives forever with His He arose!
Saints to reign.

[1.3]
He arose!
He arose!
Hallelujah!
Christ arose!

[1.4]
He arose!
He arose!

[2]
Vainly they watch His bed- Jesus my Savior!
Vainly they seal the dead- Jesus my Lord!

[3]
Death cannot keep his prey- Jesus my Savior!
He tore the bars away- Jesus my Lord!

songs.title: Christ Jesus Lay In Death's Strong Bands
songs.author: Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. Richard Massie (1800-1887))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Christ Jesus lay in death's strong bands,
For our offenses given;
But now at God's right hand He stands,
And brings us life from Heaven.

[1.2]
Wherefore let us joyful be,
And sing to God right thankfully Loud songs of Alleluia!
Alleluia!

[2.1]
No son of man could conquer Death,
Such mischief sin had wrought us,
For innocence dwelt not on earth,

[2.2]
And therefore Death had brought us Into thralldom
From of old And ever grew more strong
And bold And kept us in his bondage.
Alleluia!

[3.1]
But Jesus Christ,
God's only Son,
To our low state descended,
The cause of Death He has undone,

[3.2]
His power forever ended,
Ruined all his right and claim And left
Him nothing but the name,

[3.3]
His sting is lost forever.
Alleluia!

[4.1]
It was a strange and dreadful strife When life and death contended;
The victory remained with life;
The reign of death was ended.

[4.2]
Stripped of power, no more it reigns,
An empty form alone remains Death's sting is lost forever!
Alleluia!

[5.1]
Here the true Paschal Lamb we see,
Whom God so freely gave us;
He died on the accursed tree So strong His love!
To save us.

[5.2]
See,
His blood doth mark our door;

[5.3]
Faith points to it,
Death passes o'er,
And Satan cannot harm us.
Alleluia!

songs.title: Christ My King On High
songs.author: Jay C. Wingard
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Lord, my sin, it grieves me so.
How I long for my Lord to come.
Bless my God who clothes me bright, wraps
Me pure in heav'n's Great Light.

[2]
Spotless Lamb made sin for me.
God, Great Judge, just always be.
Sealed on high with Christ's Great Pledge
Never more shall death I dread.

[3.1]
One with Him,
I stand secure,
Safe in Triune hands I'm sure.

[3.2]
Christ's great merits giv'n to me.
I now hear Him say, "Whom I'm pleased."

[4]
Long to see the skies burn bright,
Heaven's hosts all clothed in white.
See the King, His vic'try won.
Come, pure Bride behold the Son.

songs.title: Christ Returneth
songs.author: H. L. Turner (18th Century)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
It may be at morn, when the day is awaking,
When sunlight through darkness and shadow is breaking
That Jesus will come in the fullness of
Glory To receive from the world "His own."

[1.2]
O Lord Jesus, how long, how long Ere
We shout the glad song,
Christ returneth!
Hallelujah!

[1.3]
Hallelujah!
Amen.
Hallelujah!
Amen.

[2.1]
It may be at midday, it may be at twilight,
It may be, perchance, that the blackness of
Midnight Will burst into light in the blaze

[2.2]
Of His glory,
When Jesus receives "His own."

[3]
While hosts cry Hosanna, from heaven descending,
With glorified saints and the angels attending,
With grace on His brow, like a halo of glory,
Will Jesus receive "His own."

[4.1]
Oh, joy!
Oh, delight!
Should we go without dying,
No sickness, no sadness, no dread and no crying.

[4.2]
Caught up through the clouds with our Lord into glory,
When Jesus receives "His own."

songs.title: Christ The Lord Is Risen Today (Lyra)
songs.author: Charles Wesley (1707-1788), unknown (trad. unknown)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Christ, the Lord, is risen today,
Alleluia!
Sons of men and angels say,
Alleluia!

[1.2]
Raise your joys and triumphs high,
Alleluia!
Sing, ye heavens, and earth, reply,
Alleluia!

[2.1]
Love's redeeming work is done,
Alleluia!
Fought the fight, the battle won,
Alleluia!

[2.2]
Lo!
The Sun's eclipse is o'er,
Alleluia!
Lo!

[2.3]
He sets in blood no more,
Alleluia!

[3.1]
Vain the stone, the watch, the seal,
Alleluia!
Christ hath burst the gates of hell,
Alleluia!

[3.2]
Death in vain forbids His rise,
Alleluia!
Christ hath opened paradise,
Alleluia!

[4.1]
Lives again our glorious King,
Alleluia!
Where,
O death, is now thy sting?

[4.2]
Alleluia!
Once He died our souls to save,
Alleluia!

[4.3]
Where thy victory,
O grave?
Alleluia!

[5.1]
Soar we now where Christ hath led,
Alleluia!
Following our exalted Head,
Alleluia!

[5.2]
Made like Him, like Him we rise,
Alleluia!
Ours the cross, the grave, the skies,
Alleluia!

songs.title: Come Down, O Love Divine
songs.author: Bianco of Siena (?-1434) (trad. Richard Frederick Littledale (1833-1890))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Come down, O love divine,
Seek Thou this soul of mine,
And visit it with Thine own ardor glowing.

[1.2]
O Comforter, draw near,
Within my heart appear,
And kindle it, Thy holy flame bestowing.

[2.1]
O let it freely burn,
Til earthly passions turn
To dust and ashes in its heat consuming;

[2.2]
And let Thy glorious light
Shine ever on my sight,
And clothe me round, the while my path illuming.

[3.1]
Let holy charity
Mine outward vesture be,
And lowliness become mine inner clothing;

[3.2]
True lowliness of heart,
Which takes the humbler part,
And o'er its own shortcomings weeps with loathing.

[4.1]
And so the yearning strong,
With which the soul will long,
Shall far outpass the pow'r of human telling;

[4.2]
For none can guess its grace,
Till he become the place
Wherein the Holy Spirit makes His dwelling.

songs.title: Come Holy Spirit, Lord Our God
songs.author: Latin, Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. Arthur Tozel Russell (1806-1874))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Come,
Holy Spirit,
Lord our God,
And pour Thy gifts of grace abroad;

[1.2]
Thy faithful people fill with blessing,
Love's fire their hearts possessing.

[1.3]
O Lord,
Thou by Thy heav'nly Light Dost gather and
In faith unite Through all the world a
Holy nation To sing to Thee with exultation,

[1.4]
Hallelujah!
Hallelujah!

[2.1]
O, holiest Light!
O Rock adored!

[2.2]
Give us Thy light,
Thy living Word,
To God Himself our spirits leading,
With Him as children pleading.

[2.3]
From error,
Lord, our souls defend,
That they on Christ alone attend;

[2.4]
In Him with faith unfeigned abiding,
In Him with all their might confiding.

[3.1]
O holiest Fire!
O Source of rest!

[3.2]
Grant that with joy and hope possest,
And in Thy service kept forever,
Naught us from Thee may sever.
Lord, may Thy pow'r prepare each heart;

[3.3]
To our weak nature strength impart,
Onward to press, our foes defying,
To Thee, through living and through dying.

songs.title: Come Thou Fount Of Every Blessing
songs.author: Robert Robinson (1735-1790)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Come, Thou Fount of every blessing,
Tune my heart to sing Thy grace;
Streams of mercy, never ceasing,
Call for songs of loudest praise.

[1.2]
Teach me some melodious sonnet,
Sung by flaming tongues above.
Praise the mount! I'm fixed upon it,
Mount of Thy redeeming love.

[2.1]
Sorr'wing I shall be in spirit,
Till released from flesh and sin,
Yet from what I do inherit,
Here Thy praises I'll begin;

[2.2]
Here I raise my Ebenezer;
Here by Thy great help I've come;
And I hope, by Thy good pleasure,
Safely to arrive at home.

[3.1]
Jesus sought me when a stranger,
Wand'ring from the fold of God;
He, to rescue me from danger,
Interposed His precious blood;

[3.2]
How His kindness yet pursues me
Mortal tongue can never tell,
Clothed in flesh, till death shall loose me
I cannot proclaim it well.

[4.1]
O to grace how great a debtor
Daily I'm constrained to be!
Let Thy goodness, like a fetter,
Bind my wand'ring heart to Thee.

[4.2]
Prone to wander, Lord, I feel it,
Prone to leave the God I love;
Here's my heart, O take and seal it,
Seal it for Thy courts above.

[5.1]
O that day when freed from sinning,
I shall see Thy lovely face;
Cloth�d then in blood washed linen
How I'll sing Thy sovereign grace;

[5.2]
Come, my Lord, no longer tarry,
Take my ransomed soul away;
Send thine angels now to carry
Me to realms of endless day.

songs.title: Come, God Creator, Holy Ghost
songs.author: Charlemagne (742-814), Rhabanus Maurus (776-856), Gregory the Great (c. 540-604), Ambrose of Milan (340-397) (trad. Martin Luther (1483-1546), Leonard Woolsey Bacon (1830-1907))
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Come, God Creator, Holy Ghost,
And visit Thou these souls of men;
Fill them with graces, as Thou dost,
Thy creatures make pure again.

[2]
For Comforter Thy name we call.
Sweet gift of God most high above,
A holy unction to us all
O Fount of life, Fire of love.

[3]
Our minds illumine and refresh,
Deep in our hearts let love burn bright;
Thou know'st the weakness of our flesh;
And strengthen us with Thy might.

[4]
Thou with Thy wondrous sev'nfold gifts
The finger art of God's right hand;
The Father's Word Thou sendest swift
On tongues of fire to each land.

[5]
Drive far from us our wily foe;
Grant us Thy bless�d peace within,
That in Thy footsteps we may go,
And shun the dark ways of sin.

[6]
Teach us the Father well to know,
Likewise His only Son our Lord,
Thyself to us believing show,
Spirit of both, aye adored

[7]
Praise to the Father, and the Son
Who from the dead is risen again;
Praise to the Comforter be done
Both now and ever. Amen.

songs.title: Come, Thou Long-Expected Jesus
songs.author: Charles Wesley (1707-1788)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Come, Thou long expected Jesus
Born to set Thy people free;
From our fears and sins release us,
Let us find our rest in Thee.

[1.2]
Israel's Strength and Consolation,
Hope of all the earth Thou art;
Dear Desire of every nation,
Joy of every longing heart.

[2.1]
Born Thy people to de liver,
Born a child and yet a King,
Born to reign in us forever,
Now Thy gracious kingdom bring.

[2.2]
By Thine own eternal Spirit
Rule in all our hearts alone;
By Thine all sufficient merit,
Raise us to Thy glorious throne.

songs.title: Come, Ye Disconsolate
songs.author: Thomas Moore (1779-1852), Thomas Hastings (1784-1872)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Come, ye disconsolate, wher'er ye languish;
Come to the mercy seat, fervently kneel.
Here bring your wounded hearts, here tell your anguish;
Earth has no sorrow that Heav'n cannot heal.

[2]
Joy of the desolate, light of the straying,
Hope of the penitent, fadeless and pure,
Here speaks the Comforter, tenderly saying,
"Earth has no sorrow that Heav'n cannot cure."

[3]
Here see the Bread of Life; see waters flowing
Forth from the throne of God, pure from above;
Come to the feast of love; come, ever knowing
Earth has no sorrow but Heav'n can remove.

songs.title: Come, Your Heart and Voices Raising
songs.author: Paul Gerhardt (1607-1676) (trad. composite)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Come, your hearts and voices raising,
Christ the Lord with gladness praising;
Loudly sing His love amazing,
Worthy folk of Christendom.

[2]
Sin and death may well be groaning,
Satan now may well be moaning;
We, our full salvation owning,
Cast our every care away.

[3]
See how God, for us providing,
Gave His Son and life abiding;
He our weary steps is guiding
From earth's woe to heav'nly joy.

[4]
Christ, from heav'n to us descending
And in love our race befriending,
In our need His help extending,
Saved us from the wily Foe.

[5]
Jacob's Star in all its splendor
Beams with comfort sweet and tender,
Forcing Satan to surrender,
Breaking all the pow'rs of hell.

[6]
From the bondage that oppressed us,
From sin's fetters that possessed us,
From the grief that sore distressed us,
We, the captives, now are free.

[7]
Oh, the joy beyond expressing
When by faith we grasp this blessing
And to Thee we come confessing,
That our freedom thou hast wrought!

[8]
Gracious Child, we pray Thee, hear us,
From Thy lowly manger cheer us,
Gently lead us and be near us
Till we join the angelic choir.

songs.title: Comfort, Comfort Ye My People
songs.author: Olearius (Oelschlaeger), Johann (1611-1684) (trad. Catherine Winkworth (1827-1878))
songs.composer: Geneva, 1551 from Trente Quatre Pseaumes de David
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Comfort, comfort ye My people,
Speak ye peace, thus saith our God;
Comfort those who sit in darkness,
Mourning 'neath their sorrow's load;

[1.2]
Speak ye to Jerusalem
Of the peace that waits for them;
Tell her that her sins I cover,
And her warfare now is over.

[2.1]
For the herald's voice is crying
In the desert far and near,
Bidding all men to repentance,
Since the kingdom now is here.

[2.2]
O that warning cry obey!
Now prepare for God a way!
Let the valleys rise to meet Him,
And the hills bow down to greet Him.

[3.1]
Yea, her sins our God will pardon,
Blotting out each dark misdeed;
All that well deserved His anger
He will no more see nor heed.

[3.2]
She has suffered many a day,
Now her griefs have passed away,
God will change her pining sadness
Into ever springing gladness.

[4.1]
Make ye straight what long was crooked,
Make the rougher places plain:

[4.2]
Let your hearts be true and humble,
As befits His holy reign,
For the glory of the Lord
O'er the earth is shed abroad,

[4.3]
And all flesh shall see the token
That His Word is never broken.

songs.title: Crown Him With Many Crowns
songs.author: Matthew Bridges (1800-1894), Godfrey Thring (1823-1903)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Crown Him with many crowns,
The Lamb upon His throne.
Hark! How the heav'nly anthem drowns
All music but its own.

[1.2]
Awake, my soul, and sing
Of Him who died for thee,
And hail Him as thy matchless King
Through all eternity.

[2.1]
Crown Him the virgin's Son,
The God incarnate born,
Whose arm those crimson trophies won
Which now His brow adorn;

[2.2]
Fruit of the mystic rose,
As of that rose the stem;
The root whence mercy ever flows,
The Babe of Bethlehem.

[3.1]
Crown Him the Son of God,
Before the worlds began,
And ye who tread where He hath trod,
Crown Him the Son of Man;

[3.2]
Who every grief hath known
That wrings the human breast,
And takes and bears them for His own,
That all in Him may rest.

[4.1]
Crown Him the Lord of life,
Who triumphed o'er the grave,
And rose victorious in the strife
For those He came to save.

[4.2]
His glories now we sing,
Who died, and rose on high,
Who died eternal life to bring,
And lives that death may die.

[5.1]
Crown Him the Lord of peace,
Whose pow'r a scepter sways
From pole to pole, that wars may cease,
And all be prayer and praise.

[5.2]
His reign shall know no end,
And round His pierced feet
Fair flow'rs of paradise extend
Their fragrance ever sweet.

songs.title: Day of Wrath, O Day of Mourning
songs.author: Thomas of Celano (13th Century) (trad. William Josiah Irons (1812-1883))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Day of wrath, O day of mourning!
See fulfilled the prophet's warning,
Heav'n and earth in ashes burning.

[1.2]
Oh, what fear man's bosom rendeth
When from Heav'n the Judge descendeth
On whose sentence all dependeth!

[2.1]
Wondrous sound the trumpet flingeth,
Through earth's sepulchers it ringeth,
All before the throne it bringeth.
Death is struck and nature quaking;

[2.2]
All creation is awaking,
To its Judge an answer making.

[3.1]
Lo, the book, exactly worded,
Wherein all hath been recorded;
Thence shall judgment be awarded.

[3.2]
When the Judge His seat attaineth
And each hidden deed arraigneth,
Nothing unavenged remaineth.

[4.1]
What shall I, frail man, be pleading?
Who for me be interceding
When the just are mercy needing?

[4.2]
King of majesty tremendous,
Who dost free salvation send us,
Fount of pity, then befriend us.

[5.1]
Think, good Jesus, my salvation
Caused Thy wondrous incarnation;
Leave me not to reprobation!

[5.2]
Faint and weary Thou hast sought me,
On the cross of suff'ring bought me;
Shall such grace be vainly brought me?

songs.title: Dear Christians, One and All Rejoice
songs.author: Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. Richard Massie (1800-1887))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Dear Christians, one and all rejoice,
With exultation springing,
And with united heart and voice
And holy rapture singing,

[1.2]
Proclaim the wonders God hath done,
How his right arm the vict'ry won;
Right dearly it hath cost him.

[2.1]
Fast bound in Satan's chains I lay.
Death brooded darkly o'er me;
Sin was my torment night and day,
Therein my mother bore me.

[2.2]
Deeper and deeper still I fell,
Life was become a living hell,
So firmly sin possessed me.

[3.1]
My good works could avail me naught,
For they with sin were stain�d;
Freewill against God's judgment fought,
And dead to good remain�d.

[3.2]
Grief drove me to despair, and I
Had nothing left me but to die,
To hell I fast was sinking.

[4.1]
God saw, in his eternal grace,
My sorrow out of measure;
He thought upon his tenderness
To save was his good pleasure.

[4.2]
He turn'd to me a Father's heart-
Not small the cost to heal my smart
He gave his best and dearest.

[5.1]
He spake to his beloved Son:
'Tis time to take compassion;
Then go, bright jewel of my crown,
And bring to man salvation;

[5.2]
From sin and sorrow set him free,
Slay bitter death for him, that he
May live with thee forever.

songs.title: Despair Not, O Heart
songs.author: Aurelius Clemens Prudentius (348-413) (trad. O. T. Sanden (1853-1917))
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Despair not, O heart, in thy sorrow,
But hope from God's promises borrow
Beware in thy sorrow, of sinning
For death is of life the beginning.

[2]
The body is shrouded in mourning;
The garlands, the casket adorning,
Are emblems of hope that betoken,
O Death, that thy power is broken.

[3]
A dearly belov'd one hath left us;
God hath in His Wisdom bereft us;
But He will not leave us forsaken,
We know that the dead shall awaken.

[4]
When dawneth the glorious morrow,
This body that we view with sorrow,
A glorified form shall be given,
Restored to its spirit in heaven.

[5]
The seed that in springtime is planted,
Is hid in the ground, but if granted
A measure of sunshine and showers,
Will spring into fruitage and flowers;

[6]
A gift to the churchyard we tender,
As dust to the dust we surrender;
Returning the clay to its Maker,
We lay it to rest in God's acre.

[7]
A soul in that body abided,
A soul that in Jesus confided,
A soul that hath longed for salvation,
And now hath found hope's consummation.

[8]
O earth, we consign to thy keeping
This body with sorrow and weeping;
In peace to await resurrection,
When it shall arise in perfection.

[9]
O Christ, our soul's Maker and Lover;
When time and earth's travail are over,
Thou closest the grave's mournful story,
And callest Thine own to Thy glory.

songs.title: Did You Think To Pray?
songs.author: Mary Ann Pepper Kidder (1820-1905)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Ere you left your room this morning,
Did you think to pray?

[1.2]
In the name of Christ our Savior,
Did you sue for loving favor,
As a shield today?
O how praying rests the weary!

[1.3]
Prayer will change the night to day;
So when life seems dark and dreary,
Don't forget to pray.

[2]
When you met with great temptation,
Did you think to pray?
By His dying love and merit,
Did you claim the Holy Spirit As your guide and stay?

[3]
When your heart was filled with anger,
Did you think to pray?
Did you plead for grace, my brother,
That you might forgive another Who had crossed your way?

[4]
When sore trials came upon you,
Did you think to pray?
When your soul was bowed in sorrow,
Balm of Gilead did you borrow At the gates of day?

songs.title: Every Morning Mercies New
songs.author: Greville Phillimore (1821-1884)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Ev'ry morning mercies new
Fall as fresh as morning dew;
Ev'ry morning let us pay
Tribute with the early day:

[1.2]
For Thy mercies, Lord, are sure;
Thy compassion doth endure.

[2.1]
Still the greatness of Thy love
Daily doth our sins remove;
Daily, far as east from west,
Lifts the burden from the breast;

[2.2]
Gives unbought to those who pray
Strength to stand in evil day.

[3.1]
Let our prayers each morn prevail,
That these gifts may never fail;

[3.2]
And, as we confess the sin
And the tempter's pow'r within,
Feed us with the Bread of Life,
Fit us for our daily strife.

[4.1]
As the morning light returns,
As the sun with splendor burns,
Teach us still to turn to Thee,
Ever blessed Trinity,

[4.2]
With our hands our hearts to raise,
In unfailing prayer and praise.

songs.title: Faith of Our Fathers
songs.author: Frederick William Faber (1814-1863), James George Walton (1821-1905)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Faith of our fathers, living still,
In spite of dungeon, fire and sword;
O how our hearts beat high with joy
Whene'er we hear that glorious Word!

[1.2]
Faith of our fathers, holy faith!
We will be true to thee till death.

[2]
Faith of our fathers, we will strive To
Win all nations unto Thee;
And through the truth that comes from God,
We all shall then be truly free.

[3]
Faith of our fathers, we will love Both
Friend and foe in all our strife;
And preach Thee, too, as love knows how
By kindly words and virtuous life.

songs.title: Far, Far Away On Judea's Plains
songs.author: John Menzies MacFarlane (1833-1892)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Far, far away on Judea's plains,
Shepherds of old heard the joyous strains:

[1.2]
Glory to God, glory to God,
Glory to God in the Glory to God
Glory to God in the highest in the
Glory to God in the highest Glory to

[1.3]
God in the highest;
Peace on earth, good will to men;
Peace on earth, good will to men.

[2]
Sweet are these strains of redeeming love,
Message of mercy from heaven above:

[3]
Lord, with the angels we too would rejoice;
Help us to sing with the heart and voice:

[4]
Hasten the time when, from every clime,
Men shall unite in the strains sublime:

songs.title: Fear Not, O Little Flock
songs.author: King Gustavus Adolphus (1594-1632), Jacob Fabricius (1593-1654), Johann M. Altenburg (1584-1640) (trad. Catherine Winkworth (1827-1878))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Fear not, O little flock, the foe
Who madly seeks your overthrow;
Dread not his rage and pow'r;

[1.2]
What though your courage sometimes faints,
His seeming triumph o'er God's saints
Lasts but one little hour.

[2.1]
Be of good cheer; your cause belongs
To Him who can avenge your wrongs;
Leave it to Him our Lord.

[2.2]
Though hidden yet from all our eyes,
He sees the Gideon who shall rise;
To save us, and His word.

[3.1]
As true as God's own word is true,
Not earth nor hell with all their crew
Against us shall prevail.
A jest and by- word are they grown;

[3.2]
God is with us, we are His own,
Our vict'ry cannot fail.

[4.1]
Amen, Lord Jesus, grant our prayer!
Great Captain, now Thine arm make bare;
Fight for us once again.

[4.2]
So shall thy saints and martyrs raise
A mighty chorus to Thy praise,
World without end. Amen.

songs.title: For All The Saints
songs.author: William Walsham How (1823-1897)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
For all the saints, who from their labors rest,
Who Thee by faith before the world confessed,
Thy Name,
O Jesus, be forever blessed.

[1.2]
Alleluia,
Alleluia!

[1.3]
For the Evangelists, by whose blest word,
Like fourfold streams, the garden of the Lord,
Is fair and fruitful, be Thy Name adored.

[1.4]
Alleluia,
Alleluia!

[2.1]
Thou wast their Rock, their Fortress and their Might;
Thou,
Lord, their Captain in the well fought fight;
Thou, in the darkness drear, their one true Light.

[2.2]
For Martyrs, who with rapture kindled eye,
Saw the bright crown descending from the sky,
And seeing, grasped it,
Thee we glorify.

[3.1]
For the Apostles' glorious company,
Who bearing forth the Cross o'er land and sea,
Shook all the mighty world, we sing to Thee:
O blest communion, fellowship divine!

[3.2]
We feebly struggle, they in glory shine;
All are one in Thee, for all are Thine.

[4.1]
The golden evening brightens in the west;
Soon, soon to faithful warriors comes their rest;
Sweet is the calm of paradise the blessed.

[4.2]
O may Thy soldiers, faithful, true and bold,
Fight as the saints who nobly fought of old,
And win with them the victor's crown of gold.

[5.1]
But lo!
There breaks a yet more glorious day;
The saints triumphant rise in bright array;
The King of glory passes on His way.

[5.2]
And when the strife is fierce, the warfare long,
Steals on the ear the distant triumph song,
And hearts are brave, again, and arms are strong.

[6]
From earth's wide bounds, from ocean's farthest coast,
Through gates of pearl streams in the countless host,
And singing to Father, Son and Holy Ghost:

songs.title: For The Beauty Of The Earth
songs.author: Folliot Sandford Pierpoint (1835-1917)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
For the beauty of the earth
For the glory of the skies,
For the love which from our birth
Over and around us lies.

[1.2]
Lord of all, to Thee we raise,
This our hymn of grateful praise.

[2]
For the beauty of each hour,
Of the day and of the night,
Hill and vale, and tree and flow'r,
Sun and moon, and stars of light.

[3]
For the joy of ear and eye,
For the heart and mind's delight,
For the mystic harmony Linking sense to sound and sight.

[4]
For the joy of human love,
Brother, sister, parent, child,
Friends on earth and friends above,
For all gentle thoughts and mild.

[5]
For Thy Church, that evermore Lifteth holy hands above,
Off'ring up on every shore Her pure sacrifice of love.

[6]
For the martyrs' crown of light,
For Thy prophets' eagle eye,
For Thy bold confessors' might,
For the lips of infancy.

[7]
For Thy virgins' robes of snow,
For Thy maiden mother mild,
For Thyself, with hearts aglow,
Jesu, Victim undefiled.

[8]
For each perfect gift of Thine,
To our race so freely given,
Graces human and divine,
Flowers of earth and buds of Heaven.

songs.title: From Heaven Above To Earth I Come
