songs.author: Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. Catherine Winkworth (1827-1878))
songs.lyrics:
[1]
From Heaven above to earth I come,
To bear good news to every home;
Glad tidings of great joy I bring,
Whereof I now will say and sing.

[2]
To you, this night, is born a Child
Of Mary, chosen mother mild;
This tender Child of lowly birth,
Shall be the joy of all your earth.

[3]
'Tis Christ our God, Who far on high
Had heard your sad and bitter cry;
Himself will your Salvation be,
Himself from sin will make you free.

[4]
He brings those blessings long ago
Prepared by God for all below;
That in His heavenly kingdom blest
You may with us forever rest.

[5]
These are the tokens ye shall mark,
The swaddling clothes and manger dark;
There shall ye find the young Child laid,
By Whom the heav'ns and earth were made.

[6]
Now let us all, with gladsome cheer,
Follow the shepherds, and draw near
To see this wondrous Gift of God,
Who hath His own dear Son bestowed.

[7]
Give heed, my heart, lift up thine eyes!
What is it in yon manger lies?
Who is this Child, so young and fair?
The bless�d Christ Child lieth there!

[8]
Welcome to earth, Thou noble Guest,
Through Whom e'en wicked men are blest!
Thou com'st to share our misery,
What can we render, Lord, to Thee!

[9]
Ah, Lord, Who hast created all,
How hast Thou made Thee weak and small,
To lie upon the coarse dry grass,
The food of humble ox and ass.

[10]
Were earth a thousand times as fair,
Beset with gold and jewels rare,
She yet were far too poor to be
A narrow cradle, Lord, for Thee.

[11]
For velvets soft and silken stuff
Thou hast but hay and straw so rough,
Whereon Thou King, so rich and great,
As 'twere Thy heaven, art throned in state.

[12]
Thus hath it pleased Thee to make plain
The truth to us, poor fools and vain,
That this world's honor, wealth and might
Are naught and worthless in Thy sight.

[13]
Ah, dearest Jesus, holy Child,
Make Thee a bed, soft, undefiled,
Here in my poor heart's inmost shrine,
That I may evermore be Thine.

[14]
My heart for very joy doth leap,
My lips no more can silence keep,
I too must sing, with joyful tongue,
That sweetest ancient cradle song.

[15]
Glory to God in highest Heaven,
Who unto man His Son hath given,
While angels sing, with pious mirth,
A glad New Year to all the earth.

songs.title: From Nazareth
songs.author: Margaret Elizabeth Munson Sangster (1838-1912)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Comes any good from Nazareth?
The scornful challenge as of old
Is flung on many'a jeering breath
From cloistered cells and marts of gold.

[2]
Comes any good from Nazareth?
Behold, the mighty Nazarene,
The Lord of life, the Lord of death,
Through warring ages walks serene.

[3]
One touch upon His garment's fringe
Still heals the hurt of bitter years.
Before Him yet the demons cringe,
He gives the wine of joy for tears.

[4]
O city of the Carpenter,
Upon the hill slope old and gray,
The world among its pain and stir
Turns yearning eyes on thee today.

[5]
For He who dwelt in Nazareth,
And wrought with toil of hand and brain,
Alone gives victory to faith
Until the day He come again.

songs.title: Gabriel's Message
songs.author: Basque (trad. Sabine Baring Gould (1834-1924))
songs.lyrics:
[1]
The angel Gabriel from heaven came, his wings
As drifted snow, his eyes as flame;
"All hail," said he, "thou lowly maiden,
Mary, most highly favored lady," Gloria!

[2]
"For know a blessed Mother thou shalt be,
All generations laud and honor thee, thy Son
Shall be Emmanuel, by seers foretold,

[3]
Then gentle Mary meekly bowed her head, "To
Me be as it pleaseth God," she said,
"My soul shall laud and magnify His holy
Name."

[4]
Of her,
Emmanuel, the Christ was born in Bethlehem, all
On a Christmas morn, and Christian folk throughout
The world will ever say

songs.title: Gentle Mary Laid Her Child
songs.author: Joseph Simpson Cook (1859-1933)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Gentle Mary laid her Child
Lowly in a manger;
There He lay, the undefiled,
To the world a Stranger:

[1.2]
Such a Babe in such a place,
Can He be the Savior?
Ask the saved of all the race
Who have found His favor.

[2.1]
Angels sang about His birth;
Wise men sought and found Him;
Heaven's star shone brightly forth,
Glory all around Him:

[2.2]
Shepherds saw the wondrous sight,
Heard the angels singing;
All the plains were lit that night,
All the hills were ringing.

[3.1]
Gentle Mary laid her Child
Lowly in a manger;
He is still the undefiled,
But no more a stranger:

[3.2]
Son of God, of humble birth,
Beautiful the story;
Praise His Name in all the earth,
Hail the King of glory!

songs.title: Glorious Things of Thee are Spoken
songs.author: John Newton (1725-1807)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Glorious things of thee are spoken,
Zion city of our God;
He, Whose Word cannot be broken
Formed thee for His Own abode:

[1.2]
On the Rock of Ages founded,
What can shake thy sure repose?
With salvation's walls surrounded,
Thou mayst smile at all thy foes.

[2.1]
See, the streams of living waters,
Springing from Eternal Love,
Well supply thy sons and daughters,
And all fear of want remove:

[2.2]
Who can faint, while such a river
Ever will their thirst assuage?
Grace, which, like the Lord the Giver,
Never fails from age to age.

[3.1]
Round each habitation hov'ring,
See the cloud and fire appear,
For a glory and a cov'ring:
Showing that the Lord is near.

[3.2]
Thus deriving from their banner
Light by night, and shade by day,
Safe they feed upon the manna,
Which He gives them on their way.

[4.1]
Savior, if of Zion's city
I, through grace, a member am,
Let the world deride or pity,
I will glory in Thy Name:

[4.2]
Fading is the worldling's pleasure,
All his boasted pomp and show:
Solid joys and lasting treasure
None but Zion's children know.

songs.title: Go To Dark Gethsemane
songs.author: James Montgomery (1771-1854)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Go to dark Gethsemane,
Ye that feel the tempter's pow'r;

[1.2]
Your Redeemer's conflict see,
Watch with Him one bitter hour,
Turn not from His griefs away;
Learn from Jesus Christ to pray.

[2.1]
Follow to the judgment hall,
View the Lord of Life arraigned;
O the wormwood and the gall!
O the pangs His soul sustained!

[2.2]
Shun not suff'ring, shame, or loss;
Learn from Christ to bear the cross.

[3.1]
Calv'ry's mournful mountain climb;
There, adoring at His feet,
Mark that miracle of time,
God's own sacrifice complete.

[3.2]
"It is finished!" hear Him cry;
Learn from Jesus Christ to die.

[4.1]
Early hasten to the tomb
Where they laid His breathless clay;
All is solitude and gloom.
Who has taken Him away?

[4.2]
Christ is ris'n! He meets our eyes;
Savior, teach us so to rise.

songs.title: God Himself is Present
songs.author: Gerhard Tersteegen (1697-1769) (trad. Frederick William Foster (1760-1835), John Miller (1756-1790))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
God Himself is present:
Let us now adore Him,
And with awe appear before Him.

[1.2]
God is in His temple,
All within keep silence,
Prostrate lie with deepest reverence.

[1.3]
Him alone God we own,
Him our God and Savior;
Praise His name forever.

[2.1]
God Himself is present:
Hear the harps resounding!
See the crowds the throne surrounding!

[2.2]
"Holy, holy, holy",
Hear the hymn ascending,
Angels, saints, their voices blending!
Bow Thine ear to us here:

[2.3]
Hear, O Christ, the praises
That Thy Church now raises.

[3.1]
O Thou fount of blessing,
Purify my spirit;

[3.2]
Trusting only in Thy merit,
Like the holy angels
Who behold Thy glory,
May I ceaselessly adore Thee,

[3.3]
Let Thy will Ever still
Rule Thy Church terrestrial,
As the hosts celestial.

songs.title: God Rest Ye Merry Gentlemen
songs.author: English
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
God rest ye merry, gentlemen,
Let nothing you dismay,
Remember Christ our Savior
Was born on Christmas Day;

[1.2]
To save us all from Satan's pow'r
When we were gone astray.
O tidings of comfort and joy,

[1.3]
Comfort and joy;
O tidings of comfort and joy.

[2]
In Bethlehem, in Israel, this bless�d Babe was born,
And laid within a manger upon this bless�d morn;
The which His mother Mary did nothing take in scorn.

[3]
From God our heav'nly Father a bless�d angel came;
And unto certain shepherds brought tidings of the same;
How that in Bethlehem was born the Son of God by name.

[4.1]
"Fear not, then," said the angel, "Let nothing
You afright This day is born a Savior
Of a pure Virgin bright,

[4.2]
To free all those who trust in Him
From Satan's pow'r and might."

[5]
The shepherds at those tidings rejoiced much in mind,
And left their flocks afeeding in tempest, storm and wind,
And went to Bethl'em straightaway this bless�d Babe to find.

songs.title: God the Father Be Our Stay
songs.author: Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. Richard Massie (1800-1887))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
God the Father, be our Stay,
When hell's dread pow'rs assail us;
Cleanse us from our sins, we pray,
Nor in our last hour fail us.

[1.2]
Keep us from the Evil One;
Firm in the faith abiding,
In Christ our Savior hiding,
And heartily confiding.

[1.3]
Let us put God's armor on:
With all true Christians running
Our heav'nly race and shunning
The devil's wiles and cunning.

[1.4]
Amen, Amen, this be done,
So sing we, Hallelujah!

[2]
Jesus Christ be Thou our Stay,

[3]
Holy Ghost, be Thou our Stay,

[4]
1(Alt).
Triune God, be Thou our Stay,

songs.title: God Will Take Care of You
songs.author: Civilla Durfee Martin (1866-1948)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Be not dismayed whate'er betide,
God will take care of you;
Beneath His wings of love abide,
God will take care of you.

[1.2]
God will take care of you,
Through ev'ry day, o'er all the way;
He will take care of you,
God will take care of you.

[2]
Through days of toil when heart doth fail,
God will take care of you;
When dangers fierce your path assail,
God will take care of you.

[3]
All you may need He will provide,
God will take care of you;
Nothing you ask will be denied,
God will take care of you.

[4]
No matter what may be the test,
God will take care of you;
Lean, weary one, upon His breast,
God will take care of you.

songs.title: God, That Madest Earth and Heaven
songs.author: Reginald Heber (1783-1826), William Mercer (1811-1873), Richard Whately (1787-1863)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
God, that madest earth and Heaven,
Darkness and light;
Who the day for toil hast given,
For rest the night;

[1.2]
May Thine angel guards defend us,
Slumber sweet Thy mercy send us;
Holy dreams and hopes attend us,
All through the night.

[2.1]
And when morn again shall call us,
To run life's way,
May we still, whate'er befall us,
Thy will obey.

[2.2]
From the pow'r of evil hide us,
In the narrow pathway guide us,
Nor Thy smile be e'er denied us
All through the day.

[3.1]
Guard us waking, guard us sleeping,
And when we die,
May we in Thy mighty keeping
All peaceful lie;

[3.2]
When the last dread call shall wake us,
Do not Thou, our God, forsake us,
But to reign in glory take us
With Thee on high.

songs.title: God, Whose Almighty Word
songs.author: John Marriott (1780-1825)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
God, whose almighty word
Chaos and darkness heard
And took their flight:

[1.2]
Hear us, we humble pray,
And where the Gospel day
Sheds not its glorious ray,
Let there be light!

[2.1]
Lord, who once came to bring,
On your redeeming wing,
Healing and sight,
Health to the sick in mind,

[2.2]
Sight to the inly blind:
Oh, now to humankind
Let there be light!

[3.1]
Spirit of truth and love,
Life giving, holy dove,
Speed forth your flight;

[3.2]
Move on the water's face,
Bearing the lamp of grace,
And in earth's darkest place
Let there be light!

[4.1]
Holy and blessed three,
Glorious Trinity,
Wisdom, love, might!

[4.2]
Boundless as ocean's tide,
Rolling in fullest pride,
Through the earth, far and wide,
Let there be light!

songs.title: Guide Me, O Thou Great Jehovah
songs.author: William Williams (1717-1791) (trad. Peter Williams (1723-1796))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Guide me, O Thou great Jehovah,
Pilgrim through this barren land.
I am weak, but Thou art mighty;
Hold me with Thy pow'rful hand.

[1.2]
Bread of Heaven, Bread of Heaven,
Feed me till I want no more;
Feed me till I want no more.

[2.1]
Open now the crystal fountain,
Whence the healing stream doth flow;
Let the fire and cloudy pillar
Lead me all my journey through.

[2.2]
Strong Deliv'rer, strong Deliv'rer,
Be Thou still my Strength and Shield;
Be Thou still my Strength and Shield.

[3.1]
Lord, I trust Thy mighty power,
Wondrous are Thy works of old;
Thou deliver'st Thine from thralldom,
Who for naught themselves had sold:

[3.2]
Thou didst conquer, Thou didst conquer,
Sin, and Satan and the grave,
Sin, and Satan and the grave.

[4.1]
When I tread the verge of Jordan,
Bid my anxious fears subside;
Death of deaths, and hell's destruction,
Land me safe on Canaan's side.

[4.2]
Songs of praises, songs of praises,
I will ever give to Thee;
I will ever give to Thee.

[5.1]
Musing on my habitation,
Musing on my heav'nly home,
Fills my soul with holy longings:
Come, my Jesus, quickly come;

[5.2]
Vanity is all I see;
Lord,
I long to be with Thee!

[5.3]
Lord,
I long to be with Thee!

songs.title: Hallelujah, What a Savior!
songs.author: Philip Paul Bliss (1838-1876)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Man of Sorrows! what a name
For the Son of God, who came
Ruined sinners to reclaim.
Hallelujah! What a Savior!

[2]
Bearing shame and scoffing rude,
In my place condemned He stood;
Sealed my pardon with His blood.

[3]
Guilty, vile, and helpless we;
Spotless Lamb of God was He;
"Full atonement!" can it be?

[4]
Lifted up was He to die;
"It is finished!" was His cry;
Now in Heav'n exalted high.

[5]
When He comes, our glorious King,
All His ransomed home to bring,
Then anew His song we'll sing:

songs.title: Happy the Man Who Feareth God
songs.author: Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. Richard Massie (1800-1887))
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Happy the man who feareth God,
Whose feet His holy ways have trod;
Thine own good hand shall nourish thee,
And well and happy shalt thou be.

[2]
Thy wife shall, like a fruitful vine,
Fill all thy house with clusters fine;
Thy children all be fresh and sound,
Like olive- plants thy table round.

[3]
Lo! to the man these blessings cleave
Who in God's holy fear doth live;
From him the ancient curse hath fled
By Adam's race inherited.

[4]
Out of Mount Zion God shall send,
And crown with joy thy latter end;
That thou Jerusalem mayst see,
In favor and prosperity.

[5]
He shall be with thee in thy ways,
And give thee health and length of days
Yea, thou shalt children's children see,
And peace on Israel shall be.

songs.title: Hark the Glad Sound
songs.author: Philip Doddridge (1702-1751)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Hark, the glad sound!
The Savior comes!
The Sa* vior promised long;

[1.2]
Let every heart prepare a throne,
And every voice a song.

[2]
On Him the Spirit, largely poured,
Exerts* its sacred Fire;
Wisdom and might, and zeal and love,
His holy Breast inspire.

[3]
He comes the pris'ners to release,
In Sa* tan's bondage held;
The gates of brass before Him burst,
The iron fetters yield.

[4]
He comes from thickest films of vice
To clear* the mental ray,
And on the eyeballs of the blind
To pour celestial day.

[5]
He comes the broken heart to bind,
The bleed* ing soul to cure;
And with the treasures of His grace T'enrich the humble poor.

[6]
His silver trumpets publish loud
The jub'lee of the Lord
Our debts are all remitted now
Our heritage restored.

[7]
Our glad hosannas, Prince of Peace,
Thy welcome shall proclaim;
And Heav'n's eternal arches ring
With Thy belov�d name.

songs.title: Hark, Hark, My Soul!
songs.author: Frederick William Faber (1814-1863)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Hark!
Hark, my soul!
Angelic songs are swelling O'er earth's green fields
And ocean's wave- beat shore:

[1.2]
How sweet the truth those bless�d strains are
Telling Of that new life when sin shall
Be no more!

[1.3]
Onward we go, for still we hear them
Sing, "Come, weary souls, for Jesus bids you
Come";

[2.1]
And through the dark, its echoes sweetly ringing,
The music of the Gospel leads us home.

[2.2]
Far, far away, like bells at ev'ning pealing,
The voice of Jesus sounds o'er land and sea,
And laden souls, by thousands meekly stealing,
Kind Shepherd, turn their weary steps to Thee.

[3.1]
Faith's journeys end in welcome to the weary,
And Heav'n, the heart's true home will come at last.
Angels, sing on, your faithful watches keeping,
Sing us sweet fragments of the songs above;

[3.2]
Till morning's joy shall end the night of weeping,
And life's long shadows break in cloudless love.

songs.title: Hark, the Voice of Jesus Calling
songs.author: Daniel March (1816-1909)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Hark, the voice of Jesus calling,
"Who will go and work today?
Fields are ripe and harvests waiting,
Who will bear the sheaves away?"

[1.2]
Long and loud the Master calls us,
Rich reward He offers free;
Who will answer, gladly saying,
"Here am I, send me, send me?"

[2.1]
If you cannot cross the ocean,
And the distant lands explore,
You can find the lost around you,
You can help them at your door;

[2.2]
If you cannot give your thousands,
You can give the widow's mite;
What you truly give for Jesus,
Will be precious in His sight.

[3.1]
If you cannot speak like angels,
If you cannot preach like Paul,
You can tell the love of Jesus,
You can say He died for all.

[3.2]
If you cannot rouse the wicked,
With the judgment's dread alarms,
You can lead the little children
To the Savior's waiting arms.

[4.1]
If you cannot be the watchman,
Standing high on Zion's wall,
Pointing out the path to heaven,
Off'ring life and peace to all,

[4.2]
With your prayers and with your bounties
You can do what heav'n demands;
You can be like faithful Aaron,
Holding up the prophet's hands.

[5.1]
If among the older people,
You may not be apt to teach,
"Feed My lambs," said Christ, our Shepherd,
"Place the food within their reach."

[5.2]
And it may be that the children
You have led with trembling hand,
Will be found among your jewels,
When you reach the better land.

[6]
Let none hear you idly saying, "There is nothing I can do."
While the lost of earth are dying, And the Master calls for you;
Take the task He gives you gladly; Let His work your pleasure be;
Answer quickly when He calls you, "Here am I, send me, send me."

songs.title: Hark! The Herald Angels Sing
songs.author: Charles Wesley (1707-1788)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Hark! The herald angels sing,
"Glory to the newborn King;
Peace on earth, and mercy mild,
God and sinners reconciled!"

[1.2]
Joyful, all ye nations rise,
Join the triumph of the skies;
With th'angelic host proclaim,
"Christ is born in Bethlehem!"

[1.3]
Hark! the herald angels sing,
"Glory to the newborn King!"

[2.1]
Christ, by highest Heav'n adored;
Christ the everlasting Lord;
Late in time, behold Him come,
Offspring of a virgin's womb.

[2.2]
Veiled in flesh the Godhead see;
Hail th'incarnate Deity,
Pleased with us in flesh to dwell,
Jesus our Emmanuel.

[3.1]
Hail the heav'nly Prince of Peace!
Hail the Sun of Righteousness!
Light and life to all He brings,
Ris'n with healing in His wings.

[3.2]
Mild He lays His glory by,
Born that man no more may die.
Born to raise the sons of earth,
Born to give them second birth.

[4.1]
Come,
Desire of nations, come,
Fix in us Thy humble home;

[4.2]
Rise, the woman's conqu'ring Seed,
Bruise in us the serpent's head.
Now display Thy saving power,

[4.3]
Ruined nature now restore;
Now in mystic union join Thine to ours, and ours to Thine.

[5.1]
Adam's likeness,
Lord, efface,
Stamp Thine image in its place:

[5.2]
Second Adam from above,
Reinstate us in Thy love.
Let us Thee, though lost, regain,
Thee, the Life, the inner man:

[5.3]
O, to all Thyself impart,
Formed in each believing heart.

songs.title: Have Mercy On Me, O My God
songs.author: Brian L. Penney (1951-)

songs.title: He Keeps Me Singing
songs.author: Luther Burgess Bridgers (1884-1948)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
There's within my heart a melody
Jesus whispers sweet and low,
"Fear not, I am with thee, peace, be still,"
In all of life's ebb and flow.

[1.2]
Jesus, Jesus, Jesus,-
Sweetest name I know,
Fills my ev'ry longing,
Keeps me singing as I go.

[2]
All my life was wrecked by sin and strife,
Discord filled my heart with pain,
Jesus swept across the broken strings,
Stirred the slumb'ring chords again.

[3]
Feasting on the riches of His grace,
Resting 'neath His shelt'ring wing,
Always looking on His smiling face,
That is why I shout and sing.

[4]
Though sometimes He leads through waters deep,
Trials fall across the way,
Though sometimes the path seems rough and steep,
See His footprints all the way.

[5]
Soon He's coming back to welcome me,
Far beyond the starry sky;
I shall wing my flight to worlds unknown,
I shall reign with Him on high.

songs.title: He Leadeth Me
songs.author: Joseph Henry Gilmore (1834-1918)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
He leadeth me, O bless�d thought!
O words with heav'nly comfort fraught!
Whate'er I do, where'er I be
Still 'tis God's hand that leadeth me.

[1.2]
He leadeth me, He leadeth me,
By His own hand He leadeth me;
His faithful follow'r I would be,
For by His hand He leadeth me.

[2]
Sometimes mid scenes of deepest gloom,
Sometimes where Eden's bowers bloom,
By waters still, ov'r troubled sea,
Still 'tis His hand that leadeth me.

[3.1]
Lord,
I would place my hand in Thine,
Nor ever murmur nor repine;

[3.2]
Content, whatever lot I see,
Since 'tis my God that leadeth me.

[4]
And when my task on earth is done,
When by Thy grace the vict'ry's won,
E'en death's cold wave I will not flee,
Since God through Jordan leadeth me.

songs.title: He Was Not Willing
songs.author: Lucy Jane Rider Meyer (1849-1922)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
"He was not willing that any should perish";
Jesus enthroned in the glory above,
Saw our poor fallen world, pitied our sorrows,
Poured out His life for us, wonderful love!

[1.2]
Perishing, perishing! Thronging our pathway,
Hearts break with burdens too heavy to bear:
Jesus would save, but there's no one to tell them,
No one to lift them from sin and despair.

[2.1]
"He was not willing that any should perish";
Clothed in our flesh with its sorrow and pain,
Came He to seek the lost, comfort the mourner,
Heal the heart broken by sorrow and shame.

[2.2]
Perishing, perishing! Harvest is passing,
Reapers are few and the night draweth near:
Jesus is calling thee, haste to the reaping,
Thou shalt have souls, precious souls for thy hire.

[3.1]
Plenty for pleasure, but little for Jesus;
Time for the world with its troubles and toys,
No time for Jesus' work, feeding the hungry,
Lifting lost souls to eternity's joys.

[3.2]
Perishing, perishing! Hark, how they call us;
Bring us your Savior, oh, tell us of Him!
We are so weary, so heavily laden,
And with long weeping our eyes have grown dim.

[4.1]
"He was not willing that any should perish";
Am I His follower, and can I live
Longer at ease with a soul going downward,
Lost for the lack of the help I might give!

[4.2]
Perishing, perishing! Thou wast not willing;
Master, forgive, and inspire us anew;
Banish our worldliness, help us to ever
Live with eternity's values in view.

songs.title: He Who Would Valiant Be
songs.author: John Bunyan (1628-1688), Percy Dearmer (1867-1936)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
He who would valiant be 'gainst all disaster,
Let him in constancy follow the Master.
There's no discouragement shall make him once relent
His first avowed intent to be a pilgrim.

[2]
Who so beset him round with dismal stories
Do but themselves confound his strength the more is.
No foes shall stay his might; though he with giants fight,
He will make good his right to be a pilgrim.

[3]
Since, Lord, Thou dost defend us with Thy Spirit,
We know we at the end, shall life inherit.
Then fancies flee away! I'll fear not what men say,
I'll labor night and day to be a pilgrim.

songs.title: His Gifts
songs.author: Brian James Dumont (1971-)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
It's His gift, this creation,
All the glory we see,
It's the gift laid out for Adam and for Eve,
But as they turned away from His world so bright,

[1.2]
It would plunge us deep into fear of the Light.
Life, life poured out on you and me
He calls us to live and His Glory to see

[1.3]
Our Lord calls us home with Him to be
In His presence living eternally!

[2.1]
It's His gift, incarnation,
He became us to be All the things
Our fallen race could never be.

[2.2]
Our nature He would take and then justify,
To the Law's demands Christ would fully comply.

[3.1]
It's His gift, our redemption, bought and paid
In His blood All God's wrath poured out
In one tremendous flood.

[3.2]
The ransom paid for all in His act
Of Grace meant to bring you into His
Loving embrace.

[4.1]
It's His gift, resurrection Raised to life so
That we May also with Him in glory
Always be.

[4.2]
His new life is God's promise and guarantee
Of the gift He prepares for you and
For me.

[5.1]
It's His gift,
His ascension we await His return.
Not alone, yet for His nearer presence yearn.

[5.2]
Christ leads us to the Father and makes
Our home Where we'll sing together around His
Throne.

[6]
It's His gift, of His Spirit poured on us in His Word
Who reminds us of all Jesus taught and did.
His Peace was sent to Comfort and be with us
And sustain our faith in the Lord's promises.

[7]
It's His gift, our repentance even this is from Him!
When His Law and Spirit move our hearts within,
They crush our vain ambition and very thoughts,
Drive us each to God's mercy\- His Kingdom is wrought!

[8]
It's His gift of Baptism washed us clean in His Son
Placed us in His Name and took us as His own
What comfort giv'n to us in this life-long trust
Given faith that Christ's work is applied now to us.

[9]
It's His Gift of His Table where He feeds us His sheep;
Blest communion with our God forever sweet.
His Body and His Blood poured out for us all
Giv'n to heal our wounds and restore our_ soul.

[10]
It's His Gift of eternal life spent in His embrace,
To be with the Father and to sing His praise
And so with God the Son who redeemed our souls
With the Spirit together forever extolled.

songs.title: Holy Ghost, with Light Divine
songs.author: Andrew Reed (1787-1862), Samuel Longfellow (1819-1892)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Holy Ghost, with light divine
Shine upon this heart of mine;
Chase the shades of night away,
Turn the darkness into day.

[2]
Let me see my Savior's face,
Let me all His beauties trace;
Show those glorious truths to me
Which are only known to Thee.

[3]
Holy Ghost, with pow'r divine
Cleanse this guilty heart of mine;
In Thy mercy pity me,
From sin's bondage set me free.

[4]
Holy Ghost, with joy divine
Cheer this saddened heart of mine;
Yield a sacred, settled peace,
Let it grow and still increase.

[5]
Holy Spirit, all divine,
Dwell within this heart of mine;
Cast down every idol- throne,
Reign supreme, and reign alone.

[6]
See, to Thee I yield my heart,
Shed Thy life through every part;
A pure temple I would be,
Wholly dedicate to Thee.

[7]
Holy Spirit, Truth divine,
Dawn upon this soul of mine;
Word of God and inward light
Wake my spirit, clear my sight.

[8]
Holy Spirit, Love divine,
Glow within this heart of mine;
Kindle every high desire;
Perish self in Thy pure fire.

[9]
Holy Spirit, Power divine
Fill and nerve this will of mine;
Grant that I may strongly live,
Bravely bear, and nobly strive.

[10]
Holy Spirit, Right divine,
King within my conscience reign;
Be my Lord, and I shall be
Firmly bound, forever free.

[11]
Holy Spirit, Peace divine,
Still this restless heart of mine;
Speak to calm this tossing sea,
Stayed in Thy tranquility.

[12]
Holy Spirit, Joy divine,
Gladden Thou this heart of mine;
In the desert ways I sing,
"Spring, O Well, forever spring."

[13]
Now incline me to repent,
Let me now my sins lament,
Now my foul revolt deplore,
Weep, believe, and sin no more.

songs.title: Holy God, We Praise Thy Name
songs.author: Ignaz Franz (1719-1790) (trad. Clarence Alphonsus Walworth (1820-1900))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Holy God, we praise Thy Name;
Lord of all, we bow before Thee!
All on earth Thy scepter claim,
All in Heaven above adore Thee;

[1.2]
Infinite Thy vast domain,
Everlasting is Thy reign.

[2.1]
Hark!
The loud celestial hymn Angel choirs above are raising,
Cherubim and seraphim,
In unceasing chorus praising;

[2.2]
Fill the heavens with sweet accord:
Holy, holy, holy,
Lord.

[3.1]
Lo! the apostolic train
Join the sacred Name to hallow;
Prophets swell the loud refrain,
And the white robed martyrs follow;

[3.2]
And from morn to set of sun,
Through the Church the song goes on.

[4.1]
Holy Father, Holy Son,
Holy Spirit, Three we name Thee;
While in essence only One,
Undivided God we claim Thee;

[4.2]
And adoring bend the knee,
While we own the mystery.

songs.title: Holy Spirit, Ever Dwelling
songs.author: Timothy Rees (1874-1939)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Holy Spirit, ever dwelling
In the holiest realms of light
Holy Spirit, ever brooding
O'er a world of gloom and blight

[1.2]
Holy Spirit, ever raising
Earthbound souls to glory high
Living, life- imparting Spirit
You we praise and magnify.

[2.1]
Holy Spirit, ever breathing
On the church the breath of life
Holy Spirit, ever striving
Through your people's ceaseless strife

[2.2]
Holy Spirit, ever forming
In the church the mind of Christ
In our worship we will praise you
For your fruit and gifts unpriced.

[3.1]
Holy Spirit, ever working
Through the church's ministry
Quick'ning, strength'ning, and absolving
Setting captive sinners free

[3.2]
Holy Spirit, ever binding
Age to age and soul to soul
In community unending
You we worship and extol.

songs.title: Holy, Holy, Holy
songs.author: Reginald Heber (1783-1826)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Holy, holy, holy!
Lord God Almighty!
Early in the morning our song shall rise to Thee;

[1.2]
Holy, holy, holy, merciful and mighty!
God in three Persons, blessed Trinity!

[2.1]
Holy, holy, holy!
All the saints adore Thee,
Casting down their golden crowns around the glassy sea;

[2.2]
Cherubim and seraphim falling down before Thee,
Who was, and is, and evermore shall be.

[3.1]
Holy, holy, holy!
Though the darkness hide Thee,
Though the eye of sinful man Thy glory may not see;
Only Thou art holy;

[3.2]
There is none beside Thee,
Perfect in pow'r, in love, and purity.

[4.1]
Holy, holy, holy!
Lord God Almighty! All
Thy works shall praise Thy Name,
In earth, and sky, and sea;

[4.2]
Holy, holy, holy;
Merciful and mighty!
God in three Persons,
Blessed Trinity!

songs.title: Hosanna, Loud Hosanna
songs.author: Jeanette Threlfall (1821-1880)
songs.composer: Wurttemberg, 1784 from Gesangbuch der Herzogl. Hofkapelle
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Hosanna, loud hosanna,
The little children sang;
Through pillared court and temple
The lovely anthem rang.

[1.2]
To Jesus, Who had blessed them
Close folded to His breast,
The children sang their praises,
The simplest and the best.

[2.1]
From Olivet they followed
Mid an exultant crowd,
The victor palm branch waving,
And chanting clear and loud.

[2.2]
The Lord of men and angels
Rode on in lowly state,
Nor scorned that little children
Should on His bidding wait.

[3.1]
"Hosanna in the highest!"
That ancient song we sing,
For Christ is our Redeemer,
The Lord of heav'n our King.

[3.2]
O may we ever praise Him
With heart and life and voice,
And in His blissful presence
Eternally rejoice!

songs.title: How Firm A Foundation
songs.author: John Rippon (1751-1836)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
How firm a foundation, ye saints of the Lord,
Is laid for your faith in His excellent Word!
What more can He say than to you He hath said,
You, who unto Jesus for refuge have fled?

[2]
In every condition, in sickness, in health;
In poverty's vale, or abounding in wealth;
At home and abroad, on the land, on the sea,
As thy days demand, shall thy strength ever be.

[3]
Fear not, I am with thee, O be not dismayed,
For I am thy God and will still give thee aid;
I'll strengthen and help thee, and cause thee to stand
Upheld by My righteous, omnipotent hand.

[4]
When through the deep waters I call thee to go,
The rivers of woe shall not thee overflow;
For I will be with thee, thy troubles to bless,
And sanctify to thee thy deepest distress.

[5]
When through fiery trials thy pathways shall lie,
My grace, all sufficient, shall be thy supply;
The flame shall not hurt thee; I only design
Thy dross to consume, and thy gold to refine.

[6]
Even down to old age all My people shall prove
My sovereign, eternal, unchangeable love;
And when hoary hairs shall their temples adorn,
Like lambs they shall still in My bosom be borne.

[7]
The soul that on Jesus has leaned for repose,
I will not, I will not desert to its foes;
That soul, though all hell should endeavor to shake,
I'll never, no never, no never forsake.

songs.title: How Shall We Answer Terror's Cry?
songs.author: Richard W. Adams (1952-)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
How shall we answer terror's cry,
The cunning blade, the flaming sky?

[1.2]
When murderous spite knocks down our door
And violence breaks upon our shore,
O let us come and look to You
To know Your will what shall we do?

[2.1]
When Satan whispers, 'Hate your foe,
Now take your vengeance draw the bow,'
Protect us from the tempter's guile,
The lying voice, the evil smile.

[2.2]
O let us come in trust to You,
To hear the word we know is true.

[3.1]
When executioners hung You high
You turned Your prayer up to the sky,
And pled the Father to forgive,
You asked that cruel men might live.

[3.2]
O let us Your example take,
And pray for sinners as we ache.

[4.1]
We pray that You their hearts will turn;
And light a holy fire to burn
Their dross away, so they may be
Like gold refined, eternally.

[4.2]
O let us pray that they become,
Like us, with You forever one.

songs.title: I Am Jesus' Little Lamb
songs.author: Henrietta Luise von Hayn (1724-1782) (trad. composite)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
I am Jesus' little lamb,
Ever glad at heart I am;

[1.2]
For my Shepherd gently guides me,
Knows my need, and well provides me,
Loves me ev'ry day the same,
Even calls me by my name.

[2.1]
Day by day, at home, away,
Jesus is my Staff and Stay.
When I hunger, Jesus feeds me,
Into pleasant pastures leads me;

[2.2]
When I thirst, He bids me go
Where the quiet waters flow.

[3.1]
Who so happy as I am,
Even now the Shepherd's lamb?

[3.2]
And when my short life is ended,
By His angel host attended,
He shall fold me to His breast,
There within His arms to rest.

songs.title: I Bind Unto Myself Today
songs.author: Patrick of Ireland (circa 387-493) (trad. Cecil Frances Humphreys Alexander (1818-1895))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
I bind unto myself today
The strong Name of the Trinity,
By invocation of the same
The Three in One and One in Three.

[1.2]
His bursting from the spic�d tomb,
His riding up the heav'nly way,
His coming at the day of doom
I bind unto myself today.

[2.1]
I bind this day to me forever By power of faith,
Christ's incarnation;
His baptism in the Jordan river,
His death on Cross for my salvation;

[2.2]
Confessors' faith,
Apostles' word,
The Patriarchs' prayers, the prophets' scrolls,
All good deeds done unto the Lord And purity of virgin souls.

[3.1]
I bind unto myself the power Of the great love of cherubim;
The sweet "Well done" in judgment hour,
The service of the seraphim,
The flashing of the lightning free,

[3.2]
The whirling wind's tempestuous shocks,
The stable earth, the deep salt sea Around the old eternal rocks.

[4.1]
I bind unto myself today The virtues of the star lit heaven,
The glorious sun's life giving ray,
The whiteness of the moon at even,
The wisdom of my God to teach,

[4.2]
His hand to guide,
His shield to ward;
The word of God to give me speech,
His heav'nly host to be my guard.

[5.1]
I bind unto myself today The power of
God to hold and lead,
His eye to watch,

[5.2]
His might to stay,
His ear to hearken to my need.

[6.1]
Against the demon snares of sin,
The vice that gives temptation force,
The natural lusts that war within,
The hostile men that mar my course;

[6.2]
Or few or many, far or nigh,
In every place and in all hours,
Against their fierce hostility
I bind to me these holy powers.

[7.1]
Against all Satan's spells and wiles,
Against false words of heresy,
Against the knowledge that defiles,
Against the heart's idolatry,

[7.2]
Against the wizard's evil craft,
Against the death wound and the burning,
The choking wave, the poisoned shaft,
Protect me, Christ, till Thy returning.

[8.1]
Christ be with me, Christ within me,
Christ behind me, Christ before me,
Christ beside me, Christ to win me,
Christ to comfort and restore me.

[8.2]
Christ beneath me, Christ above me,
Christ in quiet, Christ in danger,
Christ in hearts of all that love me,
Christ in mouth of friend and stranger.

[9.1]
I bind unto myself the Name,
The strong Name of the Trinity,
By invocation of the same,
The Three in One and One in Three.

[9.2]
By Whom all nature hath creation,
Eternal Father, Spirit, Word:
Praise to the Lord of my salvation,
Salvation is of Christ the Lord.

songs.title: I Come, O Savior, To Thy Table
songs.author: Friedrich Christian Heyder (1677-1754) (trad. composite)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
I come, O Savior, to Thy table,
For weak and weary is my soul;
Thou, Bread of Life, alone art able
To satisfy and make me whole:

[1.2]
Lord, may Thy body and Thy blood
Be for my soul the highest good!

[2.1]
Oh, grant that I in manner worthy May
Now approach Thy heav'nly board And, as I
Lowly bow before Thee,

[2.2]
Look only unto Thee,
O Lord!

[3.1]
Unworthy though I am,
O Savior,
Because I have a sinful heart,

[3.2]
Yet Thou Thy lamb wilt banish never,
For Thou my faithful Shepherd art:

[4]
Oh, let me loathe all sin forever As
Death and poison to my soul That I
Through willful sinning never May see Thy judgment
Take its toll!

[5]
Thy heart is filled with fervent yearning That
Sinners may salvation see Who,
Lord, to Thee in faith are turning;
So I, a sinner, come to Thee.

songs.title: I Heard The Bells On Christmas Day
songs.author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow (1807-1882)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
I heard the bells on Christmas day
Their old familiar carols play,
And wild and sweet the words repeat
Of peace on earth, good will to men.

[2]
And thought how, as the day had come,
The belfries of all Christendom
Had rolled along th'unbroken song
Of peace on earth, good will to men.

[3]
Till ringing, singing on its way
The world revolved from night to day,
A voice, a chime, a chant sublime
Of peace on earth, good will to men.

[4]
And in despair I bowed my head
"There is no peace on earth," I said,
"For hate is strong and mocks the song
Of peace on earth, good will to men."

[5]
Then pealed the bells more loud and deep:
"God is not dead, nor doth He sleep;
The wrong shall fail, the right prevail
With peace on earth, good will to men."

songs.title: I Know That My Redeemer Lives
songs.author: Samuel Medley (1738-1799)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
I know that my Redeemer lives;
What comfort this sweet sentence gives!
He lives, He lives, who once was dead;
He lives, my ever living Head.

[2]
He lives to bless me with His love,
He lives to plead for me above.
He lives my hungry soul to feed,
He lives to help in time of need.

[3]
He lives triumphant from the grave,
He lives eternally to save,
He lives all glorious in the sky,
He lives exalted there on high.

[4]
He lives to grant me rich supply,
He lives to guide me with His eye,
He lives to comfort me when faint,
He lives to hear my soul's complaint.

[5]
He lives to silence all my fears,
He lives to wipe away my tears
He lives to calm my troubled heart,
He lives all blessings to impart.

[6]
He lives, my kind, wise, heavenly Friend,
He lives and loves me to the end;
He lives, and while He lives, Ill sing;
He lives, my Prophet, Priest, and King.

[7]
He lives and grants me daily breath;
He lives, and I shall conquer death:
He lives my mansion to prepare;
He lives to bring me safely there.

[8]
He lives, all glory to His Name!
He lives, my Jesus, still the same.
Oh, the sweet joy this sentence gives,
I know that my Redeemer lives!

songs.title: I Know Whom I Have Believed
songs.author: Daniel Webster Whittle (1840-1901), Elias Nathan (1840-1901)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
I know not why God's wondrous grace
To me He hath made known,
Nor why, unworthy, Christ in love
Redeemed me for His own.

[1.2]
But I know Whom I have believ�d,
And am persuaded that He is able
To keep that which I've committed
Unto Him against that day.

[2]
I know not how this saving faith To me He did impart,
Nor how believing in His Word Wrought peace within my heart.

[3]
I know not how the Spirit moves,
Convincing us of sin,
Revealing Jesus through the Word,
Creating faith in Him.

[4]
I know not what of good or ill
May be reserved for me,
Of weary ways or golden days,
Before His face I see.

[5]
I know not when my Lord may come,
At night or noonday fair,
Nor if I walk the vale with Him,
Or meet Him in the air.

songs.title: I Need Thee Every Hour
songs.author: Annie Sherwood Hawks (1836-1918)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
I need Thee ev'ry hour, Most gracious Lord;
No tender voice like Thine Can peace afford.
I need Thee, O I need Thee;

[1.2]
Ev'ry hour I need Thee;
O bless me now, my Savior, I come to Thee!

[2]
I need Thee ev'ry hour,
Stay Thou near by;
Temptations lose their pow'r When Thou art nigh.

[3]
I need Thee ev'ry hour,
In joy or pain;
Come quickly and abide,
Or life is vain.

[4]
I need Thee ev'ry hour,
Teach me Thy will;
And Thy rich promises In me fulfill.

[5]
I need Thee ev'ry hour,
Most Holy One;
O make me Thine indeed,
Thou blessed Son!

songs.title: I Place My Trust In God
songs.author: Dorothy Amstutz, Loren J. Kropf (1989-)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
I placed my trust in God today,
For it is He who knows the way,
And when uncertainties arise,
I trust His judgment, true and wise.

[1.2]
I'll place my trust in God today,
Even when I cannot see the way,
He'll lead me on with His strong hand,
Until I reach the promised land.

[2]
I placed my trust in God today,
Alone I could not find my way.
Led by His guidance, safe and sure,
I then can rest in peace, secure.

[3]
I place my trust in God each day,
Committed, yielded to His way.
Naught can o'erthrow me when I'm there Beneath His everlasting care.

[4]
I'll place my trust in God each day,
And while I walk the narrow way,
Each burden God will help me bear;
He hears my cry, my ev'ry prayer.

[5.1]
I'll place my trust in God each day,
Yes, even though the skies are gray.
Led by His hand,

[5.2]
I will not fear;
I know that God is always near.

songs.title: I Sing the Mighty Power of God
songs.author: Isaac Watts (1674-1748)
songs.composer: Wurttemberg, 1784 from Gesangbuch der Herzogl. Hofkapelle
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
I sing the mighty pow'r of God,
That made the mountains rise;
That spread the flowing seas abroad,
And built the lofty skies.

[1.2]
I sing the wisdom that ordained
The sun to rule the day:
The moon shines full at His command,
And all the stars obey.

[2.1]
I sing the goodness of the Lord,
That filled the earth with food:
He formed the creatures with His word,
And then pronounced them good.

[2.2]
Lord, how Thy wonders are displayed,
Where'er I turn my eye;
If I survey the ground I tread,
Or gaze upon the sky.

[3.1]
There's not a plant or flow'r below,
But makes Thy glories known;
And clouds arise and tempests blow,
By order from Thy throne.

[3.2]
Creatures that borrow life from Thee
Are subject to Thy care:
There's not a place where we can flee,
But God is present there.

songs.title: I'm But A Stranger Here
songs.author: Thomas Rawson Taylor (1807-1835)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
I'm but a stranger here,
Heav'n is my home;
Earth is a desert drear,
Heav'n is my home.

[1.2]
Danger and sorrow stand
Round me on every hand;
Heav'n is my fatherland,
Heav'n is my home.

[2.1]
What though the tempest rage,
Heav'n is my home;
Short is my pilgrimage,
Heav'n is my home;

[2.2]
Time's wild and wintry blast
Soon shall be over past;
I shall reach home at last,
Heav'n is my home.

[3.1]
There at my Savior's side
Heav'n is my home;
I shall be glorified,
Heav'n is my home.

[3.2]
There are the good and blest,
Those I loved most and best;
There, too, I soon shall rest,
Heav'n is my home.

[4.1]
Therefore I murmur not,
Heav'n is my home;
Whate'er my earthly lot,
Heav'n is my home;

[4.2]
And I shall surely stand
There at my Lord's right hand.
Heav'n is my fatherland,
Heav'n is my home.

songs.title: If God Had Not Been on Our Side
songs.author: Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. composite)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
If God had not been on our side
And had not come to aid us,
The foes with all their pow'r and pride
Would surely have dismayed us;

[1.2]
For we, His flock, would have to fear
The threat of men both far and near
Who rise in might against us.

[2.1]
Their furious wrath, did God permit,
Would surely have consumed us
And as a deep and yawning pit
With life and limb entombed us.

[2.2]
Like men o'er whom dark waters roll
Their wrath would have engulfed our soul
And, like a flood, o'erwhelmed us.

[3.1]
Blest be the Lord, who foiled their threat
That they could not devour us;
Our souls, like birds, escaped their net,
They could not overpow'r us.

[3.2]
The snare is broken we are free!
Our help is ever, Lord, in Thee,
Who madest earth and heaven.

songs.title: If God Himself Be For Me
songs.author: Paul Gerhardt (1607-1676) (trad. Richard Massie (1800-1887))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
If God Himself be for me,
I may a host defy;
For when I pray, before me
My foes, confounded, fly.

[1.2]
If Christ, my Head and Master,
Befriend me from above,
What foe or what disaster
Can drive me from His love?

[2.1]
This I believe, yea, rather,
Of this I make my boast,
That God is my dear Father,
The Friend who loves me most,

[2.2]
And that, whate'er betide me,
My Savior is at hand
Through stormy seas to guide me
And bring me safe to land.

[3.1]
I build on this foundation,
That Jesus and His blood
Alone are my salvation,
The true, eternal good.

[3.2]
Without Him all that pleases
Is valueless on earth;
The gifts I owe to Jesus
Alone my love are worth.

[4.1]
My Jesus is my Splendor,
My Sun, my Light, alone;

[4.2]
Were He not my Defender
Before God's awe- full throne,
I never should find favor
And mercy in His sight,

[4.3]
But be destroyed forever
As darkness by the light.

[5.1]
He canceled my offenses,
Delivered me from death;
He is the Lord who cleanses
My soul from sin through faith.

[5.2]
In Him I can be cheerful,
Bold, and undaunted aye;
In Him I am not fearful
Of God's great Judgment Day.

[6]
Naught, naught, can now condemn me Nor set my hope aside;
Now hell no more can claim me, Its fury I deride.
No sentence e'er reproves me, No ill destroys my peace;
For Christ, my Savior, loves me And shields me with His grace.

[7]
His Spirit in me dwelleth, And o'er my mind He reigns.
All sorrow He dispelleth And soothes away all pains.
He crowns His work with blessing And helpeth me to cry,
"My Father!" without ceasing, To Him who dwells on high.

[8]
And when my soul is lying Weak, trembling, and opprest,
He pleads with groans and sighing That cannot be exprest;
But God's quick eye discerns them, Although they give no sound,
And into language turns them E'en in the heart's deep ground.

[9]
To mine His Spirit speaketh Sweet word of holy cheer,
How God to him that seeketh For rest is always near
And how He hath erected A city fair and new,
Where what our faith expected We evermore shall view.

[10]
In yonder home doth flourish My heritage, my lot;
Though here I die and perish, My heaven shall fail me not.
Though care my life oft saddens And causeth tears to flow,
The light of Jesus gladdens And sweetens every woe.

[11]
Who clings with resolution To Him whom Satan hates
Must look for persecution; For him the burden waits
Of mockery, shame, and losses, Heaped on his blameless head;
A thousand plagues and crosses Will be his daily bread.

[12]
From me this is not hidden, Yet I am not afraid;
I leave my cares, as bidden, To whom my vows were paid.
Though life and limb it cost me And everything I won,
Unshaken shall I trust Thee And cleave to Thee alone.

[13]
Though earth be rent asunder, Thou'rt mine eternally;
Not fire nor sword nor thunder Shall sever me from Thee;
Not hunger, thirst, nor danger, Not pain nor poverty
Nor mighty princes' anger Shall ever hinder me.

[14]
No angel and no gladness, No throne, no pomp, no show,
No love, no hate, no sadness, No pain, no depth of woe,
No scheme of man's contrivance, However small or great,
Shall draw me from Thy guidance Nor from Thee separate.

[15]
My heart for joy is springing And can no more be sad,
'Tis full of mirth and singing, Sees naught but sunshine glad.
The Sun that cheers my spirit Is Jesus Christ, my King;
That which I shall inherit Makes me rejoice and sing.

songs.title: Immortal, Invisible, God Only Wise
songs.author: Walter Chalmers Smith (1824-1908)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Immortal, invisible, God only wise,
In light inaccessible hid from our eyes,
Most bless�d, most glorious, the Ancient of Days,
Almighty, victorious, Thy great Name we praise.

[2]
Unresting, unhasting, and silent as light,
Nor wanting, nor wasting, Thou rulest in might;
Thy justice, like mountains, high soaring above
Thy clouds, which are fountains of goodness and love.

[3]
To all, life Thou givest, to both great and small;
In all life Thou livest, the true life of all;
We blossom and flourish as leaves on the tree,
And wither and perish but naught changeth Thee.

[4]
Great Father of glory, pure Father of light,
Thine angels adore Thee, all veiling their sight;
But of Thy rich graces this grace, Lord, impart
Take the veil from our face, the vile from our heart.

[5]
All laud we would render; O help us to see
'Tis only the splendor of light hideth Thee,
And so let Thy glory, almighty, impart,
Through Christ in His story, Thy Christ to the heart.

songs.title: In His Temple Now Behold Him
songs.author: Henry John Pye (1825-1903), William Cooke (1821-1894)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
In His temple now behold Him,
See the long expected Lord;
Ancient prophets had foretold Him;
God has now fulfilled His word.

[1.2]
Now to praise Him, His redeem�d
Shall break forth with one accord.

[2.1]
In the arms of her who bore Him,
Virgin pure, behold Him lie,
While his ag�d saints adore Him
Ere in faith and hope they die.

[2.2]
Hallelujah! Hallelujah!
Lo, th'incarnate God most high.

[3.1]
Jesus, by Thy presentation,
Thou, who didst for us endure,
Make us see our great salvation,
Seal us with Thy promise sure.

[3.2]
And present us in Thy glory
To Thy Father, cleansed and pure.

[4.1]
Prince and Author of salvation,
Be Thy boundless love our theme!
Jesus, praise to Thee be given
By the world Thou didst redeem.

[4.2]
With the Father and the Spirit,
Lord of majesty supreme!

songs.title: In Peace and Joy I Now Depart
songs.author: Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. Leonard Woolsey Bacon (1830-1907))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
In peace and joy I now depart
At God's disposing;
For full of comfort is my heart,
Soft reposing.

[1.2]
So the Lord hath promised me,
And death is but a slumber.

[2.1]
'Tis Christ that wrought this work for me,
My faithful Savior,
Whom Thou hast made mine eyes to see
By Thy favor.

[2.2]
Now I know He is my Life,
My Help in need and dying.

[3.1]
Him Thou hast unto all set forth
Their great Salvation
And to His kingdom called the earth,
Every nation,

[3.2]
By Thy dear and wholesome Word,
In every place resounding.

[4.1]
He is the Hope and saving Light
Of lands benighted;
By Him are they who dwelt in night
Fed and lighted.

[4.2]
He is Israel's Praise and Bliss,
Their Joy, Reward, and Glory.

songs.title: In The Bleak MidWinter
songs.author: Christina Georgina Rossetti (1830-1894)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
In the bleak midwinter, frosty wind made moan,
Earth stood hard as iron, water like a stone;
Snow had fallen, snow on snow, snow on snow on snow,
In the bleak midwinter, long ago.

[2.1]
Our God,
Heav'n cannot hold Him, nor earth sustain;
Heav'n and earth shall flee away when He comes to reign.

[2.2]
In the bleak midwinter a stable place sufficed The Lord God Almighty,
Jesus Christ.

[3]
Enough for Him, whom cherubim, worship night and day,
Breastful of milk, and a mangerful of hay;
Enough for Him, whom angels fall down before,
Ox and ass and camel which adore.

[4]
Angels and archangels may have gathered there,
Cherubim and seraphim thronged the air;
But His mother only, in her maiden bliss,
Worshiped the beloved with a kiss.

[5.1]
What can I give Him, poor as I am?
If I were a shepherd,
I would bring a lamb;

[5.2]
If I were a Wise Man,
I would do my part;
Yet what can I give Him:
Give my heart.

songs.title: In These Our Days So Perilous
songs.author: Latin, Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. Richard Massie (1800-1887))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
In these our days so perilous,
Lord, peace in mercy send us;
No God but Thee can fight for us,

[1.2]
No God but Thee defend us;
Thou our only God and Savior.

songs.title: Isaiah, Mighty Seer, In Days of Old
songs.author: Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. composite)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Isaiah, mighty seer, in days of old
The Lord of all in Spirit did behold
High on a lofty throne, in splendor bright,
With flowing train that filled the Temple quite.

[1.2]
Above the throne were stately seraphim,
Six wings had they, these messengers of Him.

[1.3]
With twain they veiled their faces, as was meet,
With twain in reverent awe they hid their feet,
And with the other twain aloft they soared,
One to the other called and praised the Lord:

[1.4]
"Holy is God, the Lord of Sabaoth!
Holy is God, the Lord of Sabaoth!
Holy is God, the Lord of Sabaoth!
Behold, His glory filleth all the earth!"

[1.5]
The beams and lintels trembled at the cry,
And clouds of smoke enwrapped the throne on high.

songs.title: It Came Upon A Midnight Clear
songs.author: Edmund Hamilton Sears (1810-1876)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
It came upon the midnight clear,
That glorious song of old,
From angels bending near the earth,
To touch their harps of gold;

[1.2]
"Peace on the earth, good will to men,
From Heaven's all gracious King." The world in solemn stillness lay,
To hear the angels sing.

[2.1]
Still through the cloven skies they come With peaceful wings unfurled,
And still their heavenly music floats O'er all the weary world;

[2.2]
Above its sad and lowly plains,
They bend on hov'ring wing,
And ever over its Babel sounds The bless�d angels sing.

[3.1]
Yet with the woes of sin and strife
The world has suffered long;
Beneath the angel strain have rolled
Two thousand years of wrong;

[3.2]
And man, at war with man, hears not
The love- song which they bring;
O hush the noise, ye men of strife
And hear the angels sing.

[4.1]
And ye, beneath life's crushing load,
Whose forms are bending low,
Who toil along the climbing way
With painful steps and slow,

[4.2]
Look now! for glad and golden hours
Come swiftly on the wing.
O rest beside the weary road,
And hear the angels sing!

[5.1]
For lo! the days are hast'ning on,
By prophet- bards foretold,
When with the ever circling years
Comes round the age of gold;

[5.2]
When peace shall over all the earth
Its ancient splendors fling,
And the whole world send back the song
Which now the angels sing.

songs.title: It Is Well With My Soul
songs.author: Horatio Gates Spafford (1828-1888)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
When peace, like a river, attendeth my way,
When sorrows like sea billows roll;

[1.2]
Whatever my lot,
Thou has taught me to say,
It is well, it is well, with my soul.

[1.3]
It is well, with my soul,
It is well, it is well with my soul.
It is well, with my soul,

[2]
Though Satan should buffet, though trials should come,
Let this blest assurance control,
That Christ has regarded my helpless estate,
And hath shed His own blood for my soul.

[3.1]
My sin, oh, the bliss of this glorious thought!
My sin, not in part but the whole,
Is nailed to the cross, and I bear it no more,

[3.2]
Praise the Lord, praise the Lord,
O my soul!

[4.1]
For me, be it Christ, be it Christ hence to live:
If Jordan above me shall roll,

[4.2]
No pang shall be mine, for in death
As in life Thou wilt whisper Thy peace
To my soul.

[5.1]
But,
Lord, 'tis for Thee, for Thy coming we wait,
The sky, not the grave, is our goal;
Oh trump of the angel!

[5.2]
Oh voice of the Lord!
Bless�d hope, bless�d rest of my soul!

songs.title: Jerusalem the Golden
songs.author: Bernard of Cluny aka. Bernard of Morlaix (12th Century) (trad. John Mason Neale (1818-1866))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Jerusalem the golden,
With milk and honey blest,
Beneath thy contemplation
Sink heart and voice oppressed.

[1.2]
I know not, O I know not,
What joys await us there,
What radiancy of glory,
What bliss beyond compare.

[2.1]
They stand, those halls of Zion,
All jubilant with song,
And bright with many'an angel,
And all the martyr throng;

[2.2]
The Prince is ever in them,
The daylight is serene.
The pastures of the bless�d
Are decked in glorious sheen.

[3.1]
There is the throne of David,
And there, from care released,
The shout of them that triumph,
The song of them that feast;

[3.2]
And they are with their Leader,
Who conquered in the fight,
And won for them forever
Their gleaming robes of white.

[4.1]
O sweet and bless�d country,
The home of God's elect!
O sweet and bless�d country,
That eager hearts expect!

[4.2]
Jesus, in mercy bring us
To that dear land of rest,
Who art, with God the Father,
And Spirit, ever blessed.

[5.1]
Brief life is here our portion,
Brief sorrow, short lived care;
The life that knows no ending,
The tearless life, is there.

[5.2]
O happy retribution!
Short toil, eternal rest;
For mortals and for sinners,
A mansion with the blest.

[6]
That we should look, poor wanderers, to have our home on high!
That worms should seek for dwellings beyond the starry sky!
And now we fight the battle, but then shall wear the crown
Of full and everlasting, and passionless renown.

[7]
And how we watch and struggle, and now we live in hope,
And Zion in her anguish with Babylon must cope;
But he whom now we trust in shall then be seen and known,
And they that know and see Him shall have Him for their own.

[8]
For thee, O dear, dear country, mine eyes their vigils keep;
For very love, beholding, thy happy name, they weep:
The mention of thy glory is unction to the breast,
And medicine in sickness, and love, and life, and rest.

[9]
O one, O only mansion! O paradise of joy!
Where tears are ever banished, and smiles have no alloy;
The cross is all thy splendor, the Crucified thy praise,
His laud and benediction thy ransomed people raise.

[10]
Jerusalem the glorious! Glory of the elect!
O dear and future vision that eager hearts expect!
E'en now by faith I see thee, e'en here thy walls discern;
To thee my thoughts are kindled, and strive, and pant, and yearn.

[11]
Jerusalem, the only, that look'st from heaven below,
In thee is all my glory, in me is all my woe!
And though my body may not, my spirit seeks thee fain,
Till flesh and earth return me to earth and flesh again.

[12]
Jerusalem, exulting on that securest shore,
I hope thee, wish thee, sing thee, and love thee evermore!
I ask not for my merit: I seek not to deny
My merit is destruction, a child of wrath am I.

[13]
But yet with faith I venture and hope upon the way,
For those perennial guerdons I labor night and day.
The best and dearest Father Who made me, and Who saved,
Bore with me in defilement, and from defilement laved.

[14]
When in His strength I struggle, for very joy I leap;
When in my sin I totter, I weep, or try to weep:
And grace, sweet grace celestial, shall all its love display,
And David's royal fountain purge every stain away.

[15]
O sweet and bless�d country, shall I e'er see thy face?
O sweet and bless�d country, shall I e'er win thy grace?
I have the hope within me to comfort and to bless!
O shall I e'er win the prize? O tell me, tell me, Yes!

songs.title: Jesus Came, the Heavens Adoring
songs.author: Godfrey Thring (1823-1903)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Jesus came, the heav'ns adoring,
Came with peace from realms on high;
Jesus came for man's redemption,
Lowly came on earth to die.

[1.2]
Alleluia! Alleluia!
Came in deep humility.

[2.1]
Jesus comes again in mercy,
When our hearts are bowed with care;
Jesus comes again in answer
To an earnest, heartfelt prayer;

[2.2]
Alleluia! Alleluia!
Comes to save us from despair.

[3.1]
Jesus comes to hearts rejoicing,
Bringing news of sins forgiv'n;
Jesus comes in sounds of gladness,
Leading souls redeemed to Heav'n;

[3.2]
Alleluia! Alleluia!
Now the gate of death is riv'n.

[4.1]
Jesus comes in joy and sorrow,
Shares alike our hopes and fears;
Jesus comes, whate'er befalls us,
Glads our hearts, and dries our tears;

[4.2]
Alleluia! Alleluia!
Cheering e'en our failing years.

[5.1]
Jesus comes on clouds triumphant,
When the heav'ns shall pass away;
Jesus comes again in glory;

[5.2]
Let us then our homage pay,
Alleluia! Alleluia!
Till the dawn of endless day.

songs.title: Jesus Christ Is Risen Today
songs.author: Bohemian, Charles Wesley (1707-1788) (trad. John Arnold)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Jesus Christ is ris'n today,
Alleluia!
Our triumphant holy day,
Alleluia!

[1.2]
Who did once, upon the cross,
Alleluia!
Suffer to redeem our loss,
Alleluia!

[2.1]
Hymns of praise then let us sing,
Alleluia!
Unto Christ, our heav'nly King,
Alleluia!

[2.2]
Who endured the cross and grave,
Alleluia!
Sinners to redeem and save,
Alleluia!

[3.1]
But the pain which He endured,
Alleluia!
Our salvation hath procured,
Alleluia!

[3.2]
Now above the sky He's king,
Alleluia!
Where the angels ever sing,
Alleluia!

[4.1]
Sing we to our God above,
Alleluia!
Praise eternal as His love,
Alleluia!

[4.2]
Praise Him, all you heav'nly host,
Alleluia!

[4.3]
Father,
Son, and Holy Ghost,
Alleluia!

songs.title: Jesus Christ Who Came to Save
songs.author: Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. Leonard Woolsey Bacon (1830-1907))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Jesus Christ, who came to save,
And overcame the grave,
Is now arisen,

[1.2]
And sin hath bound in prison.
Kyri' eleison.

[2]
Who withouten sin was found,
Bore our transgression's wound.
He is our Savior,
And brings us to God's favor.

[3]
Life and mercy, sin and death,
All in His hands He hath;
Them He'll deliver,
Who trust in Him forever.

songs.title: Jesus Christ, Our Blessed Savior
songs.author: John Hus (1369-1415), Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. Richard Massie (1800-1887), unknown)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Jesus Christ, our Blessed Savior,
Turned away God's wrath forever;
Suff'ring pains no tongue can tell,
He saved us from the pains of hell.

[2]
To remind us that, to save us
He hath died, His flesh He gave us
With this bread, a quick'ning food,
And with this wine, His precious blood.

[3]
Whoso to this board repaireth,
Take good heed how He prepareth;
Death instead of life shall He
Receive who comes unworthily.

[4]
Praise the Father, God in heaven,
Who such dainty food hath given,
And for misdeeds thou hast done
Gave to die His beloved Son.

[5]
Thou shalt hold with faith unshaken,
That this food is to be taken
By the sick who are distressed,
By those whose heart is sin- oppressed.

[6]
To such grace and mercy turneth
Every soul that truly mourneth;
Art thou well? Avoid this board,
Else thou reapest an ill reward.

[7]
Christ says: "Come ye heavy-laden,
I your weary hearts will gladden;
They that are yet strong  and well,
Despise the best physician's skill.

[8]
Couldst thou earn thine own salvation,
Useless were my death and passion;
This feast is not spread for thee,
If thine own helper thou wilt be.

[9]
If thou this believest truly,
And confession makest duly,
Thou a welcome guest art here,
This heavenly food thy soul shall cheer.

[10]
But the fruits must not be missing,
Love thy neighbor without ceasing,
That true love let him receive,
Which here to thee thy God doth give.

songs.title: Jesus Grant That Balm and Healing
songs.author: Johann Heermann (1585-1647) (trad. composite)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Jesus, grant that balm and healing
In Thy holy wounds I find,
Every hour that I am feeling,
Pains of body and of mind.

[1.2]
Should some evil thought within
Tempt my treacherous heart to sin,
Show the peril, and from sinning
Keep me ere its first beginning.

[2.1]
Should some lust or sharp temptation
Prove too strong for flesh and blood,
Let me think upon Thy Passion,
And the breach is soon made good.

[2.2]
Or should Satan press me hard,
Let me then be on my guard,
Saying, "Christ for me was wounded,"
That the tempter flee confounded.

[3.1]
If the world my heart entices
On the broad and easy road
With its mirth and luring vices,

[3.2]
Let me think upon the load
Thou didst carry and endure
That I flee all thoughts impure,

[3.3]
Banishing each wild emotion,
Calm and blest in my devotion.

[4.1]
Every wound that pains or grieves me,
By Thy stripes, Lord, is made whole;
When I'm faint, Thy cross revives me,
Granting new life to my soul.

[4.2]
Yea, Thy comfort renders sweet
Every bitter cup I meet;
For Thy all atoning Passion
Has procured my soul's salvation.

[5.1]
O my God, my Rock and Tower,
Grant that in Thy death I trust,
Knowing death has lost his power
Since Thou trodd'st him in the dust.

[5.2]
Savior, let Thine agony
Ever help and comfort me;
When I die, be my Protection,
Light and Life and Resurrection.

[6]
Jesus, grant that balm and healing In Thy holy wounds I find,
Every hour that I am feeling, Pains of body and of mind.
And when I this world must leave, Grant that, Lord, to Thee I cleave,
In Thy wounds find consolation And obtain my soul's salvation

songs.title: Jesus Is All the World To Me
songs.author: Will Lamartine Thompson (1847-1909)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Jesus is all the world to me,
My life, my joy, my all;
He is my strength from day to day,
Without Him I would fall.

[1.2]
When I am sad, to Him I go,
No other one can cheer me so;
When I am sad, He makes me glad,
He's my friend.

[2.1]
Jesus is all the world to me,
My friend in trials sore;
I go to Him for blessings and
He gives them ov'r and o'er.

[2.2]
He sends the sunshine and the rain,
He sends the harvest's golden grain;
Sunshine and rain, harvest of grain,
He's my friend.

[3.1]
Jesus is all the world to me,
And true to Him I'll be;
O how could I this friend deny,
When He's so true to me?

[3.2]
Following Him I know I'm right,
He watches o'er me day and night;
Following Him, by day and night,
He's my friend.

[4.1]
Jesus is all the world to me,
I want no better friend;
I trust Him now, I'll trust Him when
Life's fleeting days shall end.

[4.2]
Beautiful life with such a friend;
Beautiful life that has no end;
Eternal life, eternal joy,
He's my friend.

songs.title: Jesus Loves Me
songs.author: Anna B. Warner (1827-1915)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Jesus loves me! This I know,
For the Bible tells me so.
Little ones to Him belong;
They are weak, but He is strong.

[1.2]
Yes, Jesus loves me! Yes, Jesus loves me!
Yes, Jesus loves me! The Bible tells me so.

[2]
Jesus loves me!
He who died Heaven's gate to open wide;
He will wash away my sin,
Let His little child come in.

[3]
Jesus loves me!
He will stay Close beside me all the way;
Thou hast bled and died for me,
I will henceforth live for Thee.

songs.title: Jesus Shall Reign
songs.author: Isaac Watts (1674-1748)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Jesus shall reign where'er the sun
Does his successive journeys run;
His kingdom stretch from shore to shore
Till moons shall wax and wane no more.

[2]
For Him shall endless prayer be made,
And praises throng to crown His head;
His Name, like sweet perfume shall rise
With every morning sacrifice.

[3]
People and realms of every tongue
Dwell on His love with sweetest song;
And infant voices shall proclaim
Their early blessings on His Name.

[4]
Blessings abound where'er He reigns;
The prisoner leaps to lose his chains,
The weary find eternal rest,
And all the sons of want are blest.

[5]
Where He displays His healing power
Death and the curse are known no more;
In Him the tribes of Adam boast
More blessings than their father lost.

[6]
Let every creature rise and bring
Peculiar honors to our King,
Angels descend with songs again,
And earth repeat the loud Amen.

songs.title: Jesus Sinners Doth Receive
songs.author: Erdmann Neumeister (1671-1756) (trad. Henry Mills (1786-1867))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Jesus sinners doth receive;
Well may we this saying ponder
Who in sin's delusions live,
And from God and Heaven wander:

[1.2]
Here is hope for all who grieve-
Jesus sinners doth receive.

[2.1]
We deserve but grief and shame,-
Yet His words, rich grace revealing,
Pardon, peace, and life proclaim;

[2.2]
Here their ills have perfect healing
Who with humble hearts believe-
Jesus sinners doth receive.

[3.1]
As the shepherd seeks to find
His lost sheep that from Him strayeth,
So hath Christ each soul in mind,
And for its salvation prayeth;

[3.2]
Fain He'd have each wand'rer live:
Jesus sinners doth receive.

[4.1]
Come, then, all by guilt oppressed,
Jesus calls, and He would make you
God's own children, pure and blest,
And to glory He would take you;

[4.2]
Think on this, and well believe
Jesus sinners doth receive.

[5.1]
Savior, now I come to Thee:
Great my sins, a weary burden!
Wilt Thou mercy show to me?
Can I hope to find a pardon?

[5.2]
I will trust: my soul relieve!
Me, a sinner, Lord, receive!

[6]
Rich Thy mercy\- strangely good!  O how oft have I offended!
But through Thy redeeming blood All my fear of wrath is ended:
Yes I now can witness give: Jesus sinners doth receive!

[7]
Now my conscience is at peace; From the Law I stand acquitted;
Christ hath purchased my release, And my every sin remitted.
Naught remains my soul to grieve: Jesus sinners doth receive.

[8]
Jesus sinners doth receive! Happy in His ceaseless favor,
Here for Heaven I will live, There shall live with Him forever,
"Joy in death these tidings give; Jesus sinners doth receive!"

songs.title: Jesus Wants All Of His Children
songs.author: Mrs. James W. Wood, Brian James Dumont (1971-)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Jesus wants all of His children
To be good and true;
He will help if we but ask Him,
Help us gladly too.

[2]
Jesus was so meek and lowly,
As a little child.
We will try to be like Jesus,
Gentle, patient, mild.

[3]
Jesus wants us to be loving,
Helping when we may.
We will try to be kindhearted,
Merciful each day.

[4]
"Blessed are the pure in heart," thus the Savior taught.
Clean in mind, in soul, in body, pure in every thought.

[5]
When we find our friends are angry,
We will to them say,
"Jesus wants you to be loving,
Each and every day."

[6]
When I know that I have done wrong, to Jesus I flee.
He has paid for all transgressions, He has paid for me!

[7]
Jesus knew that we would fail Him so He came to be
Life to all the poor and lost ones, life eternally!

songs.title: Jesus, In Thy Dying Woes
songs.author: Thomas Benson Pollock (1836-1896)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Jesus, in Thy dying woes,
Even while Thy lifeblood flows,
Craving pardon for Thy foes;
Hear us, holy Jesus.

[2]
Savior, for our pardon sue,
When our sins Thy pangs renew,
For we know not what we do:
Hear us, holy Jesus.

[3]
O may we, who mercy need,
Be like Thee in heart and deed,
When with wrong our spirits bleed:
Hear us, holy Jesus.

songs.title: Jesus, King of Glory
songs.author: W. Hope Davison (1827-1894)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Jesus, King of glory,
Throned above the sky,
Jesus, tender Savior,
Hear Thy children cry.

[1.2]
Pardon our transgressions,
Cleanse us from our sin,
By Thy Spirit help us
Heav'nly life to win.

[1.3]
Jesus, King of glory,
Throned above the sky,
Jesus, tender Savior,
Hear Thy children cry.

[2.1]
On this day of gladness,
Bending low the knee In thine earthly temple,
Lord, we worship thee;

[2.2]
Celebrate thy goodness,
Mercy, grace, and truth,
All thy loving guidance Of our heedless youth.

[3]
For the little children Who have come to thee;
For the glad, bright spirits Who thy glory see;
For the loved ones resting In thy dear embrace;
For the pure and holy Who behold thy face,

[4]
Help us ever steadfast in the faith to be:
In Thy Church's conflicts fighting valiantly.
Loving Savior, strengthen these weak hearts of ours,
Through Thy cross to conquer crafty evil powers.

[5.1]
When the shadows lengthen, show us,
Lord,
Thy way;
Through the darkness lead us to the heav'nly day;

[5.2]
When our course is finished, ended all the strife,
Grant us, with the faithful, palms and crowns of life.

[6]
For thy faithful servants Who have entered in;
For thy fearless soldiers Who have conquered sin;
For the countless legions Who have followed thee,
Heedless of the danger, On to victory,

songs.title: Jesus, Tender Shepherd, Hear Me
songs.author: Mary Lundie Duncan (1814-1840)

songs.title: Jesus, Thy Boundless Love To Me
songs.author: Paul Gerhardt (1607-1676) (trad. John Wesley (1703-1791))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Jesus, Thy boundless love to me
No thought can reach, no tongue declare;
Unite my thankful heart with Thee
And reign without a rival there.

[1.2]
To Thee alone, dear Lord, I live;
Myself to Thee, dear Lord, I give.

[2.1]
O, grant that nothing in my soul
May dwell but Thy pure love alone!
Oh, may Thy love possess me whole,
My joy, my treasure, and my crown!

[2.2]
All coldness from my heart remove;
My every act, word, thought, be love.

[3.1]
O love, how cheering is thy ray!
All pain before thy presence flies;
Care, anguish, sorrow, melt away
Where'er thy healing beams arise.

[3.2]
O Jesus, nothing may I see,
Nothing desire or seek, but Thee!

[4.1]
This love unwearied I pursue
And dauntlessly to Thee aspire.
Oh, may Thy love my hope renew
Burn in my soul like heav'nly fire!

[4.2]
And day and night be all my care
To guard this sacred treasure there.

[5.1]
My Savior, Thou Thy love to me
In shame, in want, in pain, hast showed;
For me, on the accursed tree,
Thou pourest forth Thy guiltless blood;

[5.2]
Thy wounds upon my heart impress,
Nor aught shall the lov'd stamp efface.

songs.title: Joy to the World
songs.author: Isaac Watts (1674-1748)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Joy to the world, the Lord is come!
Let earth receive her King;

[1.2]
Let ev'ry heart prepare Him room,
And Heav'n and nature sing,
And Heav'n and nature sing,
And Heav'n, and Heav'n, and nature sing.

[2.1]
Joy to the earth, the Savior reigns!
Let men their songs employ;

[2.2]
While fields and floods, rocks, hills and plains
Repeat the sounding joy,
Repeat the sounding joy,
Repeat, repeat, the sounding joy.

[3.1]
No more let sins and sorrows grow,
Nor thorns infest the ground;

[3.2]
He comes to make His blessings flow
Far as the curse is found,
Far as the curse is found,
Far as, far as, the curse is found.

[4.1]
He rules the world with truth and grace,
And makes the nations prove
The glories of His righteousness,
And wonders of His love,

[4.2]
And wonders of His love,
And wonders, wonders, of His love.

songs.title: Joyful, Joyful, We Adore Thee
songs.author: Henry Jackson van Dyke (1852-1933)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Joyful, joyful, we adore Thee,
God of glory, Lord of love;
Hearts unfold like flowers before Thee,
Opening to the sun above.

[1.2]
Melt the clouds of sin and sadness;
Drive the dark of doubt away;
Giver of immortal gladness,
Fill us with the light of day!

[2.1]
All Thy works with joy surround Thee,
Earth and heaven reflect Thy rays,
Stars and angels sing around Thee,
Center of unbroken praise.

[2.2]
Field and forest, vale and mountain,
Flowery meadow, flashing sea,
Singing bird and flowing fountain
Call us to rejoice in Thee.

[3.1]
Thou art giving and forgiving,
Ever blessing, ever blessed,
Wellspring of the joy of living,
Ocean depth of happy rest!

[3.2]
Thou our Father, Christ our Brother,
All who live in love are Thine;
Teach us how to love each other,
Lift us to the joy divine.

[4.1]
Mortals, join the happy chorus,
Which the morning stars began;
Father love is reigning o'er us,
Brother love binds man to man.

[4.2]
Ever singing, march we onward,
Victors in the midst of strife,
Joyful music leads us Sunward
In the triumph song of life.

songs.title: Lamp of Our Feet
songs.author: Bernard Barton (1784-1849)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Lamp of our feet! whereby we trace
Our path, when wont to stray;
Stream from the fount of heav'nly grace!
Brook by the trav'ler's way!

[2]
Bread of our souls! whereon we feed;
True manna from on high!
Our guide, and chart wherein we read
Of realms beyond the sky.

[3]
Pillar of fire- through watches dark!
Or radiant cloud by day!
When waves would whelm our tossing bark-
Our anchor and our stay!

[4]
Pole- star on life's tempestuous deep!
Beacon! when doubts surround;
Compass! by which our course we keep;
Our deep sea- lead, to sound!

[5]
Riches in poverty! our aid
In every needful hour!
Unshaken rock! the pilgrim's shade;
The soldier's fortress tow'r.

[6]
Our shield and buckler in the fight!
Vict'ry's triumphant palm!
Comfort in grief! in weakness, might!
In sickness, Gilead's balm.

[7]
Childhood's preceptor! manhood's trust!
Old age's firm ally!
Our hope\-when we go down to dust,
Of immortality.

[8]
Pure oracles of truth divine!
Unlike each fabled dream
Given forth from Delphos' mystic shrine
Or groves of Academe!

[9]
Word of the ever-living God!
Will of His glorious Son!
Without Thee, how could earth be trod?
Or Heaven itself be won?

[10]
Yet to unfold thy hidden worth,
Thy mysteries to reveal,
That Spirit which first gave thee forth,
Thy volume must unseal!

[11]
And we, if we aright would learn
The wisdom it imparts,
Must to its heavenly teaching turn
With simple, child-like hearts!

songs.title: Let All Mortal Flesh Keep Silence
songs.author: from Liturgy of St. James (trad. Gerard Moultrie (1829-1885))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Let all mortal flesh keep silence,
And with fear and trembling stand;

[1.2]
Ponder nothing earthly minded,
For with blessing in His hand,
Christ our God to earth descendeth,
Our full homage to demand.

[2.1]
King of kings, yet born of Mary,
As of old on earth He stood,
Lord of lords, in human vesture,
In the body and the blood;

[2.2]
He will give to all the faithful
His own self for heav'nly food.

[3.1]
Rank on rank the host of heaven
Spreads its vanguard on the way,
As the Light of light descendeth
From the realms of endless day,

[3.2]
That the pow'rs of hell may vanish
As the darkness clears away.

[4.1]
At His feet the six wing�d seraph,
Cherubim with sleepless eye,
Veil their faces to the presence,
As with ceaseless voice they cry:

[4.2]
Alleluia, Alleluia
Alleluia, Lord Most High!

songs.title: Let Children Hear The Mighty Deeds
songs.author: Isaac Watts (1674-1748)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Let children hear the mighty deeds
Which God performed of old;
Which in our younger years we saw,
And which our fathers told.

[2]
He bids us make His glories known,
His works of pow'r and grace;
And we'll convey His wonders down
Through every rising race.

[3]
Our lips shall tell them to our sons,
And they again to theirs;
That generations yet unborn
May teach them to their heirs.

[4]
Thus shall they learn in God alone
Their hope securely stands,
That they may ne'er forget His work
But practice His commands.

songs.title: Let Our Gladness Have No End
songs.author: Tobias Zavorka (trad. unknown)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Let our gladness have no end,
Hallelujah!
For to earth did Christ descend.
Hallelujah!

[1.2]
On this day God gave us Christ,
His Son, to save us;
Christ,
His Son, to save us.

[2]
See, the loveliest blooming rose,
Hallelujah!
From the branch of Jesse grows.
Hallelujah!

[3]
Into flesh is made the Word.
Hallelujah!
He, our refuge and our Lord.
Hallelujah!

songs.title: Lift High The Cross
songs.author: George William Kitchin (1827-1912), Michael Robert Newbolt (1874-1956)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Lift high the cross, the love of Christ proclaim,
Till all the world adore His sacred Name.
Come, brethren, follow where our Captain trod,
Our King victorious, Christ the Son of God.

[2]
Led on their way by this triumphant sign,
The hosts of God in conquering ranks combine.

[3]
Each newborn servant of the Crucified Bears on
