The brow the seal of Him Who died.

[4]
This is the sign which Satan's legions fear
And angels veil their faces to revere.

[5]
Saved by this Cross whereon their Lord was
Slain, the sons of Adam their lost home
Regain.

songs.title: Lift Up Your Heads, Ye Mighty Gates
songs.author: Georg Weissel (1590-1635) (trad. Catherine Winkworth (1827-1878))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Lift up your heads, ye mighty gates!
Behold, the King of glory waits;
The King of kings is drawing near,
The Savior of the world is here;

[1.2]
Life and salvation doth He bring,
Wherefore rejoice and gladly sing:
We praise Thee, Father, now!
Creator, wise art Thou!

[2.1]
The Lord is just, a Helper tried,
Mercy is ever at His side,
His kingly crown is holiness,
His scepter, pity in distress,

[2.2]
The end of all our woe He brings;
Wherefore the earth is glad and sings:
We praise Thee, Savior, now!
Mighty in deed art Thou!

[3.1]
O blest the land, the city blest,
Where Christ the Ruler is confessed!
O happy hearts and happy homes
To whom this King in triumph comes!

[3.2]
The cloudless Sun of joy He is,
Who bringeth pure delight and bliss.
O Comforter divine,
What boundless grace is Thine!

[4.1]
Fling wide the portals of your heart;
Make it a temple, set apart
From earthly use for heav'ns employ,
Adorned with prayer and love and joy;

[4.2]
So shall your Sovereign enter in,
And new and nobler life begin;
To Thee, O God, be praise,
For Word, and deed, and grace!

[5.1]
Redeemer, come! I open wide
My heart to Thee; here, Lord, abide!
Let me Thy inner presence feel,
Thy grace and love in me reveal.

[5.2]
Thy Holy Spirit guide us on,
Until our glorious goal be won!
Eternal praise and fame
We offer to Thy Name.

songs.title: Lo, God To Heav'n Ascendeth
songs.author: Gottfried Wilhelm Sacer (1635-1699) (trad. Frances Elizabeth Cox (1812-1897))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Lo, God to Heav'n ascendeth!
Throughout its regions vast
With shouts triumphant blendeth
The trumpet's thrilling blast:

[1.2]
Sing praise to Christ the Lord;
Sing praise with exultation,
King of each heathen nation,
The God of Hosts adored!

[2.1]
With joy is Heav'n resounding
Christ's glad return to see;
Behold the saints surrounding
The Lord who set them free.

[2.2]
Bright myriads, thronging, come;
The cherub band rejoices,
And loud seraphic voices
Welcome Messiah home.

[3.1]
No more the way is hidden,
Since Christ our Head arose:
No more to man forbidden
The road to Heav'n that goes.

[3.2]
Our Lord is gone before;
Yet here He will not leave us,
And soon in Heav'n receive us
And open wide the door.

[4.1]
Christ is our place preparing;
To Heav'n we, too, shall rise,
And, joys angelic sharing,
Be where our treasure lies:

[4.2]
There may each heart be found!
Where Jesus Christ has entered,
There let our Hope be centered;
Our course still heav'nward bound.

[5.1]
May we, His servants, thither
In heart and mind ascend,
And let us sing together:

[5.2]
"We seek Thee, Christ, our friend,
Thee, God's exalted Son,
Our Life, and Way to Heaven,

[5.3]
To whom all pow'r is given,
Our Joy and Hope and Crown."

songs.title: Lo, How A Rose E'er Blooming
songs.author: German, Fridrich Layriz (1808-1859) (trad. Theodore Baker (1851-1934), Harriet Reynolds Krauth (1845-1925), Harriet Reynolds Spaeth (1845-1925), John Casper Mattes (1876-1948))
songs.composer: K�ln, 1599 from Altes Catholische Geistliche Kirchengeseng
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Lo, how a Rose e'er blooming
From tender stem hath sprung!
Of Jesse's lineage coming,
As men of old have sung.

[1.2]
It came, a flow'ret bright,
Amid the cold of winter,
When half spent was the night.

[2.1]
Isaiah 'twas foretold it,
The Rose I have in mind;
With Mary we behold it,
The virgin mother kind.

[2.2]
To show God's love aright,
She bore to men a Savior,
When half spent was the night.

[3.1]
The shepherds heard the story
Proclaimed by angels bright,
How Christ, the Lord of glory
Was born on earth this night.

[3.2]
To Bethlehem they sped
And in the manger found Him,
As angel heralds said.

[4.1]
This Flow'r, whose fragrance tender
With sweetness fills the air,
Dispels with glorious splendor
The darkness everywhere;

[4.2]
True Man, yet very God,
From sin and death He saves us,
And lightens ev'ry load.

[5.1]
O Savior, Child of Mary,
Who felt our human woe,
O Savior, King of glory,
Who dost our weakness know;

[5.2]
Bring us at length we pray,
To the bright courts of Heaven,
And to the endless day!

songs.title: Lo! He Comes With Clouds Descending
songs.author: John Cennick (1718-1755), Charles Wesley (1707-1788)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Lo! He comes with clouds descending,
Once for ev'ry sinner slain;
Thousand thousand saints attending,
Swell the triumph of His train:

[1.2]
Hallelujah! Hallelujah! Hallelujah!
God appears on earth to reign.

[2.1]
Ev'ry eye shall now behold Him
Robed in dreadful majesty;

[2.2]
Those who set at naught and sold Him,
Pierced and nailed Him to the tree,
Deeply wailing, deeply wailing, deeply wailing,
Shall the true Messiah see.

[3.1]
Ev'ry island, sea, and mountain,
Heav'n and earth, shall flee away;
All who hate Him must, confounded,
Hear the trump proclaim the day:

[3.2]
Come to judgment! Come to judgment! Come to judgment!
Come to judgment! Come away!

[4.1]
Now redemption, long expected,
See in solemn pomp appear;
All His saints, by man rejected,
Now shall meet Him in the air:

[4.2]
Hallelujah! Hallelujah! Hallelujah!
See the day of God appear!

[5.1]
Answer Thine own bride and Spirit,
Hasten, Lord, the gen'ral doom!
The new Heav'n and earth inherit,
Take Thy pining exiles home:

[5.2]
All creation, all creation, all creation,
Travails! groans! and bids Thee come!

songs.title: Look Down, O Lord, From Heaven Behold
songs.author: Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. Frances Elizabeth Cox (1812-1897))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Look down, O Lord, from heav'n behold,
And let thy pity waken!
How few the flock within thy fold,
Neglected and forsaken!

[1.2]
Almost thou'lt seek for faith in vain,
And those who should thy truth maintain
Thy Word from us have taken.

[2.1]
With frauds which they themselves invent
Thy truth they have confounded;
Their hearts are not with one consent
On thy pure doctrine grounded;

[2.2]
And, whilst they gleam with outward show,
They lead thy people to and fro,
In error's maze astounded.

[3.1]
God surely will uproot all those
With vain deceits who store us,
With haughty tongue who God oppose,
And say, "Who'll stand before us?

[3.2]
By right or might we will prevail;
What we determine cannot fail,
For who can lord it o'er us?"

[4.1]
For this, saith God, I will arise,
These wolves my flock are rending;
I've heard my people's bitter sighs
To heav'n my throne ascending:

[4.2]
Now will I up, and set at rest
Each weary soul by fraud opprest,
The poor with might defending.

[5.1]
The silver sev'n times tried is pure
From all adulteration;
So, through God's word, shall men endure
Each trial and temptation:

[5.2]
Its worth gleams brighter through the cross,
And, purified from human dross,
It shines through every nation.

[6]
Thy truth thou wilt preserve, O Lord, From this vile generation;
Make us to lean upon thy word, With calm anticipation.
The wicked walk on every side When, 'mid thy flock, the vile abide In pow'r and exaltation.

songs.title: Lord Jesus Think On Me
songs.author: Synesius of Cyrene (375-430) (trad. Allen William Chatfield (1808-1896))
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Lord Jesus, think on me
And purge away my sin;
From earthborn passions set me free
And make me pure within.

[2]
Lord Jesus, think on me,
With many'a care oppressed;
Let me Thy loving servant be
And taste Thy promised rest.

[3]
Lord Jesus, think on me
Amid the battle's strife;
In all my pain and misery
Be Thou my Health and Life.

[4]
Lord Jesus, think on me
Nor let me go astray;
Through darkness and perplexity
Point Thou the heav'nly way.

[5]
Lord Jesus, think on me
When floods the tempest high;
When on doth rush the enemy,
O Savior, be Thou nigh!

[6]
Lord Jesus, think on me
That, when the flood is past,
I may th'eternal brightness see
And share Thy joy at last.

[7]
Lord Jesus, think on me
That I may sing above
To Father, Spirit, and to Thee
The strains of praise and love.

songs.title: Lord of Glory, Who Hast Bought Us
songs.author: Eliza Sibbald Dykes Alderson (1818-1889)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Lord of Glory, who hast bought us
With Thy lifeblood as the price,
Never grudging for the lost ones
That tremendous sacrifice;

[1.2]
And with that hast freely given
Blessings countless as the sand,
To th'unthankful and the evil
With Thine own unsparing hand.

[2.1]
Grant us hearts, dear Lord, to yield Thee
Gladly, freely, of Thine own.
With the sunshine of Thy goodness
Melt our thankless hearts of stone.

[2.2]
Till our cold and selfish natures,
Warmed by Thee, at length believe
That more happy and more blessed
'Tis to give than to receive.

[3.1]
Wondrous honor hast Thou given
To our humblest charity.
In Thine own mysterious sentence,
"Ye have done it unto Me."

[3.2]
Can it be, O gracious Master,
Thou dost deign for alms to sue,
Saying by Thy poor and needy,
"Give as I have given you"

[4.1]
Lord of Glory, who hast bought us
With Thy lifeblood as the price,
Never grudging for the lost ones
That tremendous sacrifice;

[4.2]
Give us faith, to trust Thee boldly;
Hope, to stay our souls on Thee;
But O, best of all Thy graces,
Give us Thine own charity.

songs.title: Lord of Life, All Praise Excelling
songs.author: Clement Clarke Moore (1779-1863)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Lord of life, all praise excelling,
Thou, in glory unconfined,
Deignst to make Thy humble dwelling
With the poor of humble mind.

[1.2]
As Thy love, through all creation,
Beams like Thy diffusive light;
So the high and humble station
Both are equal in Thy sight.

[2.1]
Thus Thy care, for all providing,
Warmed Thy faithful prophet's tongue;
Who, the lot of all deciding,
To Thy chosen Israel sung.

[2.2]
When Thy harvest yields Thee pleasure,
Thou the golden sheaf shalt bind;
To the poor belongs the treasure
Of the scattered ears behind.

[3.1]
Still we read Thy Word declaring
Mercy, Lord, Thine own decree;
Mercy ev'ry sorrow sharing,
Warms the heart resembling Thee.

[3.2]
Still the orphan and the stranger,
Still the widow owns Thy care;
Screened by Thee in ev'ry danger,
Heard by Thee in ev'ry prayer.

songs.title: Lord Of Our Life
songs.author: Matth�us Apelles von L�wenstern (1594-1648) (trad. Philip Pusey (1799-1855))
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Lord of our life, and God of our salvation,
Star of our night, and Hope of every nation,
Hear and receive Thy church's supplication,
Lord God Almighty.

[2]
See round Thine Ark the hungry billows curling!
See how Thy foes their banners are unfurling!
Lord, while their darts envenomed they are hurling,
Thou canst preserve us.

[3]
Lord, Thou canst help when earthly armor faileth;
Lord, Thou canst save when sin itself assaileth;
Lord, o'er Thy Rock nor death nor hell prevaileth;
Grant us Thy peace, Lord.

[4]
Peace, in our hearts, our evil thoughts assuaging,
Peace, in Thy Church, where brothers are engaging,
Peace, when the world its busy war is waging;
Calm Thy foes raging!

[5]
Grant us Thy help till backward they are driven;
Grant them Thy Truth, that they may be forgiven;
Grant peace on earth, and after we have striven,
Peace in Thy Heaven.

songs.title: Lord Who Throughout These Forty Days
songs.author: Claudia Frances Ibotson Hernaman (1838-1898)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Lord, who throughout these forty days
For us didst fast and pray,
Teach us with Thee to mourn our sins
And close by Thee to stay.

[2]
As Thou with Satan didst contend,
And didst the vict'ry win,
O give us strength in Thee to fight,
In Thee to conquer sin.

[3]
As Thou didst hunger bear, and thirst,
So teach us, gracious Lord,
To die to self, and chiefly live
By Thy most holy Word.

[4]
And through these days of penitence,
And through Thy passiontide,
Yea, evermore in life and death,
Jesus, with us abide.

[5]
Abide with us, that so, this life
Of suff'ring over past,
An Easter of unending joy
We may attain at last.

songs.title: Lord, Dismiss Us With Thy Blessing
songs.author: John Fawcett (1740-1817), Godfrey Thring (1823-1903)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Lord, dismiss us with Thy blessing;
Fill our hearts with joy and peace;
Let us each Thy love possessing,
Triumph in redeeming grace.

[1.2]
O refresh us, O refresh us,
Trav'ling through this wilderness.

[2.1]
Thanks we give and adoration
For Thy Gospel's joyful sound;
May the fruits of Thy salvation
In our hearts and lives abound.

[2.2]
Ever faithful, ever faithful,
To the truth may we be found.

[3.1]
So that when Thy love shall call us,
Savior, from the world away,
Fear of death shall not appall us,
Glad Thy summons to obey.

[3.2]
May we ever, may we ever,
Reign with Thee in endless day.

songs.title: Lord, Enthroned in Heavenly Splendor
songs.author: George Hugh Bourne (1840-1925)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Lord, enthroned in heav'nly splendor,
First begotten from the dead,
You alone, our strong Defender,
Now lift up Your people's head.

[1.2]
Alleluia!
Alleluia!
Alleluia!

[1.3]
Jesus, true and living Bread!
Jesus, true and living Bread!

[2.1]
Here our humblest homage pay we,
Here in loving reference bow;
Here for faith's discernment pray we,
Lest we fail to know You now.

[2.2]
Thou art here, we ask not how.
Thou art here, we ask not how.

[3.1]
Though the lowliest form doth veil Thee As of old in Bethlehem,
Here as there Thine angels hail Thee,
Branch and Flow'r of Jesse's stem.

[3.2]
We in worship join with them.
We in worship join with them.

[4.1]
Paschal Lamb,
Your offering finished Once for all when You were slain,
In its fullness undiminished Shall forevermore remain.

[4.2]
Cleansing souls from every stain.
Cleansing souls from every stain.

[5.1]
Great High Priest of our profession,
Through the veil Thou wentest in,
By Thy mighty intercession,
Grace and peace for us to win.

[5.2]
Jesus, true and living Bread!
Jesus, true and living Bread!

[6.1]
Life imparting heavenly Manna,
Smitten Rock with streaming side,
Heaven and earth with loud hosanna
Worship You, the Lamb Who died.

[6.2]
Alleluia! Alleluia! Alleluia!
Risen, Ascended, Glorified!

songs.title: Lord, Keep Us Steadfast in Thy Word
songs.author: Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. Catherine Winkworth (1827-1878))
songs.composer: Wittenberg, 1543 from Klug's Geistliche Lieder auffs new gebessert
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Lord, keep us steadfast in Thy Word;
Curb those who fain by craft and sword
Would wrest the kingdom from Thy Son
And set at naught all He hath done.

[2]
Lord Jesus Christ, Thy pow'r make known,
For Thou art Lord of lords alone;
Defend Thy Christendom that we
May evermore sing praise to Thee.

[3]
O Comforter of priceless worth,
Send peace and unity on earth.
Support us in our final strife
And lead us out of death to life.

songs.title: Lord, Thee I Love with All My Heart
songs.author: Martin Schalling (1532-1608) (trad. Catherine Winkworth (1827-1878))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Lord, Thee I love with all my heart;
I pray Thee, ne'er from me depart;
With tender mercy cheer me.

[1.2]
Earth has no pleasure I would share,
Yea, Heav'n itself were void and bare
If Thou, Lord, wert not near me.

[1.3]
And should my heart for sorrow break,
My trust in Thee can nothing shake.
Thou art the portion I have sought;
Thy precious blood my soul has bought.

[1.4]
Lord Jesus Christ, My God and Lord,
My God and Lord,
Forsake me not! I trust Thy Word.

[2.1]
Yea, Lord, 'twas Thy rich bounty gave
My body, soul, and all I have
In this poor life of labor.

[2.2]
Lord, grant that I in every place
May glorify Thy lavish grace
And serve and help my neighbor.

[2.3]
Let no false doctrine me beguile,
Let Satan not my soul defile.
Give strength and patience unto me
To bear my cross and follow Thee.

[2.4]
Lord Jesus Christ, My God and Lord,
My God and Lord,
In death Thy comfort still afford.

[3.1]
Lord, let at last Thine angels come,
To Abr'am's bosom bear me home,
That I may die unfearing;

[3.2]
And in its narrow chamber keep
My body safe in peaceful sleep
Until Thy reappearing.

[3.3]
And then from death awaken me,
That these mine eyes with joy may see,
O Son of God, Thy glorious face,
My Savior and my fount of grace.

[3.4]
Lord Jesus Christ, My prayer attend,
My prayer attend,
And I will praise Thee without end!

songs.title: Lord, Who at Cana's Wedding Feast
songs.author: Adelaide Thrupp (1831-1908)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Lord, who at Cana's wedding feast
Didst as a Guest appear,
Thou dearer far than earthly guest,
Vouchsafe Thy presence here.

[1.2]
For holy Thou indeed dost prove
The marriage vow to be,
Proclaiming it a type of love
Between the Church and Thee.

[2.1]
The holiest vow that man can make,
The golden thread in life,
The bond that none may dare to break,
That bindeth man and wife,

[2.2]
Which, blest by Thee, whate'er betide,
No evil shall destroy,
Through careworn days each care divides
And doubles every joy.

[3.1]
On those who at Thine altar kneel,
O Lord, Thy blessing pour,
That each may wake the other's zeal
To love Thee more and more.

[3.2]
Oh, grant them here in peace to live,
In purity and love,
And, this world leaving, to receive
A crown of life above.

songs.title: Magnificat
songs.author: Brian L. Penney (1951-)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
My soul shall magnify the Lord,
And with my spirit I rejoice;
My Savior has regard for me,
He hears His lowly servant's voice.

[2]
Behold, I am forever blessed,
For God has done great things for me;
His mercy rests on those who fear,
Who honor His Name most holy.

[3]
The Lord has shown His mighty arm,
Those proud in heart He shall put down;
The haughty from their thrones removed,
The lowly have God's blessing found.

[4]
The hungry with good things are filled,
They see God's kindness ev'ry day;
But on the rich no blessing rests,
With empty hands they're sent away.

[5]
The Lord helps His beloved ones,
In mercy He His cov'nant keeps;
Just as He promised long ago,
To Abraham, and to his Seed.

songs.title: May God Bestow on Us His Grace
songs.author: Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. Richard Massie (1800-1887))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
May God bestow on us His grace,
With blessings rich provide us,

[1.2]
And may the brightness of His face
To life eternal guide us
That we His saving health may know,
His gracious will and pleasure,

[1.3]
And also to the heathen show
Christ's riches without measure
And unto God convert them.

[2.1]
Thine over all shall be the praise
And thanks of every nation,
And all the world with joy shall raise
The voice of exultation;

[2.2]
For Thou shalt judge the earth, O Lord,
Nor suffer sin to flourish;

[2.3]
Thy people's pasture is Thy Word
Their souls to feed and nourish,
In righteous paths to keep them.

[3.1]
Oh, let the people praise Thy worth,
In all good works increasing;
The land shall plenteous fruit bring forth,
Thy Word is rich in blessing.

[3.2]
May God the Father, God the Son,
And God the Spirit bless us!
Let all the world praise Him alone,

[3.3]
Let solemn awe possess us.
Now let our hearts say, Amen.

songs.title: Moment By Moment
songs.author: Daniel Webster Whittle (1840-1901)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Dying with Jesus, by death reckoned mine;
Living with Jesus, a new life divine;
Looking to Jesus till glory doth shine,
Moment by moment, O Lord, I am Thine.

[1.2]
Moment by moment I'm kept in His love;
Moment by moment I've life from above;
Looking to Jesus till glory doth shine;
Moment by moment, O Lord, I am Thine.

[2.1]
Never a trial that He is not there,
Never a burden that He doth not bear,
Never a sorrow that He doth not share,

[2.2]
Moment by moment,
I'm under His care.

[3]
Never a heartache, and never a groan,
Never a teardrop and never a moan;
Never a danger but there on the throne,
Moment by moment He thinks of His own.

[4]
Never a weakness that He doth not feel,
Never a sickness that He cannot heal;
Moment by moment, in woe or in weal,
Jesus my Savior, abides with me still.

songs.title: More Love to Thee
songs.author: Elizabeth Payson Prentis (1818-1878)

songs.title: My Faith Looks Up To Thee
songs.author: Ray Palmer (1808-1887)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
My faith looks up to Thee,
Thou Lamb of Calvary,
Savior divine!

[1.2]
Now hear me while I pray,
Take all my guilt away,
O let me from this day
Be wholly Thine!

[2.1]
May Thy rich grace impart
Strength to my fainting heart,
My zeal inspire!

[2.2]
As Thou hast died for me,
O may my love to Thee,
Pure warm, and changeless be,
A living fire!

[3.1]
While life's dark maze I tread,
And griefs around me spread,
Be Thou my Guide;

[3.2]
Bid darkness turn to day,
Wipe sorrow's tears away,
Nor let me ever stray
From Thee aside.

[4.1]
When ends life's transient dream,
When death's cold sullen stream
Over me roll;

[4.2]
Blest Savior, then in love,
Fear and distrust remove;
O bear me safe above,
A ransomed soul!

songs.title: My Hope Is Built
songs.author: Edward Mote (1797-1874)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
My hope is built on nothing less
Than Jesus' blood and righteousness.
I dare not trust the sweetest frame,
But wholly trust in Jesus' Name.

[1.2]
On Christ the solid Rock I stand,
All other ground is sinking sand.

[2]
When darkness veils His lovely face,
I rest on His unchanging grace.
In every high and stormy gale,
My anchor holds within the veil.

[3.1]
His oath,
His covenant,
His blood,
Support me in the whelming flood.

[3.2]
When all around my soul gives way,
He then is all my hope and stay.

[4]
When He shall come with trumpet sound,
Oh may I then in Him be found.
Dressed in His righteousness alone,
Faultless to stand before the throne.

songs.title: My Jesus, As Thou Wilt
songs.author: Benjamin Schmolck (1672-1737) (trad. Jane Laurie Borthwick (1813-1897))
songs.composer: Carl Maria Friedrich Ernst von Weber (1786-1826)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
My Jesus, as Thou wilt!
Oh, may Thy will be mine!
Into Thy hand of love
I would my all resign;

[1.2]
Through sorrow, or through joy,
Conduct me as Thine own,
And help me still to say,
My Lord, Thy will be done!

[2.1]
My Jesus, as Thou wilt!
If needy here and poor,
Give me Thy people's bread,
Their portion rich and sure.

[2.2]
The manna of Thy Word
Let my soul feed upon;
And if all else should fail,
My Lord, thy will be done!

[3.1]
My Jesus, as Thou wilt!
Though seen through many'a tear,
Let not my star of hope
Grow dim or disappear;

[3.2]
Since Thou on earth hast wept,
And sorrowed oft alone,
If I must weep with Thee,
My Lord, Thy will be done!

[4.1]
My Jesus, as Thou wilt!
All shall be well for me;
Each changing future scene
I gladly trust with Thee:

[4.2]
Straight to my home above
I travel calmly on,
And sing, in life or death,
My Lord, Thy will be done!

songs.title: My Neighbor
songs.author: John G. Fleischmann (1960-)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Unclean and battered, torn by sin,
By things I do, my thoughts within,
I lie there bloodied on life's road
With death and sin my only load.

[2]
Across that road the world passed by
Turning a deaf ear to my cry,
No help to give, they could not save
And so they left me for my grave.

[3]
And, what of me, when I saw need?
Did I my Savior's bidding heed?
Too often on the other side
I've walked away because of pride.

[4]
Sin bleeds from me and stops my breath,
In Adam all I know is death;
My works are rags, my offerings vain,
From dust I came in dust remain.

[5]
But in my need my Savior died,
Not passing on the other side.
Rebreathed His Spirit in my dust,
Bound up my wounds, declared me just.

[6]
Now safe within His Church I'm free; Blood, Water, Spirit plead for me,
The Ark of God, the Inn of Grace Where I behold my Father's face.

[7]
May I in Christ my neighbor know Binding his wounds serves Christ below.
Your love for him make plain through me, that he may, too, your Glory see.

[8]
You loved me when I could not love, For my sin barred me from above.
In Christ my love is now set free, O praise and bless the Trinity.

songs.title: My Savior's Love
songs.author: Charles Hutchinson Gabriel (1856-1932)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
I stand amazed in the presence Of Jesus the Nazarene,
And wonder how He could love me,
A sinner, condemn'd, unclean.
How marvelous!

[1.2]
How wonderful!
And my song shall ever be:
O how marvelous!
O how wonderful!

[1.3]
And my song shall ever be:
How marvelous!
How wonderful!
Is my Savior's love for me!

[1.4]
O how marvelous!
O how wonderful!
Is my Savior's love for me!

[2]
For me it was in the garden He
Pray'd "Not my will, but Thine;" He had
No tears for His own griefs,
But sweat drops of blood for mine.

[3]
In pity angels beheld Him,
And came from the world of light To
Comfort Him in the sorrows,
He bore for my soul that night.

[4]
When with the ransomed in glory His face
I at last shall see, 'Twill be my
Joy thro' the ages,
To sing of His love for me.

songs.title: My Song Shall Be Of Jesus
songs.author: Fanny Jane Crosby (1820-1915), Edith Margaret Clarkson (1915-2008)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
My song shall be of Jesus,
His Mercy crowns my days
He fills my cup with blessings
And tunes my heart to praise

[1.2]
My song shall be of Jesus
The precious Lamb of God
Who gave Himself my ransom
And bought me with His blood

[2.1]
My song shall be of Jesus,
While sitting at His feet
He calls to mind His goodness,
And makes my joy complete;

[2.2]
My song shall be of Jesus,
Whatever ills befall,
I'll sing the grace that saves me,
And triumphs over all.

[3.1]
My song shall be of Jesus,
When pressing on my way
To where my home shines glorious
In pure and perfect day.

[3.2]
And when my soul shall enter
The many mansions fair,
A song of praise to Jesus
I'll sing forever there.

songs.title: My Soul, Now Praise Thy Maker
songs.author: Johann Graumann (1487-1541) (trad. Catherine Winkworth (1827-1878))
songs.composer: Augsburg, 1540 from Johannes Kugelmann's Concentus Novi
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
My soul, now praise thy maker!
Let all within me bless His name
Who maketh thee partaker
Of mercies more than thou dar'st claim.

[1.2]
Forget Him not whose meekness
Still bears with all thy sin,
Who healeth all thy weakness,
Renews thy life within.

[1.3]
Whose grace and care are endless
And saved thee through the past;
Who leaves no suff'rer friendless,
But rights the wronged at last.

[2.1]
He shows to man His treasure
Of judgment, truth, and righteousness,
His love beyond all measure,
His yearning pity o'er distress,

[2.2]
Nor treats us as we merit,
But lays His anger by.
The humble, contrite spirit
Finds His compassion nigh;

[2.3]
And high as Heav'n above us,
As break from close of day,
So far, since He doth love us,
He puts our sins away.

[3.1]
For as a tender father
Hath pity on his children here,
He in His arms will gather
All who are His in childlike fear.

[3.2]
He knows how frail our powers
Who but from dust are made;
We flourish like the flowers,
And even so we fade;

[3.3]
The wind but o'er them passes,
And all their bloom is o'er-
We wither like the grasses,
Our place knows us no more.

[4.1]
God's grace alone endureth,
And children's children yet shall prove
How He with strength assureth
The hearts of all that seek His love.

[4.2]
In Heav'n is fixed His dwelling,
His rule is over all;
Angels, in might excelling,
Bright hosts, before Him fall.

[4.3]
Praise Him who ever reigneth,
All ye who hear His Word,
Nor our poor hymns disdaineth-
My soul, O praise the Lord!

songs.title: Nearer, My God, To Thee
songs.author: Sarah Fuller Flower Adams (1805-1848), Hervey Doddridge Ganse (1822-1891), Edward Henry Jr. Bickersteth (1825-1906)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

[1.2]
E'en though it be a cross
That raiseth me,
Still all my song shall be,
Nearer, my God, to Thee.

[1.3]
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

[2.1]
Though like the wanderer,
The sun gone down,
Darkness be over me,
My rest a stone.

[2.2]
Yet in my dreams I'd be
Nearer, my God to Thee.
Then evermore to be
Nearer to Thee!

[3.1]
Nearer, my Lord, to thee,
Nearer to thee!
Who to the cross didst come,
Dying for me!

[3.2]
Strengthen my willing feet,
Hold me in service sweet

[4.1]
Nearer,
O Comforter,
Nearer to thee!
Who with my loving Lord Dwellest with me!

[4.2]
Grant me thy fellowship!
Help me each day to keep

[5.1]
But to be nearer still,
Bring me,
O God,
Not by the visioned steeps Angels have trod.

[5.2]
Here where thy cross I see,
Jesus,
I wait for thee,

[6]
There in my Father's home, safe and at rest,
There in my Savior's love, perfectly blest; Age
After age to be, nearer my God to Thee.

songs.title: No, Not One!
songs.author: Jr., Johnson Oatman (1856-1922)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
There's not a friend like the lowly Jesus,
No, not one! no, not one!
None else could heal all our soul's diseases,
No, not one! no, not one!

[1.2]
Jesus knows all about our struggles,
He will guide till the day is done;
There's not a friend like the lowly Jesus,
No, not one! no, not one!

[2.1]
No friend like Him is so high and holy,
No, not one!
No, not one!

[2.2]
And yet no friend is so meek and lowly,
No, not one!
No, not one!

[3.1]
There's not an hour that He is not near us,
No, not one!
No, not one!

[3.2]
No night so dark but His love can cheer us,
No, not one!
No, not one!

[4.1]
Did ever saint find this friend forsake him?
No, not one!
No, not one!
Or sinner find that He would not take him?

[4.2]
No, not one!
No, not one!

[5.1]
Was e'er a gift like the Savior given?
No, not one!
No, not one!
Will He refuse us a home in heaven?

[5.2]
No, not one!
No, not one!

songs.title: None Other Lamb
songs.author: Christina Georgina Rossetti (1830-1894)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
None other Lamb, none other name,
None other hope in Heav'n or earth or sea,
None other hiding place from guilt and shame,
None beside Thee!

[2]
My faith burns low, my hope burns low;
Only my heart's desire cries out in me
By the deep thunder of its want and woe,
Cries out to Thee.

[3]
Lord, Thou art life, though I be dead;
Love's fire Thou art, however cold I be:
Nor Heav'n have I, nor place to lay my head,
Nor home, but Thee.

songs.title: Not Worthy, Lord, to Gather Up the Crumbs
songs.author: Edward Henry Jr. Bickersteth (1825-1906)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Not worthy, Lord, to gather up the crumbs
With trembling hand that from Thy table fall,
A weary, heavy laden sinner comes
To plead Thy promise and obey Thy call.

[2]
I am not worthy to be thought Thy child,
Nor sit the last and lowest at Thy board;
Too long a wanderer and too oft beguiled;
I only ask one reconciling word.

[3]
One word from Thee, my Lord, one smile, one look,
And I could face the cold, rough world again;
And with that treasure in my heart could brook
The wrath of devils and the scorn of men.

[4]
And is not mercy Thy prerogative-
Free mercy, boundless, fathomless, divine?
Me, Lord, the chief of sinners, me forgive,
And Thine the greater glory, only Thine.

[5]
I hear Thy voice; Thou bid'st me come and rest;
I come, I kneel, I clasp Thy pierc�d feet;
Thou bid'st me take my place, a welcome guest
Among Thy saints, and of Thy banquet eat.

[6]
My praise can only breathe itself in prayer,
My prayer can only lose itself in Thee;
Dwell Thou forever in my heart, and there,
Lord, let me sup with Thee; sup Thou with me.

songs.title: Now Praise We Christ, the Holy One
songs.author: Coelius Sedulius (5th Century) (trad. Martin Luther (1483-1546), Richard Massie (1800-1887))
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Now praise we Christ, the Holy One,
The spotless virgin Mary's Son,
Far as the bless�d sun doth shine
E'en to the world's remote confine

[2]
He, who Himself all things did make,
A servant's form vouchsafed to take,
That He as man mankind might win,
And save His creatures from their sin.

[3]
The grace of God, th'Almighty Lord,
On the chaste mother was outpoured
A virgin pure and undefiled
In wondrous wise conceived a child.

[4]
The holy maid became th'abode
And temple of the living God;
And she, who knew not man, was blest
With God's own Word made manifest.

[5]
The noble mother bare a Son,
For so did Gabriel's promise run,
Whom John confessed and leapt with joy,
Ere yet the mother knew her boy.

[6]
In a rude manger, stretched on hay, In poverty content He lay;
With milk was fed the Lord of all, Who feeds the ravens when they call.

[7]
Th' angelic choir rejoice, and raise Their voice to God in songs of praise;
To humble shepherds is proclaimed The Shepherd who the world hath framed.

[8]
Honor to Thee, O Christ, be paid, Pure offspring of a holy maid,
With Father and with Holy Ghost, Till time in time's abyss be lost.

songs.title: Now Rest Beneath Night's Shadow
songs.author: Paul Gerhardt (1607-1676) (trad. composite)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Now rest beneath night's shadow
The woodland, field, and meadow,
The world in slumber lies;

[1.2]
But Thou, my heart, awake thee,
To prayer and song betake thee;
Let praise to thy Creator rise.

[2.1]
The radiant sun hath vanished,
His golden rays are banished
By night, the foe of day;

[2.2]
But Christ, the Sun of gladness,
Dispelling all my sadness,
Within my heart holds constant sway.

[3.1]
The rule of day is over
And shining jewels cover
The heaven's boundless blue.

[3.2]
Thus I shall shine in heaven,
Where crowns of gold are given
To all who faithful prove and true.

[4.1]
To rest my body hasteth,
Aside its garments casteth,
Types of mortality;

[4.2]
These I put off and ponder
How Christ will give me yonder
A robe of glorious majesty.

[5.1]
Lord Jesus, who dost love me,
Oh, spread Thy wings above me
And shield me from alarm!

[5.2]
Though evil would assail me,
Thy mercy will not fail me:
I rest in Thy protecting arm.

[6]
My loved ones, rest securely, For God this night will surely
From peril guard your heads. Sweet slumbers may He send you
And bid His hosts attend you And through the night watch o'er your beds.

songs.title: Now Thank We All Our God
songs.author: Martin Rinkart (1586-1649) (trad. Catherine Winkworth (1827-1878))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Now thank we all our God,
With heart and hands and voices,
Who wondrous things has done,
In Whom this world rejoices;

[1.2]
Who from our mothers' arms
Has blessed us on our way
With countless gifts of love,
And still is ours today.

[2.1]
O may this bounteous God
Through all our life be near us,
With ever joyful hearts
And blessed peace to cheer us;

[2.2]
And keep us in His grace,
And guide us when perplexed;
And free us from all ills,
In this world and the next!

[3.1]
All praise and thanks to God
The Father now be given;
The Son and Him Who reigns
With Them in highest Heaven;

[3.2]
The one eternal God,
Whom earth and Heav'n adore;
For thus it was, is now,
And shall be evermore.

songs.title: Now the Light Has Gone Away
songs.author: Frances Ridley Havergal (1836-1879)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Now the light has gone away;
Father, listen while I pray,
Asking Thee to watch and keep
And to send me quiet sleep.

[2]
Jesus, Savior, wash away
All that has been wrong today;
Help me every day to be
Good and gentle, more like Thee.

[3]
Let my near and dear ones be
Always near and dear to Thee.
Oh, bring me and all I love
To Thy happy home above.

[4]
Now my evening praise I give;
Thou didst die that I might live.
All my blessings come from Thee;
Oh, how good Thou art to me!

[5]
Thou, my best and kindest Friend,
Thou wilt love me to the end.
Let me love Thee more and more,
Always better than before.

songs.title: O Be Glad All Nations on Earth
songs.author: Brian L. Penney (1951-)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
O be glad, all nations on Earth,
Come let Jesus' Name be praised;
He is crowned, the King of glory,
At God's right hand He is raised.

[1.2]
Angels bowing down before Him,
Singing with the heav'nly throng;
Elders casting crowns before Him,
Singing an eternal song.

[2.1]
Great and marvelous are Your works,
Just and true are all Your ways;
All the nations bow in worship,
King of kings, Your Name they praise.

[2.2]
Angels bowing down before Him,
Singing with the heav'nly throng;
Elders casting crowns before Him,
Singing an eternal song.

[3.1]
When shall Heav'n and Earth together,
Walk before the Lamb, its Light?
When shall all the saints be gathered,
And that Day shall end the night?

[3.2]
Angels bowing down before Him,
Singing with the heav'nly throng;
Elders casting crowns before Him,
Singing an eternal song.

[4.1]
Lo, that day shall come with glory,
When Christ comes with trumpet sound;
Then the saints will cease their groaning,
Never more by death's chains bound.

[4.2]
Let us all bow down before Him,
Sing, O sing th'eternal song;
Work in hope until we meet Him,
And we join the heav'nly throng.

songs.title: O Chief of Cities Bethlehem
songs.author: Aurelius Clemens Prudentius (348-413) (trad. Nathaniel Barratt Smithers (1818-1896), Charles Winfred Douglas (1867-1944), John Patrick Crichton-Stuart Marquess of Bute (1847-1900))
songs.lyrics:
[1]
O chief of cities, Bethlehem,
Of David's crown the fairest gem,
But more to us than David's name,
In you, as man, the Savior came.

[2]
Beyond the sun in splendor bright,
Above you stands a wondrous light
Proclaiming from the conscious skies
That here, in flesh, the Godhead lies.

[3]
The wise men, seeing Him so fair,
Bow low before Him, and with prayer
Their treasured eastern gifts unfold
Of incense, myrrh, and royal gold.

[4]
The golden tribute owns Him King,
But frankincense to God they bring,
And last, prophetic sign, with myrrh,
They shadow forth His sepulcher.

[5]
O Jesus, whom the Gentiles see,
With Father, Spirit, One in Three:
To You, O God, be glory giv'n
By saints on earth and saints in Heav'n.

songs.title: O Come O Come Emmanuel
songs.author: unknown (trad. John Mason Neale (1818-1866))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
O come, O come, Emmanuel,
And ransom captive Israel,
That mourns in lonely exile here
Until the Son of God appear.

[1.2]
Rejoice! Rejoice! Emmanuel
Shall come to thee, O Israel.

[2.1]
O come,
Thou Wisdom from on high,
Who orderest all things mightily;

[2.2]
To us the path of knowledge show,
And teach us in her ways to go.

[3]
O come,
Thou Rod of Jesse, free Thine own from Satan's tyranny;
From depths of hell Thy people save,
And give them vict'ry ov'r the grave.

[4]
O come,
Thou Dayspring, come and cheer Our spirits by Thine advent here;
Disperse the gloomy clouds of night,
And death's dark shadows put to flight.

[5.1]
O come,
Thou Key of David, come,
And open wide our heav'nly home;

[5.2]
Make safe the way that leads on high,
And close the path to misery.

songs.title: O Come, All Ye Faithful
songs.author: John Francis Wade (circa 1710-1786) (trad. Frederick Oakeley (1802-1880), William Thomas Brooke (1848-1917))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
O come, all ye faithful, joyful and triumphant,
O come ye,
O come ye, to Bethlehem.
Come and behold Him, born the King of angels;

[1.2]
O come, let us adore Him,
O come, let us adore Him,
O come, let us adore Him,
Christ the Lord.

[2.1]
True God of true God,
Light from Light Eternal,
Lo,

[2.2]
He shuns not the Virgin's womb;
Son of the Father, begotten, not created;

[3]
Sing, choirs of angels, sing in exultation;
O sing, all ye citizens of heav'n above!
Glory to God, glory in the highest;

[4]
See how the shepherds, summoned to His cradle,
Leaving their flocks, draw nigh to gaze;
We too will thither bend our joyful footsteps;

[5.1]
Lo!
Star led chieftains,
Magi,
Christ adoring,

[5.2]
Offer Him incense, gold, and myrrh;
We to the Christ Child bring our hearts' oblations.

songs.title: O Day of Rest And Gladness
songs.author: Christopher Wordsworth (1807-1885)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
O day of rest and gladness,
O day of joy and light,
O balm of care and sadness,
Most beautiful, most bright:

[1.2]
On thee, the high and lowly,
Through ages joined in tune,
Sing holy, holy, holy,
To the great God Triune.

[2.1]
On thee, at the creation,
The light first had its birth;
On thee, for our salvation,
Christ rose from depths of earth;

[2.2]
On thee, our Lord, victorious,
The Spirit sent from heaven,
And thus on thee, most glorious,
A triple light was given.

[3.1]
Thou art a port, protected
From storms that round us rise;
A garden, intersected
With streams of paradise;

[3.2]
Thou art a cooling fountain
In life's dry, dreary sand;
From thee, like Pisgah's mountain,
We view our promised land.

[4.1]
Thou art a holy ladder,
Where angels go and come;
Each Sunday finds us gladder,
Nearer to heaven, our home;

[4.2]
A day of sweet refection,
Thou art a day of love,
A day of resurrection
From earth to things above.

[5.1]
Today on weary nations
The heavenly manna falls;

[5.2]
To holy convocations
The silver trumpet calls,
Where Gospel light is glowing
With pure and radiant beams,

[5.3]
And living water flowing,
With soul refreshing streams.

[6]
New graces ever gaining from this our day of rest,
We reach the rest remaining to spirits of the blessed.
To Holy Ghost be praises, to Father, and to Son;
The church her voice upraises to Thee, blessed Three in One.

songs.title: O Father, All Creating
songs.author: John Ellerton (1826-1893)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
O Father, all creating,
Whose wisdom, love, and pow'r
First bound two lives together
In Eden's primal hour,

[1.2]
Today to these Thy children
Thy earliest gifts renew:
A home by Thee made happy,
A love by Thee kept true.

[2.1]
O Savior, Guest most bounteous
Of old in Galilee,
Vouchsafe today Thy presence
With these who call on Thee;

[2.2]
Their store of earthly gladness
Transform to heav'nly wine,
And teach them, in the tasting
To know the gift is Thine.

[3.1]
O Spirit of the Father,
Breathe on them from above,
So mighty in Thy pureness,
So tender in Thy love;

[3.2]
That, guarded by Thy presence,
From sin and strife kept free,
Their lives may own Thy guidance,
Their hearts be rul'd by Thee.

[4.1]
Except Thou build it, Father,
The house is built in vain;
Except Thou, Savior, bless it,
The joy will turn to pain;

[4.2]
But naught can break the union
Of hearts in Thee made one,
And love Thy Spirit hallow'd
Is endless love begun.

songs.title: O For A Thousand Tongues
songs.author: Charles Wesley (1707-1788)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
O for a thousand tongues to sing
My great Redeemer's praise,
The glories of my God and King,
The triumphs of His grace!

[2]
My gracious Master and my God,
Assist me to proclaim,
To spread through all the earth abroad
The honors of Thy name.

[3]
Jesus! the name that charms our fears,
That bids our sorrows cease;
'Tis music in the sinner's ears,
'Tis life, and health, and peace.

[4]
He breaks the pow'r of canceled sin,
He sets the prisoner free;
His blood can make the foulest clean,
His blood availed for me.

[5]
He speaks, and, listening to His voice,
New life the dead receive,
The mournful, broken hearts rejoice,
The humble poor believe.

[6]
Hear Him, ye deaf; His praise, ye dumb,
Your loosened tongues employ;
Ye blind, behold your Savior come,
And leap, ye lame, for joy.

[7]
In Christ your Head, you then shall know,
Shall feel your sins forgiven;
Anticipate your heaven below,
And own that love is heaven.

[8]
Glory to God, and praise and love
Be ever, ever given,
By saints below and saints above,
The church in earth and heaven.

[9]
On this glad day the glorious Sun
Of Righteousness arose;
On my benighted soul He shone
And filled it with repose.

[10]
Sudden expired the legal strife,
'Twas then I ceased to grieve;
My second, real, living life
I then began to live.

[11]
Then with my heart I first believed,
Believed with faith divine,
Power with the Holy Ghost received
To call the Savior mine.

[12]
I felt my Lord's atoning blood
Close to my soul applied;
Me, me He loved, the Son of God,
For me, for me He died!

[13]
I found and owned His promise true,
Ascertained of my part,
My pardon passed in heaven I knew
When written on my heart.

[14]
Look unto Him, ye nations, own
Your God, ye fallen race;
Look, and be saved through faith alone,
Be justified by grace.

[15]
See all your sins on Jesus laid:
The Lamb of God was slain,
His soul was once an offering made
For every soul of man.

[16]
Awake from guilty nature's sleep,
And Christ shall give you light,
Cast all your sins into the deep,
And wash the �thiop white.

[17]
Harlots and publicans and thieves
In holy triumph join!
Saved is the sinner that believes
From crimes as great as mine.

[18]
Murderers and all ye hellish crew,
Ye sons of lust and pride,
Believe the Savior died for you;
For me the Savior died.

[19]
With me, your chief, ye then shall know,
Shall feel your sins forgiven;
Anticipate your heaven below,
And own that love is heaven.

songs.title: O Holy Spirit, Enter In
songs.author: Michael Schirmer (1606-1673) (trad. Catherine Winkworth (1827-1878))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
O Holy Spirit, enter in,
And in our hearts Thy work begin
Thy Temple deign to make us;

[1.2]
Sun of the soul, Thou Light divine,
Around and in us brightly shine,
To joy and gladness wake us.

[1.3]
That we to Thee
Truly living, To Thee giving
Prayer unceasing
May in love be still increasing.

[2.1]
Give to Thy Word impressive pow'r
That in our hearts, from this good hour,
As fire it may be glowing;

[2.2]
That we confess the Father, Son,
And Thee, the Spirit, Three in One,
Thy glory ever showing.

[2.3]
Stay Thou, guide now
Our souls ever that they never
May forsake Thee.
But by faith their refuge make Thee.

[3.1]
Thou fountain whence all wisdom flows
Which God on pious hearts bestows,
Grant us Thy consolation.

[3.2]
That in our pure faith's unity
We faithful witnesses may be
Of grace that brings salvation.

[3.3]
Hear us, cheer us,
By Thy teaching; let our preaching,
And our labor
Praise Thee, Lord, and serve our neighbor.

[4.1]
Left to ourselves, we shall but stray;
O lead us on the narrow way,
With wisest counsel guide us;

[4.2]
And give us steadfastness, that we
May ever faithful prove to Thee,
Whatever woes betide us;

[4.3]
Lord now Heal Thou
All hearts broken, And betoken
Thou art near us,
Whom we trust to light and cheer us.

[5.1]
Thy heav'nly strength sustain our heart
That we may act the valiant part
With Thee as our Reliance;

[5.2]
Be Thou our Refuge and our Shield
That we may never quit the field,
But stand in bold defiance.

[5.3]
Descend, defend
From all errors And earth's terrors
Thy salvation
Be our constant consolation.

[6.1]
O mighty Rock, O Source of life,
Let Thy dear Word 'mid doubt and strife
Be so within us burning,
That we be faithful unto death,

[6.2]
In Thy pure love and holy faith,
From Thee true wisdom learning!

[6.3]
Thy grace And peace
On us shower; By Thy power
Christ confessing,
Let us win our Savior's blessing.

[7.1]
O gentle Dew, from Heav'n now fall
With pow'r upon the hearts of all,
Thy tender love instilling,
That heart to heart more closely bound,

[7.2]
Fruitful in kindly deeds be found,
The law of love fulfilling;
The Lord, Discord
Shall not grieve Thee; We recieve Thee;

[7.3]
Where Thou livest.
Peace, and love, and joy Thou givest.

[8.1]
Grant that our days, while life shall last,
In purest holiness be passed,
Be Thou our Strength forever;

[8.2]
Grant that our hearts henceforth be free
From sinful lust and vanity
Which us from Thee must sever.

[8.3]
Keep Thou pure Now
From offenses Heart and senses.
Blessed Spirit!
Let us heavenly life inherit.

songs.title: O Holy, Blessed Trinity
songs.author: Martin Behm (1557-1622) (trad. Conrad Herman Louis Schuette (1843-1926))
songs.lyrics:
[1]
O Holy, Blessed Trinity,
Divine, Essential Unity,
God Father, Son, and Holy Ghost,
Be Thou this day my Guide and Host.

[2]
My soul and body keep from harm,
O'er all I have extend Thine arm,
That Satan may not cause distress
Nor bring me shame or wretchedness.

[3]
The Father's might shield me this day,
The Son's pure wisdom cheer my way,
The Holy Spirit's light divine
Illume my heart's benighted shrine.

[4]
My Maker, strengthen Thou my heart,
O my Redeemer, help impart,
Blest Comforter, keep at my side
That faith and love in me abide.

[5]
Lord, bless and keep Thou me as Thine;
Lord, make Thy face upon me shine;
Lord, lift Thy countenance on me
And give me peace- sweet peace, from Thee.

songs.title: O Little Town of Bethlehem
songs.author: Phillips Brooks (1835-1893)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
O little town of Bethlehem,
How still we see thee lie!
Above thy deep and dreamless sleep
The silent stars go by.

[1.2]
Yet in thy dark streets shineth
The everlasting Light;
The hopes and fears of all the years
Are met in thee tonight.

[2.1]
For Christ is born of Mary, and gathered all above,
While mortals sleep, the angels keep their watch of wond'ring love.

[2.2]
O morning stars together, proclaim the holy birth,
And praises sing to God the King, and
Peace to men on earth!

[3.1]
How silently, how silently,
The wondrous Gift is giv'n;
So God imparts to human hearts
The blessings of His Heav'n.

[3.2]
No ear may hear His coming,
But in this world of sin,
Where meek souls will receive Him still,
The dear Christ enters in.

[4.1]
Where children pure and happy pray to the bless�d Child,
Where misery cries out to Thee,
Son of the mother mild;

[4.2]
Where charity stands watching and faith holds wide the door,
The dark night wakes, the glory breaks, and Christmas comes once more.

[5.1]
O holy Child of Bethlehem,
Descend to us, we pray;
Cast out our sin, and enter in,
Be born in us today.

[5.2]
We hear the Christmas angels
The great glad tidings tell;
O come to us, abide with us,
Our Lord Emmanuel!

songs.title: O Lord My Soul Convicted
songs.author: James Maxwell
songs.lyrics:
[1]
O Lord, my soul convicted stands
Of breaking all Thy ten commands:
And on me justly might'st Thou pour
Thy wrath in one eternal show'r.

[2]
But thanks to God, its loud alarms
Have warn'd me of approaching harms;
And now, O Lord, my wants I see,
Lost and undone, I come to Thee.

[3]
I know my fig leaf righteousness
Can ne'er Thy broken law redress;
Yet in the gospel plan I see,
There's hope of pardon e'en for me.

[4]
There, I behold with wonder, Lord!
That Christ hath to Thy law restor'd
Those honors on th'atoning day,
Which guilty sinners took away.

[5]
Amazing wisdom, pow'r and love,
Display'd to rebels from above!
Do Thou, O Lord, my faith increase
To love and trust Thy plan of grace.

songs.title: O Lord of Heav'n and Earth and Sea
songs.author: Christopher Wordsworth (1807-1885)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
O Lord of Heav'n and earth and sea,
To Thee all praise and glory be;
How shall we show our love to Thee,
Who givest all?

[2]
The golden sunshine, vernal air,
Sweet flow'rs and fruits, Thy love declare;
Where harvests ripen, Thou art there,
Who givest all.

[3]
For peaceful homes and healthful days,
For all the blessings earth displays,
We owe Thee thankfulness and praise,
Who givest all.

[4]
Thou didst not spare Thine only Son,
But gav'st Him for a world undone,
And freely, with that bless�d One,
Thou givest all.

[5]
Thou giv'st the Spirit's bless�d dow'r,
Spirit of life and love and pow'r,
And dost His sev'nfold graces show'r
Upon us all.

[6]
For souls redeemed, for sins forgiv'n,
For means of grace and hopes of Heav'n,
Father, all praise to Thee be giv'n,
Who givest all.

[7]
We lose what on ourselves we spend,
We have as treasure without end
Whatever, Lord, to Thee we lend,
Who givest all.

[8]
To Thee, from Whom we all derive
Our life, our gifts, our power to give:
O may we ever with Thee live,
Who givest all.

songs.title: O Lord We Praise Thee
songs.author: Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. composite)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
O Lord, we praise Thee, bless Thee, and adore Thee,
In thanksgiving bow before Thee
Thou with Thy body and Thy blood didst nourish
Our weak souls that they may flourish:

[1.2]
O Lord, have mercy!
May Thy body, Lord, born of Mary,
That our sins and sorrows did carry,

[1.3]
And Thy blood for us plead
In all trial, fear, and need:
O Lord, have mercy!

[2.1]
Thy holy body into death was given,
Life to win for us in heaven.
No greater love than this to Thee could bind us;
May this feast thereof remind us!

[2.2]
O Lord, have mercy!
Lord, Thy kindness did so constrain Thee
That Thy blood should bless and sustain me.
All our debt Thou hast paid;

[2.3]
Peace with God once more is made:
O Lord, have mercy.

[3.1]
May God bestow on us His grace and favor
To please Him with our behavior
And live as brethren here in love and union
Nor repent this blest Communion!

[3.2]
O Lord, have mercy!
Let not Thy good Spirit forsake us;
Grant that heav'nly- minded He make us;

[3.3]
Give Thy Church, Lord, to see
Days of peace and unity:
O Lord, have mercy!

songs.title: O Lord, How Shall I Meet Thee
songs.author: Paul Gerhardt (1607-1676) (trad. unknown)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
O Lord, how shall I meet Thee,
How welcome Thee aright?
All nations long to see Thee,
My Hope, my heart's Delight!

[1.2]
O kindle, Lord, most holy,
Thy lamp within my breast,
To do in spirit lowly
All that may please Thee best.

[2.1]
Thy Zion palms is strewing,
And branches fresh and fair;
My heart, its pow'rs renewing,
An anthem shall prepare.

[2.2]
My soul puts off her sadness
Thy glories to proclaim;
With all her strength and gladness
She fain would serve Thy Name.

[3.1]
What hast Thou left ungranted
To give me glad relief?

[3.2]
When soul and body panted
In utmost depth of grief,
In deepest degradation,
Devoid of joy and peace,

[3.3]
Then, Thou, my soul's Salvation,
Didst come to bring release.

[4.1]
I lay in fetters groaning,
Thou com'st to set me free;
I stood, my shame bemoaning,
Thou com'st to honor me.

[4.2]
A glory Thou dost give me,
A treasure safe on high,
That will not fail nor leave me
As earthly riches fly.

[5.1]
Love caused Thine incarnation
Love brought Thee down to me;
Thy thirst for my salvation
Procured my liberty.

[5.2]
O love beyond all telling,
That led Thee to embrace,
In love all love excelling,
Our lost and fallen race!

songs.title: O Lord, I Am Not Worthy
songs.author: 1777 from Landshuter Gesangbuch (trad. unknown)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
O Lord, I am not worthy
That Thou should'st come to me,
But speak the words of comfort,
My spirit healed shall be.

[2]
O Lord, Thou art all holy,
The angels Thee adore;
How, then, ought I sincerely
My wrongs and sins deplore!

[3]
But when Thou soon wilt enter
My heart, my sinful heart,
Then heal me, be my shelter,
For Thou my Savior art.

[4]
O Lord, how can I thank Thee
For such a gift as this?
A gift which truly filleth
My soul with heav'nly bliss!

[5]
I praise Thee, I extol Thee,
I love Thee O my Sire,
Till once in joy and glory,
In heav'n I Thee admire.

songs.title: O Lord, My God, I Thirst For You
songs.author: Anthony Robertson (1932-)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
O Lord, my God, I thirst for You,
I long to see your face,
Just as the hunted deer is stressed
I falter in the race;

[1.2]
My heart cries out, my tears run down,
I am in deep distress,
'Where is your God?' men say to me,
They taunt me and oppress.

[2.1]
Lord, when will I be helped by You,
I struggle day and night?
O hear my prayer, enable me
To stand in your great might;

[2.2]
I look back on those days gone by
When, Lord, You were so near,
When in your house with festive throng
I praised your Name so dear.

[3.1]
So why am I cast down, O Lord,
And why should I feel low?
You are my God, my Savior strong,
Your praise from me shall flow;

[3.2]
I think of all your works, O Lord,
Your saving pow'r of old,
So when beset and overwhelmed,
I will your strength take hold.

[4.1]
Your loving- kindness fills my days,
Your song at night I sing,
And when my fears assail again
To You I'll tightly cling;

[4.2]
My hope is fixed on God, my Rock,
His own He won't forget;
Be still my soul, my face will shine
And I will praise Him yet.

songs.title: O Love, How Deep, How Broad, How High
songs.author: unknown (trad. Benjamin Webb (1819-1885))
songs.lyrics:
[1]
O love, how deep, how broad, how high,
How passing thought and fantasy,
That God, the Son of God, should take
Our mortal form for mortals' sake!

[2]
He sent no angel to our race
Of higher or of lower place,
But wore the robe of human frame
And He Himself, to this world came.

[3]
Nor willed He only to appear;
His pleasure was to tarry here;
And God and Man with man would be
The space of thirty years and three.

[4]
For us baptized, for us He bore
His holy fast and hungered sore,
For us temptations sharp He knew;
For us the tempter overthrew.

[5]
For us He prayed; for us He taught;
For us His daily works He wrought;
By words and signs and actions thus
Still seeking not Himself, but us.

[6]
For us to wicked men betrayed,
Scourged, mocked, in crown of thorns arrayed,
For us He bore the cross's death,
For us at length gave up His breath.

[7]
For us He rose from death again;
For us He went on high to reign;
For us He sent His Spirit here,
To guide, to strengthen, and to cheer.

[8]
All honor, laud, and glory be,
O Jesus, virgin-born to Thee!
All glory, as is ever meet
To Father and to Paraclete.

songs.title: O Sacred Head, Now Wounded
songs.author: Bernard of Clairvaux (1091-1153) (trad. James Waddel Alexander (1804-1859))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
O sacred Head, now wounded,
With grief and shame weighed down,
Now scornfully surrounded
With thorns, Thine only crown;

[1.2]
O sacred Head, what glory,
What bliss till now was Thine!
Yet, though despised and gory,
I joy to call Thee mine.

[2.1]
What Thou, my Lord, hast suffered,
Was all for sinners' gain;
Mine, mine was the transgression,
But Thine the deadly pain.

[2.2]
Lo, here I fall, my Savior!
'Tis I deserve Thy place;
Look on me with Thy favor,
Vouchsafe to me Thy grace.

[3.1]
Men mock and taunt and jeer Thee,
Thou noble countenance,
Though mighty worlds shall fear Thee
And flee before Thy glance.

[3.2]
How art thou pale with anguish,
With sore abuse and scorn!
How doth Thy visage languish
That once was bright as morn!

[4.1]
Now from Thy cheeks has vanished
Their color once so fair;
From Thy red lips is banished
The splendor that was there.

[4.2]
Grim death, with cruel rigor,
Hath robbed Thee of Thy life;
Thus Thou hast lost Thy vigor,
Thy strength in this sad strife.

[5.1]
My burden in Thy Passion,
Lord, Thou hast borne for me,
For it was my transgression
Which brought this woe on Thee.

[5.2]
I cast me down before Thee,
Wrath were my rightful lot;
Have mercy, I implore Thee;
Redeemer, spurn me not!

[6]
What language shall I borrow to thank Thee, dearest friend,
For this Thy dying sorrow, Thy pity without end?
O make me Thine forever, and should I fainting be,
Lord, let me never, never outlive my love to Thee.

[7]
My Shepherd, now receive me; my Guardian, own me Thine.
Great blessings Thou didst give me, O source of gifts divine.
Thy lips have often fed me with words of truth and love;
Thy Spirit oft hath led me to heavenly joys above.

[8]
Here I will stand beside Thee, from Thee I will not part;
O Savior, do not chide me! When breaks Thy loving heart,
When soul and body languish in death's cold, cruel grasp,
Then, in Thy deepest anguish, Thee in mine arms I'll clasp.

[9]
The joy can never be spoken, above all joys beside,
When in Thy body broken I thus with safety hide.
O Lord of Life, desiring Thy glory now to see,
Beside Thy cross expiring, I'd breathe my soul to Thee.

[10]
My Savior, be Thou near me when death is at my door;
Then let Thy presence cheer me, forsake me nevermore!
When soul and body languish, oh, leave me not alone,
But take away mine anguish by virtue of Thine own!

[11]
Be Thou my consolation, my shield when I must die;
Remind me of Thy passion when my last hour draws nigh.
Mine eyes shall then behold Thee, upon Thy cross shall dwell,
My heart by faith enfolds Thee. Who dieth thus dies well.

songs.title: O That The Lord Would Guide My Ways
songs.author: Isaac Watts (1674-1748)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
O that the Lord would guide my ways
To keep His statutes still!
O that my God would grant me grace
To know and do His will!

[2]
O send Thy Spirit down to write
Thy law upon my heart!
Nor let my tongue indulge deceit,
Nor act the liar's part.

[3]
From vanity turn off mine eyes;
Let no corrupt design,
Nor covetous desires arise
Within this soul of mine.

[4]
Order my footsteps by Thy Word,
And make my heart sincere;
Let sin have no dominion, Lord,
But keep my conscience clear.

[5]
Assist my soul, too apt to stray,
A stricter watch to keep;
And should I e'er forget Thy way,
Restore Thy wand'ring sheep.

[6]
Make me to walk in Thy commands, 'Tis a delightful road;
Nor let my head, or heart, or hands, Offend against my God.

songs.title: O The Deep, Deep Love of Jesus
songs.author: Samuel Trevor Francis (1834-1925)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
O the deep, deep love of Jesus,
Vast, unmeasured, boundless, free!
Rolling as a mighty ocean
In its fullness over me!

[1.2]
Underneath me, all around me,
Is the current of Thy love
Leading onward, leading homeward
To Thy glorious rest above!

[2.1]
O the deep, deep love of Jesus,
Spread His praise from shore to shore!
How He loveth, ever loveth,
Changeth never, nevermore!

[2.2]
How He watches o'er His loved ones,
Died to call them all His own;
How for them He intercedeth,
Watcheth o'er them from the throne!

[3.1]
O the deep, deep love of Jesus,
Love of every love the best!
'Tis an ocean full of blessing,
'Tis a haven giving rest!

[3.2]
O the deep, deep love of Jesus,
'Tis a heav'n of heav'ns to me;
And it lifts me up to glory,
For it lifts me up to Thee!

songs.title: O Trinity of Blessed Light
songs.author: Ambrose of Milan (340-397) (trad. John Mason Neale (1818-1866))
songs.lyrics:
[1]
O Trinity of bless�d light,
O Unity of princely might,
The fiery sun now goes his way;
Shed Thou within our hearts a ray.

[2]
To Thee our morning song of praise,
To Thee our evening prayer we raise;
O grant us with Thy saints on high
To praise Thee through eternity.

[3]
All laud to God the Father be,
All praise, eternal Son, to Thee,
All glory, as is ever meet,
To God the holy Paraclete.

songs.title: O Wondrous Type, O Vision Fair
songs.author: Latin (trad. John Mason Neale (1818-1866))
songs.lyrics:
[1]
O wondrous type! O vision fair
Of glory that the Church may share,
Which Christ upon the mountain shows,
Where brighter than the sun He glows!

[2]
From age to age the tale declare,
How with the three disciples there,
Where Moses and Elijah meet,
The Lord holds converse high and sweet.

[3]
The law and prophets there have place,
Two chosen witnesses of grace;
The Father's voice from out the cloud
Proclaims His only Son aloud.

[4]
With shining face and bright array,
Christ deigns to manifest today
What glory shall be theirs above
Who joy in God with perfect love.

[5]
And faithful hearts are raised on high
By this great vision's mystery;
For which in joyful strains we raise
The voice of prayer, the hymn of praise.

[6]
O Father, with th'Eternal Son,
And Holy Spirit, ever One,
Vouchsafe to bring us by Thy grace
To see Thy glory face to face.

songs.title: Of The Father's Love Begotten
songs.author: Aurelius Clemens Prudentius (348-413) (trad. John Mason Neale (1818-1866), Henry Williams Baker (1821-1877))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Of the Father's love begotten
Ere the worlds began to be,
He is Alpha and Omega,
He the source, the ending He,

[1.2]
Of the things that are, that have been,
And that future years shall see,
Evermore and evermore!

[2.1]
At His Word they were created;
He commanded; it was done:
Heav'n and earth and depths of ocean
In their threefold order one;

[2.2]
All that grows beneath the shining
Of the moon and burning sun,
Evermore and evermore!

[3.1]
He is found in human fashion,
Death and sorrow here to know,
That the race of Adam's children,
Doomed by law to endless woe,

[3.2]
May not henceforth die and perish
In the dreadful gulf below,
Evermore and evermore!

[4.1]
Oh that birth forever bless�d!
When the virgin, full of grace,
By the Holy Ghost conceiving,
Bare the Savior of our race;

[4.2]
And the Babe, the world's Redeemer,
First revealed His sacred face,
Evermore and evermore!

[5.1]
O ye heights of heav'n adore Him;
Angel hosts, His praises sing;
Pow'rs, dominions, bow before Him,
And extol our God and King:

[5.2]
Let no tongue on earth be silent,
Every voice in concert ring,
Evermore and evermore!

[6]
He is here, Whom seers in old time Chanted of, while ages ran;
Whom the writings of the prophets Promised since the world began:
Then foretold, now manifested, to receive the praise of man,
Evermore and evermore!

[7]
Righteous Judge of souls departed, Righteous King of them that live,
On the Father's throne exalted None in might with Thee may strive;
Who at last in vengeance coming Sinners from Thy face shalt drive,
Evermore and evermore!

[8]
Thee let old men, Thee let young men, Thee let choirs of infants sing;
Thee the matrons and the virgins, And the children answering:
Let their guileless songs re-echo, And the heart its music bring,
Evermore and evermore!

[9]
Christ, to Thee with God the Father, And, O Holy Ghost, to Thee,
Hymn and chant with high thanksgiving, And unwearied praises be:
Honor, glory, and dominion, And eternal victory,
Evermore and evermore!

songs.title: Oh, Blest the House
songs.author: Christoph Karl Ludwig von Pfeil (1712-1784) (trad. Catherine Winkworth (1827-1878))
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Oh blest the house, whate'er befall,
Where Jesus Christ is All in All;
Yea, if He were not dwelling there,
How poor and dark and void it were!

[2]
Oh blest that house where faith ye find,
And all within have set their mind
To trust their God and serve Him still,
And do in all His holy will.

[3]
Blest, where their prayers shall daily rise
As fragrant incense to the skies,
While in their lives the world is taught
That forms without the heart are naught.

[4]
Blest, where the busy hands fulfil
Their proper task with ready skill,
While through their different works ye see
One spirit run of unity.

[5]
Blest such a house, it prospers well,
In peace and joy the parents dwell,
And in their children's lot is shown
How richly God can bless His own.

[6]
Then here will I and mine to-day
A solemn covenant make, and say,--
Though all the world forsake Thy Word,
I and my house will serve the Lord.

songs.title: On Jordan's Bank the Baptist's Cry
songs.author: Charles Coffin (or Carolo or Carolus) (1676-1749) (trad. John Chandler (1806-1876))
songs.lyrics:
[1]
On Jordan's bank the Baptist's cry
Announces that the Lord is nigh;
Come, then, and hearken, for he brings
Glad tidings from the King of kings!

[2]
Then cleansed be every breast from sin;
Make straight the way for God within;
Prepare we in our hearts a home,
Where such a mighty Guest may come.

[3]
For Thou art our Salvation, Lord,
Our Refuge, and our great Reward.
Without Thy grace our souls must fade
And wither like a flow'r decayed.

[4]
Stretch forth Thine hand, to heal our sore,
And make us rise and fall no more;
Once more upon Thy people shine,
And fill the world with love divine.

[5]
To Him Who left the throne of Heav'n
To save mankind, all praise be giv'n;
Like praise be to the Father done,
And Holy Spirit, Three in One.

songs.title: On What Has Now Been Sown
songs.author: John Newton (1725-1807)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
On what has now been sown
Thy blessing, Lord, bestow;
The pow'r is Thine alone
To make it spring and grow.

[1.2]
Do Thou in grace the harvest raise,
And Thou alone shalt have the praise.

[2.1]
To Thee our wants are known,
From Thee are all our pow'rs;
Accept what is Thine own
And pardon what is ours.

[2.2]
Our praises, Lord, and prayers receive
And to Thy Word a blessing give.

[3.1]
Oh, grant that each of us
Now met before Thee here
May meet together thus
When Thou and Thine appear

[3.2]
And follow Thee to Heav'n, our home.
E'en so, Amen, Lord Jesus, come!

songs.title: One Thing's Needful
songs.author: Johann Heinrich Schr�der (1667-1699) (trad. Frances Elizabeth Cox (1812-1897))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
One thing's needful: then, Lord Jesus,
Keep this one thing in my mind;
All beside, though first it please us,
Soon a grievous yoke we find:

[1.2]
Beneath it the heart is still fretting and striving,
No true, lasting happiness ever deriving.
The gain of this one thing all loss can requite
And teach me in all things to find true delight.

[2.1]
Soul, wilt thou this one thing find thee?
Seek not midst created things;
What is earthly, leave behind thee,
Over nature stretch thy wings;

[2.2]
For where God and man both in One are united,
With God's perfect fullness the heart is delighted;
There, there is the worthiest lot and the best,
My One and my All, and my Joy, and my Rest.

[3.1]
How were Mary's thoughts devoted,
Her eternal joy to find,
As intent each word she noted,
At her Savior's feet reclined:

[3.2]
How kindled her heart, how devout was its feeling,
While hearing the lessons that Christ was revealing;
For Jesus all earthly concerns she forgot,
And all was repaid in that one happy lot.

[4.1]
Thus my longings, heav'nward tending,
Jesus, rest alone on Thee;
Help me, thus on Thee depending,
Savior! come and dwell in me:

[4.2]
Although all the world should forsake and forget Thee,
In love I will follow Thee, ne'er will I quit Thee;
For Jesus, both Spirit and life is Thy Word,
And is there a joy which Thou dost not afford?

[5.1]
Wisdom's highest noblest treasure,
Jesus, lies conceal'd in Thee;
Grant that this may still the measure
Of my will and actions be:

[5.2]
Humility there and simplicity reigning,
My steps shall in wisdom for ever be training;
Oh! if I of Christ have this knowledge divine,
The fullness of heavenly wisdom is mine.

[6.1]
Christ, Thou art the sole oblation
That I'll bring before my God;
In his sight I've acceptation
Only through Thy streaming blood:

[6.2]
Immaculate righteousness now I've acquired,
Since Thou on the tree of the cross hast expired;
The robe of salvation for ever is mine,
In this shall my faith through eternity shine.

[7.1]
Let my soul, in full exemption,
Wake up in Thy likeness now;
Thou art made to me redemption,
My sanctification Thou.

[7.2]
Whatever I need for my Journey to Heaven
In Thee, I my Savior, is unto me given.
Oh! let me all perishing pleasures forgo,
And Thy life, O Jesus! alone let me know.

[8.1]
Where should else my hopes be centered?
Grace o'erwhelms me with its flood;
Thou, my Savior, once hast enter'd
Holiest heaven through Thy blood:

[8.2]
Eternal redemption for sinners there finding,
From hell's dark dominion my spirit unbinding,
To me perfect freedom Thy entrance has brought,
And childlike to cry, "Abba, Father," I'm taught.

[9.1]
Christ Himself, my Shepherd, feeds me,
Peace and joy my spirit fill;
In a pasture green He leads me
Forth beside the waters still:

[9.2]
Oh! naught to my soul is so sweet and reviving,
As thus unto Jesus alone to be living;
True happiness this, and this only supplies,
Through faith on my Savior to fasten my eyes.

[10.1]
Therefore, Jesus, my Salvation,
Thou my One, my All shalt be;
Prove my fix'd determination,
Root out all hypocrisy:

[10.2]
Look well if on sin's slippery paths I am hasting,
And lead me, O Lord, in the way everlasting;
This one thing is needful, all others are vain,
I count all but loss that I Christ may obtain.

songs.title: Open Now Thy Gates of Beauty
songs.author: Benjamin Schmolck (1672-1737) (trad. Catherine Winkworth (1827-1878))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Open now thy gates of beauty,
Zion, let me enter there,
Where my soul in joyful duty
Waits for Him Who answers prayer.

[1.2]
Oh, how bless�d is this place,
Filled with solace, light and grace!

[2.1]
Lord, my God, I come before Thee,
Come Thou also unto me;
Where we find Thee and adore Thee,
There a heav'n on earth must be.

[2.2]
To my heart, oh, enter Thou,
Let it be Thy temple now!

[3.1]
Here Thy praise is gladly chanted,
Here Thy seed is duly sown;

[3.2]
Let my soul, where it is planted,
Bring forth precious sheaves alone,
So that all I hear may be
Fruitful unto life in me.

[4.1]
Thou my faith increase and quicken,
Let me keep Thy gift divine,
Howsoe'er temptations thicken;

[4.2]
May Thy Word still o'er me shine
As my guiding star through life,
As my comfort in my strife.

[5.1]
Speak, O God, and I will hear Thee,
Let Thy will be done indeed;
May I undisturbed draw near Thee
While Thou dost Thy people feed.

[5.2]
Here of life the fountain flows,
Here is balm for all our woes.

songs.title: Our Father Thou in Heaven Above
songs.author: Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. composite)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Our Father, Thou in heav'n above,
Who biddest us to dwell in love,
As brethren of one family,
To cry in ev'ry need to Thee,

[1.2]
Teach us no thoughtless word to say,
But from our inmost heart to pray.

[2.1]
Thy name be hallowed. Help us, Lord,
In purity to keep Thy Word,
That to the glory of Thy Name
We walk before Thee free from blame.

[2.2]
Let no false doctrine us pervert;
All poor, deluded souls convert.

[3.1]
Thy kingdom come. Thine let it be
In time and in eternity.
Let Thy good Spirit e'er be nigh
Our hearts with graces to supply.

[3.2]
Break Satan's pow'r, defeat his rage;
Preserve Thy Church from age to age.

[4.1]
Thy gracious will on earth be done
As 'tis in heav'n before Thy throne;
Obedience in our weal and woe
And patience in all grief bestow.

[4.2]
Curb flesh and blood and ev'ry ill
That sets itself against Thy will.

[5.1]
Give us this day our daily bread
And let us all be clothed and fed.

[5.2]
From war and strife be our Defense,
From famine and from pestilence,
That we may live in godly peace,
Free from all care and avarice.

[6.1]
Forgive our sins, Lord, we implore,
Remove from us their burden sore,
As we their trespasses forgive
Who by offenses us do grieve.

[6.2]
Thus let us dwell in charity
And serve our brother willingly.

[7.1]
Into temptation lead us not.
When evil foes against us plot
And vex our souls on every hand,

[7.2]
Oh, give us strength that we may stand
Firm in the faith, a well-armed host,
Through comfort of the Holy Ghost!

[8.1]
From evil, Lord, deliver us;
The times and days are perilous.

[8.2]
Redeem us from eternal death,
And when we yield our dying breath,
Console us, grant us calm release,
And take our souls to Thee in peace.

[9.1]
Amen, that is, So shall it be.
Confirm our faith and hope in Thee
That we may doubt not, but believe
What here we ask we shall receive.

[9.2]
Thus in Thy name and at Thy word
We say: Amen. Oh, hear us, Lord! Amen.

songs.title: Our God, Our Help In Ages Past
songs.author: Isaac Watts (1674-1748)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Our God, our help in ages past,
Our hope for years to come,
Our shelter from the stormy blast,
And our eternal home.

[2]
Under the shadow of Thy throne
Thy saints have dwelt secure;
Sufficient is Thine arm alone,
And our defense is sure.

[3]
Before the hills in order stood,
Or earth received her frame,
From everlasting Thou art God,
To endless years the same.

[4]
Thy Word commands our flesh to dust,
'Return, ye sons of men:'
All nations rose from earth at first,
And turn to earth again.

[5]
A thousand ages in Thy sight
Are like an evening gone;
Short as the watch that ends the night
Before the rising sun.

[6]
The busy tribes of flesh and blood,
With all their lives and cares,
Are carried downwards by the flood,
And lost in following years.

[7]
Time, like an ever rolling stream,
Bears all its sons away;
They fly, forgotten, as a dream
Dies at the opening day.

[8]
Like flowery fields the nations stand
Pleased with the morning light;
The flowers beneath the mower's hand
Lie withering ere 'tis night.

[9]
Our God, our help in ages past,
Our hope for years to come,
Be Thou our guard while troubles last,
And our eternal home.

songs.title: Out of the Deep I Cry to Thee
songs.author: Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. Arthur Tozel Russell (1806-1874))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Out of the deep I cry to Thee;
O Lord God, hear my crying:
Incline Thy gracious ear to me,
With prayer to Thee applying.

[1.2]
For if Thou fix Thy searching eye
On all sin and iniquity,
Who, Lord, can stand before Thee?

[2.1]
But love and grace with Thee prevail,
O God, our sins forgiving;
The holiest deeds can naught avail
Of all before Thee living.

[2.2]
Before Thee none can boast him clear;
Therefore must each Thy judgment fear,
And live on Thy compassion.

[3.1]
For this, my hope in God shall rest,
Naught building on my merit;
My heart confides, of Him possest,
His goodness stays my spirit.

[3.2]
His precious word assureth me;
My solace, my sure Rock is he,
Whereon my soul abideth.

[4.1]
And though I wait the livelong night
And till the morn returneth,
My heart undoubting trusts His might
Nor in impatience mourneth.

[4.2]
Born of His Spirit, Israel
In the right Way thus fareth well,
And on his God reposeth

[5.1]
What though our sins are manifold?
Supreme His mercy reigneth;
No limit can His hand withhold,
Where evil most obtaineth.

[5.2]
He the good Shepherd is alone,
Who Israel will redeem and own,
Forgiving all transgression.

songs.title: Over Kidron Jesus Treadeth
songs.author: Thomas Hansen Kingo (1634-1703) (trad. J. Jeffrey (19th Century))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Over Kidron Jesus treadeth
To His passion for us all;
Every human eye be weeping,
Tears of bitter grief let fall!

[1.2]
Round His Spirit flock the foes,
Place their shafts and bend their bows,
Aiming at the Savior solely,
While the world forsakes Him wholly.

[2.1]
David once, with heart afflicted,
Crossed the Kidron's narrow strand,
Clouds of gloom and grief about him
When an exile from his land.

[2.2]
But, O Jesus, blacker now
Bends the cloud above Thy brow,
Hasting to death's dreary portals
For the shame and sin of mortals.

[3.1]
See how, anguish struck, He falleth
Prostrate, and with struggling breath,
Three times on His God He calleth,

[3.2]
Praying that the bitter death
And the cup of doom may go,
Still He cries, in all His woe:

[3.3]
"Not My will, but Thine, O Father!"
And the angels round Him gather.

[4.1]
See how, in that hour of darkness,
Battling with the evil pow'r,
Agonies untold assail Him,
On His soul the arrows show'r;

[4.2]
All the garden flow'rs are wet
With the drops of bloody sweat,
From His anguished frame distilling-
World's redemption thus fulfilling!

[5.1]
But, O flow'rs, so sadly watered
By this pure and precious dew,
In some blessed hour your blossoms
'Neath the olive shadows grew!

[5.2]
Eden's garden did not bear
Aught that can with you compare,
For the blood, thus freely given,
Makes my soul the heir of heaven.

[6]
When as flow'rs themselves I wither, When I droop and fade like grass,
When the life-streams through my pulses Dull and ever duller pass,
When at last they cease to roll, Then, to cheer my sinking soul,
Grace of Jesus, be Thou given- Source of triumph! pledge of heaven!

songs.title: Pass Me Not, O Gentle Savior
songs.author: Fanny Jane Crosby (1820-1915)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Pass me not, O gentle Savior,
Hear my humble cry;
While on others Thou art calling,
Do not pass me by.

[1.2]
Savior, Savior, Hear my humble cry;
While on others Thou art calling,
Do not pass me by.

[2]
Let me at Thy throne of mercy Find a sweet relief,
Kneeling there in deep contrition;
Help my unbelief.

[3.1]
3,
Trusting only in Thy merit,
Would I seek Thy face;

[3.2]
Heal my wounded, broken spirit,
Save me by Thy grace.

[4]
Thou the Spring of all my comfort,
More than life to me,
Whom have I on earth beside Thee?
Whom in Heav'n but Thee?

songs.title: Praise God From Whom All Blessings Flow
songs.author: Thomas Ken (1637-1711)

songs.title: Praise My Soul The King Of Heaven
songs.author: Henry F. Lyte (1793-1847)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Praise, my soul, the King of heaven;
To His feet thy tribute bring.
Ransomed, healed, restored, forgiven,
Evermore His praises sing:

[1.2]
Alleluia! Alleluia!
Praise the everlasting King.

[2.1]
Praise Him for His grace and favor
To our fathers in distress.
Praise Him still the same as ever,
Slow to chide, and swift to bless.

[2.2]
Alleluia! Alleluia!
Glorious in His faithfulness.

[3.1]
Father like He tends and spares us;
Well our feeble frame He knows.
In His hands He gently bears us,
Rescues us from all our foes.

[3.2]
Alleluia! Alleluia!
Widely yet His mercy flows.

[4.1]
Frail as summer's flower we flourish,
Blows the wind and it is gone;

[4.2]
