But while mortals rise and perish
Our God lives unchanging on,
Praise Him, Praise Him, Hallelujah
Praise the High Eternal One!

[5.1]
Angels, help us to adore Him;
Ye behold Him face to face;
Sun and moon, bow down before Him,
Dwellers all in time and space.

[5.2]
Alleluia! Alleluia!
Praise with us the God of grace.

songs.title: Praise The Lord, Ye Heavens Adore Him
songs.author: Edward Osler (1798-1863)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Praise the Lord, ye heav'ns, adore Him;
Praise Him, angels in the height.
Sun and moon, rejoice before Him;
Praise Him, all ye stars of light.

[1.2]
Praise the Lord, for He hath spoken;
Worlds His mighty voice obeyed.
Laws which never shall be broken
For their guidance He hath made.

[2.1]
Praise the Lord, for He is glorious;
Never shall His promise fail.
God hath made His saints victorious;
Sin and death shall not prevail.

[2.2]
Praise the God of our salvation;
Hosts on high, His pow'r proclaim.
Heav'n and earth and all creation,
Laud and magnify His name.

[3.1]
Worship, honor, glory, blessing,
Lord, we offer unto Thee.
Young and old, Thy praise expressing,
In glad homage bend the knee.

[3.2]
All the saints in Heav'n adore Thee;
We would bow before Thy throne.
As Thine angels serve before Thee,
So on earth Thy will be done.

songs.title: Praise To The Lord, The Almighty
songs.author: Joachim Neander (1650-1680) (trad. Catherine Winkworth (1827-1878))
songs.composer: 1665 from Ander Theil des Erneuerten Gesangbuch
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Praise to the Lord, the Almighty, the King of creation!
O my soul, praise Him, for He is thy health and salvation!
All ye who hear,

[1.2]
Now to His temple draw near;
Praise Him in glad adoration.

[2.1]
Praise to the Lord, Who o'er all things so wondrously reigneth,
Shelters thee under His wings, yea, so gently sustaineth!

[2.2]
Hast thou not seen
How thy desires have been
Granted in what He ordaineth

[3.1]
Praise to the Lord, Who hath fearfully, wondrously, made thee;
Health hath vouchsafed and, when heedlessly falling, hath stayed thee.
What need or grief

[3.2]
Ever hath failed of relief?
Wings of His mercy did shade thee.

[4.1]
Praise to the Lord, Who doth prosper thy work and defend thee;
Surely His goodness and mercy here daily attend thee.

[4.2]
Ponder anew
What the Almighty can do,
If with His love He befriend thee.

[5.1]
Praise to the Lord, Who, when tempests their warfare are waging,
Who, when the elements madly around thee are raging,
Biddeth them cease,

[5.2]
Turneth their fury to peace,
Whirlwinds and waters assuaging.

songs.title: Rejoice, My Heart, Be Glad and Sing
songs.author: Paul Gerhardt (1607-1676) (trad. composite)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Rejoice, my heart, be glad and sing,
A cheerful trust maintain;
For God, the Source of everything,
Thy Portion shall remain.

[2]
He is thy Treasure, He thy Joy,
Thy Life and Light and Lord,
Thy Counselor when doubts annoy,
Thy Shield and great Reward.

[3]
Why spend the day in blank despair,
In restless thought the night?
On thy Creator cast thy care;
He makes thy burdens light.

[4]
Did not His love and truth and pow'r
Watch o'er thy childhood day?
Has He not oft in threat'ning hour
Turned dreaded ills away?

[5]
His wisdom never plans in vain,
Ne'er falters or mistakes;
All that His counsels did ordain
A happy ending makes.

songs.title: Rejoice, O Pilgrim Throng
songs.author: Edward Hayes Plumptre (1821-1891)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Rejoice,
O pilgrim throng!
Rejoice, give thanks, and sing;

[1.2]
Your festal banner wave on high,
The cross of Christ your King.
Rejoice, rejoice, rejoice,
Give thanks and sing.

[1.3]
Rejoice, rejoice, rejoice,
Give thanks and sing.

[2]
With all the angel choirs,
With all the saints on earth,
Pour out the strains of joy and bliss,
True rapture, noblest mirth.

[3]
With voice as full and strong As ocean's surging praise,
Send forth the hymns our fathers loved,
The psalms of ancient days.

[4]
Still lift your standard high,
Still march in firm array,
As warriors through the darkness toil,
Till dawns the golden day.

[5]
Yes, on through life's long path,
Still chanting as ye go;
From youth to age, by night and day,
In gladness and in woe.

[6]
Yes onward, onward still With hymn, and chant and song,
Through gate, and porch and columned aisle, The hallowed pathways throng.

[7]
At last the march shall end; The wearied ones shall rest;
The pilgrims find their Father's house, Jerusalem the bless'd.

[8]
Then on, ye pure in heart! Rejoice, give thanks and sing!
Your festal banner wave on high, The cross of Christ your King.

songs.title: Rescue the Perishing
songs.author: Fanny Jane Crosby (1820-1915)

songs.title: Rock of Ages
songs.author: Augustus Montague Toplady (1740-1778)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Rock of Ages, cleft for me,
Let me hide myself in Thee;

[1.2]
Let the water and the blood,
From Thy wounded side which flowed,
Be of sin the double cure;
Save from wrath and make me pure.

[2.1]
Not the labor of my hands
Can fulfill Thy law's demands;

[2.2]
Could my zeal no respite know,
Could my tears forever flow,
All for sin could not atone;
Thou must save, and Thou alone.

[3.1]
Nothing in my hand I bring,
Simply to the cross I cling;
Naked, come to Thee for dress;
Helpless look to Thee for grace;

[3.2]
Foul, I to the fountain fly;
Wash me, Savior, or I die.

[4.1]
While I draw this fleeting breath,
When mine eyes shall close in death,
When I soar to worlds unknown,
See Thee on Thy judgment throne,

[4.2]
Rock of Ages, cleft for me,
Let me hide myself in Thee.

songs.title: Salvation Unto Us Has Come
songs.author: Paul Speratus (1484-1551) (trad. composite)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Salvation unto us has come
By God's free grace and favor;
Good works cannot avert our doom,
They help and save us never.

[1.2]
Faith looks to Jesus Christ alone,
Who did for all the world atone;
He is our one Redeemer.

[2.1]
What God did in His law demand
And none to Him could render
Caused wrath and woe on every hand
For man, the vile offender.

[2.2]
Our flesh has not those pure desires
The spirit of the Law requires,
And lost is our condition.

[3.1]
It was a false, misleading dream
That God His Law had given
So sinners could themselves redeem
And by their works gain Heaven.

[3.2]
The Law is but a mirror bright
To bring the inbred sin to light
That lurks within our nature.

[4.1]
From sin our flesh could not abstain
Sin held its sway unceasing;
The task was useless and in vain,
Our guilt was e'er increasing.

[4.2]
None can remove sin's poisoned dart
Or purify our guileful heart?
So deep is our corruption.

songs.title: Savior Of The Nations Come
songs.author: Ambrose of Milan (340-397) (trad. Martin Luther (1483-1546), William Morton Reynolds (1812-1876))
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Savior of the nations, come;
Virgin's Son, here make Thy home!
Marvel now, O heav'n and earth,
That the Lord chose such a birth.

[2]
Not by human flesh and blood;
By the Spirit of our God
Was the Word of God made flesh,
Woman's offspring, pure and fresh.

[3]
Wondrous birth!
O wondrous Child Of the virgin undefiled!
Though by all the world disowned,
Still to be in heaven enthroned.

[4]
From the Father forth He came
And returneth to the same,
Captive leading death and hell
High the song of triumph swell!

[5]
Thou, the Father's only Son,
Hast o'er sin the vict'ry won.
Boundless shall Thy kingdom be;
When shall we its glories see?

[6]
Brightly doth Thy manger shine,
Glorious is its light divine.
Let not sin o'ercloud this light;
Ever be our faith thus bright.

[7]
Praise to God the Father sing,
Praise to God the Son, our King,
Praise to God the Spirit be
Ever and eternally.

songs.title: Savior When In Dust To Thee
songs.author: Robert Grant (1778-1838)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Savior, when in dust to Thee
Low we bow th'adoring knee,
When, repentant, to the skies
Scarce we lift our weeping eyes,

[1.2]
O by all the pains and woes
Suffered once for man below,
Bending from Thy throne on high,
Hear our penitential cry!

[2.1]
By Thy helpless infant years,
By Thy life of want and tears,
By Thy days of sore distress
In the savage wilderness,

[2.2]
By the dread mysterious hour
Of th'insulting tempter's pow'r,
Turn, O turn a fav'ring eye,
Hear our penitential cry!

[3.1]
By the sacred griefs that wept O'er the grave where Laz'rus slept,
By the boding tears that flowed Over Salem's loved abode,
By the anguished sigh that told Treachery lurked within Thy fold,

[3.2]
From Thy seat above the sky,
Hear our penitential cry!

[4.1]
By Thine hour of dire despair,
By Thine agony of prayer,
By the cross, the nail, the thorn,
Piercing spear, and torturing scorn,

[4.2]
By the gloom that veiled the skies
O'er the dreadful sacrifice,
Listen to our humble cry,
Hear our penitential cry!

[5.1]
By Thy deep expiring groan,
By the sad sepulchral stone,
By the vault whose dark abode
Held in vain the rising God,

[5.2]
O from earth to heaven restored,
Mighty, reascended Lord,
Listen, listen to the sigh
Of our penitential cry!

songs.title: Savior, Like A Shepherd Lead Us
songs.author: Dorothy Ann Thrupp (1779-1847)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Savior, like a shepherd lead us,
Much we need Thy tender care;
In Thy pleasant pastures feed us,
For our use Thy folds prepare.

[1.2]
Bless�d Jesus, bless�d Jesus!
Thou hast bought us, Thine we are.
Bless�d Jesus, bless�d Jesus!
Thou hast bought us, Thine we are.

[2.1]
We are Thine, Thou dost befriend us,
Be the guardian of our way;
Keep Thy flock, from sin defend us,
Seek us when we go astray.

[2.2]
Bless�d Jesus, bless�d Jesus!
Hear, O hear us when we pray.
Bless�d Jesus, bless�d Jesus!
Hear, O hear us when we pray.

[3.1]
Thou hast promised to receive us,
Poor and sinful though we be;
Thou hast mercy to relieve us,
Grace to cleanse and pow'r to free.

[3.2]
Bless�d Jesus, bless�d Jesus!
We will early turn to Thee.
Bless�d Jesus, bless�d Jesus!
We will early turn to Thee.

[4.1]
Early let us seek Thy favor,
Early let us do Thy will;
Bless�d Lord and only Savior,
With Thy love our bosoms fill.

[4.2]
Bless�d Jesus, bless�d Jesus!
Thou hast loved us, love us still.
Bless�d Jesus, bless�d Jesus!
Thou hast loved us, love us still.

songs.title: Savior, Who Thy Flock Art Feeding
songs.author: William Augustus M�hlenberg (1796-1877)
songs.composer: Basel, 1745 from Johann Thommen's Musicalischer Christenschatz
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Savior, who Thy flock art feeding
With the Shepherd's kindest care,
All the feeble gently leading,
While the lambs Thy bosom share.

[2]
Now, these little ones receiving,
Fold them in Thy gracious arm;
There, we know, Thy Word believing,
Only there secure from harm.

[3]
Never, from Thy pasture roving,
Let them be the lion's prey;
Let Thy tenderness, so loving,
Keep them through life's dang'rous way.

[4]
Then within Thy fold eternal
Let them find a resting place,
Feed in pastures ever vernal,
Drink the rivers of Thy grace.

songs.title: See Amid the Winter's Snow
songs.author: Edward Caswall (1814-1878)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
See amid the winter's snow,
Born for us on earth below,
See, the gentle Lamb appears,
Promised from eternal years.

[1.2]
Hail that ever bless�d morn,
Hail redemption's happy dawn,
Sing through all Jerusalem:
Christ is born in Bethlehem.

[2]
Lo, within a manger lies He Who built the starry skies;
He Who, thron�d in height sublime,
Sits amid the cherubim.

[3]
Say, you holy shepherds, say,
Tell your joyful news today.
Why have you now left your sheep On the lonely mountain steep?

[4]
"As we watched at dead of night,
Lo, we saw a wondrous light;
Angels singing 'Peace on earth' Told us of the Savior's birth."

[5]
Sacred Infant, all divine,
What a tender love was Thine,
Thus to come from highest bliss Down to
Such a world as this.

[6]
Teach, O teach us, holy Child,
By Thy face so meek and mild,
Teach us to resemble Thee,
In Thy sweet humility.

songs.title: See, The Lord Ascends In Triumph
songs.author: Christopher Wordsworth (1807-1885)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
See, the Lord ascends in triumph;
See the King in royal state,
Riding on the clouds, His chariot,
To His heav'nly palace gate.

[1.2]
Hark! the choirs of angel voices
Joyful alleluias sing,
And the portals high are lifted
To receive their heav'nly King.

[1.3]
Holy Ghost, Illuminator,
Shed Thy beams upon our eyes,
Help us to look up with Stephen,
And to see beyond the skies,

[1.4]
Where the Son of Man in glory
Standing is at God's right hand,
Beck'ning on His martyr army,
Succoring His faithful band.

[2.1]
Who is this that comes in glory,
With the trump of jubilee?
Lord of battles, God of armies,
He has gained the victory.

[2.2]
He Who on the cross did suffer,
He who from the grave arose,
He has vanquished sin and Satan,
He by death has spoiled His foes.

[2.3]
See Him, Who is gone before us,
Heav'nly mansions to prepare,
See Him, who is ever pleading
For us with prevailing prayer,

[2.4]
See Him, who with sound of trumpet,
And with His angelic train,
Summoning the world to judgment,
On the clouds will come again.

[3.1]
While He lifts His hands in blessing,
He is parted from His friends
While their eager eyes behold Him,
He upon the cloud ascends;

[3.2]
He Who walked with God and pleased Him,
Preaching truth and doom to come,
He, our Enoch, is translated
To His everlasting home.

[3.3]
Raise us up from earth to Heaven,
Give us wings of faith and love,
Gales of holy aspirations
Wafting us to realms above;

[3.4]
That, with hearts and minds uplifted,
We with Christ our Lord may dwell,
Where He sits enthroned in glory
In His heav'nly Citadel.

[4.1]
Now our heav'nly Aaron enters,
With His blood, within the veil;
Joshua now is come to Canaan,
And the kings before Him quail;

[4.2]
Now He plants the tribes of Israel
In their promised resting place;
Now our great Elijah offers
Double portion of His grace.

[4.3]
So at last, when He appeareth,
We from out our graves may spring,
With our youth renewed like eagles,
Flocking round our Heav'nly King.

[4.4]
Caught up on the clouds of Heaven,
And may meet Him in the air,
Rise to realms where He is reigning,
And may reign for ever there.

[5.1]
He has raised our human nature
In the clouds to God's right hand;
There we sit in heav'nly places,
There with Him in glory stand:

[5.2]
Jesus reigns, adored by angels;
Man with God is on the throne;
Mighty Lord, in Thine ascension
We by faith behold our own.

[5.3]
Glory be to God the Father,
Glory be to God the Son,
Dying, ris'n, ascending for us,
Who the heav'nly realm has won;

[5.4]
Glory to the Holy Spirit,
To One God in Persons Three;
Glory both in earth and Heaven,
Glory, endless glory, be.

songs.title: Silent Night
songs.author: Josef Mohr (1792-1848) (trad. John Freeman Young (1820-1885))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Silent night, holy night,
All is calm, all is bright Round yon virgin mother and Child.

[1.2]
Holy Infant, so tender and mild,
Sleep in heavenly peace,
Sleep in heavenly peace.

[2.1]
Silent night, holy night,
Shepherds quake at the sight;
Glories stream from heaven afar,
Heavenly hosts sing Alleluia!

[2.2]
Christ the Savior is born,
Christ the Savior is born!

[3.1]
Silent night, holy night,
Son of God, love's pure light;

[3.2]
Radiant beams from Thy holy face
With the dawn of redeeming grace,
Jesus, Lord, at Thy birth,
Jesus, Lord, at Thy birth.

[4.1]
Silent night, holy night Wondrous star, lend thy light;
With the angels let us sing,
Alleluia to our King;

[4.2]
Christ the Savior is born,
Christ the Savior is born!

songs.title: Sing, O Sing, This Blessed Morn
songs.author: Christopher Wordsworth (1807-1885)

songs.title: Songs of Thankfulness and Praise
songs.author: Christopher Wordsworth (1807-1885)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Songs of thankfulness and praise,
Jesus, Lord, to Thee we raise,
Manifested by the star
To the sages from afar;

[1.2]
Branch of royal David's stem
In Thy birth at Bethlehem;
Anthems be to Thee addressed,
God in man made manifest.

[2.1]
Manifest at Jordan's stream,
Prophet, Priest, and King supreme;
And at Cana, wedding guest,
In Thy Godhead manifest;

[2.2]
Manifest in pow'r divine,
Changing water into wine;
Anthems be to Thee addressed,
God in man made manifest.

[3.1]
Manifest in making whole
Palsied limbs and fainting soul;
Manifest in valiant fight,
Quelling all the devil's might;

[3.2]
Manifest in gracious will,
Ever bringing good from ill;
Anthems be to Thee addressed,
God in man made manifest.

[4.1]
Sun and moon shall darkened be,
Stars shall fall, the heav'ns shall flee,
Christ will then like lightning shine,
All will see His glorious sign:

[4.2]
All will then the trumpet hear;
All will see the Judge appear;
Thou by all wilt be confessed,
God in man made manifest.

[5.1]
Grant us grace to see Thee, Lord,
Mirrored in Thy holy Word;
May we imitate Thee now,
And be pure, as pure art Thou;

[5.2]
That we like to Thee may be
At Thy great Epiphany;
And may praise Thee, ever blest,
God in man made manifest.

songs.title: Souls of Men! Why Will Ye Scatter
songs.author: Frederick William Faber (1814-1863)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Souls of men! why will ye scatter
Like a crowd of frightened sheep?
Foolish hearts! why will ye wander
From a love so true and deep?

[1.2]
Was there ever kinder shepherd
Half so gentle, half so sweet,
As the Savior who would have us
Come and gather round His feet?

[2.1]
It is God: His love looks mighty,
But is mighti'r than it seems;
'Tis our Father: and His fondness
Goes far out beyond our dreams.

[2.2]
There's a wideness in God's mercy,
Like the wideness of the sea;
There's a kindness in His justice,
Which is more than liberty.

[3.1]
There is no place where earth's sorrows
Are more felt than up in Heav'n;
There is no place where earth's failings
Have such wondrous judgment giv'n.

[3.2]
There is welcome for the sinner,
Grace poured out as in a flood
There is mercy with the Savior;
There is healing in His blood.

[4.1]
There is grace enough for thousands
Of new worlds as great as this;
There is room for fresh creations
In that upper home of bliss.

[4.2]
For the love of God is broader
Than the measure of man's mind;
And the heart of the Eternal
Is most wonderfully kind.

[5.1]
There is plentiful redemption
In Christ's blood that has been shed;
There is joy for all the members
In the sorrows of the Head.

[5.2]
Not just all we owe to Jesus;
It is something more than all;
Greater good because of evil,
Larger mercy through the fall.

songs.title: Stricken, Smitten, and Afflicted
songs.author: Thomas Kelly (1769-1855)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Stricken, smitten, and afflicted,
See Him dying on the tree!
'Tis the Christ by man rejected;
Yes, my soul, 'tis He, 'tis He!

[1.2]
'Tis the long expected prophet,
David's Son, yet David's Lord;
Proofs I see sufficient of it:
'Tis a true and faithful Word.

[2.1]
Tell me, ye who hear Him groaning,
Was there ever grief like His?
Friends through fear His cause disowning,
Foes insulting his distress:

[2.2]
Many hands were raised to wound Him,
None would interpose to save;
But the deepest stroke that pierced Him
Was the stroke that Justice gave.

[3.1]
Ye who think of sin but lightly,
Nor suppose the evil great,
Here may view its nature rightly,
Here its guilt may estimate.

[3.2]
Mark the Sacrifice appointed!
See Who bears the awful load!
'Tis the Word, the Lord's Anointed,
Son of Man, and Son of God.

[4.1]
Here we have a firm foundation,
Here the refuge of the lost.
Christ the Rock of our salvation,
Christ the Name of which we boast.

[4.2]
Lamb of God for sinners wounded!
Sacrifice to cancel guilt!
None shall ever be confounded
Who on Him their hope have built.

songs.title: Take My Life And Let It Be
songs.author: Frances Ridley Havergal (1836-1879)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Take my life, and let it be
Consecrated, Lord, to Thee.
Take my moments and my days;
Let them flow in ceaseless praise.

[2]
Take my hands, and let them move
At the impulse of Thy love.
Take my feet, and let them be
Swift and beautiful for Thee.

[3]
Take my voice, and let me sing
Always, only, for my King.
Take my lips, and let them be
Filled with messages from Thee.

[4]
Take my silver and my gold;
Not a mite would I withhold.
Take my intellect, and use
Every pow'r as Thou shalt choose.

[5]
Take my will, and make it Thine;
It shall be no longer mine.
Take my heart, it is Thine own;
It shall be Thy royal throne.

[6]
Take my love, my Lord, I pour at Thy feet its treasure store.
Take myself, and I will be ever, only, all for Thee.

songs.title: Take Thou My Hand and Lead Me
songs.author: Julie Katharina von Hausmann (1826-1901) (trad. Julius Herman Edward Horstmann (1869-1954))
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Take Thou my hand, and lead me o'er life's rough way,
With Heav'nly Manna feed me from day to day.
Alone my footsteps falter and straggle wide,
Lord who my life canst alter be Thou my guide.

[2]
Take Thou my heart and hide it in folds of grace
Though pain or woe betide it to know Thy face
Draw, Lord, of Thy good pleasure Thy child to Thee,
And grant me faith's full measure though naught I see.

[3]
Though oft I think Thou hidest Thy wondrous might,
Still to my goal Thou guidest me through dark night,
Take, then, my hands and lead me till life is o'er,
With heav'nly manna feed me forevermore.

songs.title: That Men a godly Life Might Live
songs.author: Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. Richard Massie (1800-1887))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
That man a godly life might live,
God did these ten commandments give
By His true servant Moses, high

[1.2]
Upon the mount Sinai.
Have mercy, Lord.

[2]
I am thy God and Lord alone,
No other God besides Me own;
On My great mercy venture thee,
With all thy heart love thou Me.

[3]
By idle word and speech profane Take not
My holy Name in vain;
And praise not aught as good and true
But what God doth say and do.

[4]
Hallow the day which God hath blest,
That thou and all thy house may rest;
Keep hand and heart from labor free,
That God may so work in thee.

[5]
Give to thy parents honor due,
Be dutiful and loving too;
And help them when their strength decays So
Shalt thou have length of days.

songs.title: The Advent of Our God
songs.author: Charles Coffin (or Carolo or Carolus) (1676-1749) (trad. John Chandler (1806-1876))
songs.lyrics:
[1]
The advent of our God
Shall be our theme for prayer
Come, let us meet him on the road
And place for Him prepare.

[2]
The everlasting Son
Incarnate stoops to be,
Himself the servant's form puts on
To set His people free.

[3]
Come, Zion's daughter, rise
To meet your lowly King,
Nor let your faithless heart despise
The peace He comes to bring.

[4]
As judge, on clouds of light,
He soon will come again
And all His scattered saints unite
With Him on high to reign.

[5]
Before the dawning day
Let sin be put to flight;
No longer let the law hold sway,
But walk in freedom's light.

[6]
All glory to the Son
Who comes to set us free,
With Father, Spirit, ever One,
Through all eternity.

songs.title: The Apostle Looked and Heard a Voice
songs.author: Anthony Robertson (1932-)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Th'Apostle looked and heard a voice,
He saw a Lamb as had been slain;
As angels bowed and saints gave praise These
Words were heard in their refrain.

[1.2]
"There'll be no war or foe to fight,
No searing sun, no dread of night;
No more distress, no more restraint,

[1.3]
No more be weak, no more feel faint.
No more be weak, no more feel faint.

[2.1]
They sigh no more, gone are their fears,
No crying make, shed no more tears;
They grow not old, sense no more loss,
Gone are their doubts and all their dross.

[2.2]
There'll be no sin and no more stain,
Unknown is sickness, gone is pain;
The death of death, no more the hearse,

[2.3]
The end of grief, the end of curse.
The end of grief, the end of curse."

[3.1]
These words are spoken faithfully,
Alpha,
Omega,
Lord is He;

[3.2]
For all is done and done for all,
For all who come, for all who call.

[3.3]
Come see His face,
His hands,
His feet,
Come quench your thirst, partake the Feast,

[3.4]
Come enter in while still you may,
Then Jesus bring Eternal Day.
Then Jesus bring Eternal Day.

songs.title: The Bridegroom Soon Will Call Us
songs.author: Johann Walther (1496-1570) (trad. Matthias Loy (1828-1915))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
The Bridegroom soon will call us,
Come, all ye wedding guests!
May not His voice appall us,
While slumber binds our breasts;

[1.2]
May all our lamps be burning,
And oil be found in store,
That we, with Him returning,
May open find the door.

[2.1]
There shall we see delighted
Our dear Redeemer's face,
Who leads our souls benighted
To glory by His grace;

[2.2]
The patriarchs shall meet us,
The prophets' holy band,
Apostles, martyrs, greet us
In that celestial land.

[3.1]
They will not blush to own us
As brothers, sisters dear,
Love ever will be shown us
When we with them appear;

[3.2]
We all shall come before Him,
Who for us Man became,
As Lord and God adore Him,
And ever bless His Name.

[4.1]
Our Father, rich in blessing,
Will give us crowns of gold
And, to His bosom pressing,
Impart a bliss untold,

[4.2]
Will welcome with embraces
Of never ending love,
And deck us with His graces
In blissful realms above.

[5.1]
In yonder home shall never
Be silent music's voice;
With hearts and lips forever
We shall in God rejoice;

[5.2]
The angels shall adore Him,
All saints shall sing His praise,
And bring with joy before Him
Their sweetest heav'nly lays.

songs.title: The Church's One Foundation
songs.author: Samuel John Stone (1839-1900)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
The Church's one foundation
Is Jesus Christ her Lord,
She is His new creation
By water and the Word.

[1.2]
From heav'n He came and sought her
To be His holy bride;
With His own blood He bought her
And for her life He died.

[2.1]
She is from every nation,
Yet one o'er all the earth;
Her charter of salvation,
One Lord, one faith, one birth;

[2.2]
One holy Name she blesses,
Partakes one holy food,
And to one hope she presses,
With every grace endued.

[3.1]
The Church shall never perish!
Her dear Lord to defend,
To guide, sustain, and cherish,
Is with her to the end:

[3.2]
Though there be those who hate her,
And false sons in her pale,
Against or foe or traitor
She ever shall prevail.

[4.1]
Though with a scornful wonder
Men see her sore oppressed,
By schisms rent asunder,
By heresies distressed:

[4.2]
Yet saints their watch are keeping,
Their cry goes up, 'How long?'
And soon the night of weeping
Shall be the morn of song!

[5.1]
'Mid toil and tribulation,
And tumult of her war,
She waits the consummation
Of peace forevermore;

[5.2]
Till, with the vision glorious,
Her longing eyes are blest,
And the great Church victorious
Shall be the Church at rest.

[6.1]
Yet she on earth hath union
With God the Three in One,
And mystic sweet communion
With those whose rest is won,

[6.2]
With all her sons and daughters
Who, by the Master's hand
Led through the deathly waters,
Repose in Eden land.

[7.1]
O happy ones and holy!
Lord, give us grace that we
Like them, the meek and lowly,
On high may dwell with Thee:

[7.2]
There, past the border mountains,
Where in sweet vales the Bride
With Thee by living fountains
Forever shall abide!

songs.title: The Cloud Received Christ From Their Sight
songs.author: Brian James Dumont (1971-)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
The cloud received Christ from their sight.
They stood, their mouths agape.
Reminded of the things He taught
His people still do wait.

[2]
The cloud kept safe God's people as
Through the dry sea they trod,
And led them through the wilderness;
They truly walked with God!

[3]
On Sinai's height the cloud did rest
To make a home below.
The Ark first then His written Word
His presence now would show.

[4]
Appearing on the mercy seat
Within the inmost place,
The Temple showed God's promises
To save our fallen race.

[5]
On mountain high Christ's face did shine
Like sun, a blazing light.
The cloud once more appeared on earth
A truly fearful sight.

[6]
While here in flesh You taught us, Lord
The object sure and right:
To see our Father's glory bright,
To have eternal life.

[7]
A goal beyond our reach You've shown;
We cannot pay the price.
No work of ours atones for sin,
We cannot set things right.

[8]
You are the Truth, You are the Way
For us to see His face.
You died for us a sinner's death
Abandoned in our place.

[9]
On Easter day, Lord, You were raised
Firstfruits of our new Life;
And in the cloud we see the day
When joy will end all strife.

[10]
We wait to see the cloud's return
To be with us below,
When You fulfill Your promises
To bring us to Your home.

[11]
And though we wait to see You now
We know that You are near.
Your promises to build our faith
Are stronger than our fear.

[12]
You give us faith by Your strong Word
In water, wine, and bread.
The Spirit works through earthly means,
In pastures green we're fed.

songs.title: The Comforter Has Come
songs.author: Frank Bottome (1823-1894)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
O spread the tidings 'round, wherever man is found,
Wherever human hearts and human woes abound;
Let ev'ry Christian tongue proclaim the joyful sound:
The Comforter has come!

[1.2]
The Comforter has come, The Comforter has come!
The Holy Ghost from heav'n, The Father's promise giv'n;
O spread the tidings 'round, Wherever man is found:
The Comforter has come!

[2]
The long, long night is past, the morning breaks at last,
And hush'd the dreadful wail and fury of the blast,
As o'er the golden hills the day advances fast!
The Comforter has come!

[3]
Lo, the great King of kings, with healing in His wings,
To ev'ry captive soul a full deliv'rance brings;
And thro' the vacant cells the song of triumph rings;
The Comforter has come!

[4.1]
O boundless love divine!
How shall this tongue of mine To wond'ring
Mortals tell the matchless grace divine;

[4.2]
That I, a child of hell, should in His image shine!
The Comforter has come!

[5]
Sing, till the echoes fly above the vaulted sky,
And all the saints above to all below reply,
In strains of endless love the song that ne'er will die:
The Comforter has come!

songs.title: The Day is Surely Drawing Near
songs.author: Bartholom�us Ringwaldt (1532-1599) (trad. Phillip Adam Peter (1832-1919))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
The day is surely drawing near,
When God's Son, the Anointed,
Shall with great majesty appear,
As Judge of all appointed.

[1.2]
All mirth and laughter then shall cease
When flames on flames will still increase,
As Scripture truly teacheth.

[2.1]
A trumpet loud shall then resound,
And all the earth be shaken;
Then all who in their graves are found
Shall from their sleep awaken.

[2.2]
But all that live shall in that hour,
By the Almighty's boundless pow'r
Be changed at His commanding.

[3.1]
A book is opened then to all,
A record truly telling
What each hath done, both great and small,
When he on earth was dwelling;

[3.2]
And every heart be clearly seen,
And all be known as they have been,
In thoughts and words and actions.

[4.1]
Then woe to those who scorned the Lord,
And sought but carnal pleasures,
Who here despised His precious Word,
And loved their earthly treasures!

[4.2]
With shame and trembling they will stand,
And at the Judge's stern command
To Satan be delivered.

[5.1]
O Jesus, who my debt didst pay
And for my sin wast smitten
Within the Book of Life, oh, may
My name be also written!

[5.2]
I will not doubt; I trust in Thee,
From Satan Thou hast made me free
And from all condemnation.

songs.title: The First Noel
songs.author: English
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
The first Noel the angel did say Was
To certain poor shepherds in fields as they
Lay;

[1.2]
In fields where they lay tending their sheep,
On a cold winter's night that was so deep.

[1.3]
Noel,
Noel,
Noel,

[1.4]
Noel,
Born is the King of Israel.

[2]
They look�d up and saw a star Shining
In the east, beyond them far;
And to the earth it gave great light,
And so it continued both day and night.

[3]
And by the light of that same star
Three Wise Men came from country far;
To seek for a King was their intent,
And to follow the star wherever it went.

[4]
This star drew nigh to the northwest,
Over Bethlehem it took its rest;
And there it did both stop and stay,
Right over the place where Jesus lay.

[5]
Then did they know assuredly Within that house the King did lie;
One entered it them for to see,
And found the Babe in poverty.

songs.title: The Galilean Fishers Toil
songs.author: Christopher Wordsworth (1807-1885)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
The Galilean fishers toil
All night, and nothing take;
But Jesus comes,- a wondrous spoil
Is lifted from the lake.

[1.2]
Lord, when our labors are in vain
And vain the help of men,
When fruitless is our care and pain,
Come blessed Jesus then!

[2.1]
The night is dark, the surges fill
The bark, the wild winds roar;
But Jesus comes and all is still,-
The ship is at the shore.

[2.2]
O Lord, when storms around us howl,
And all is dark and drear,
In all the tempests of the soul,
O blessed Jesus hear.

[3.1]
A frail one, thrice denying Thee
Saw mercy in Thine eyes,
The penitent upon the tree
Was borne to Paradise.

[3.2]
In hours of sin and deep distress
O show us, Lord, Thy Face,
In penitential loneliness,
O give us Jesus grace!

[4.1]
The faithful few retire in fear
To their closed upper room;
But suddenly with joyful cheer
They see their Master come.

[4.2]
Lord come to us, unloose our bands
And bid our terrors cease,
Lift over us Thy blessed hands,
Speak, holy Jesus Peace!

[5.1]
In days, when faith will scarce be found,
And wolves be in the fold,
When sin and sorrow will abound
And charity wax cold,

[5.2]
Then hear Thy saints, who to Thee pray
To bring them to their home,
Hear when the Bride and Spirit say,
"Come, Blessed Jesus, Come!"

songs.title: The God of Abraham Praise
songs.author: Daniel ben Judah (circa 1400) (trad. Thomas Olivers (1725-1799))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
The God of Abr'ham praise,
Who reigns enthroned above;
Ancient of everlasting days, and God of Love;
Jehovah, great I AM!

[1.2]
By earth and Heav'n confessed;
I bow and bless the sacred Name forever blessed.

[2.1]
The God of Abr'ham praise,
At Whose supreme command
From earth I rise and seek the joys at His right hand;

[2.2]
I all on earth forsake,
Its wisdom, fame, and pow'r;
And Him my only Portion make, my Shield and Tow'r.

[3.1]
The God of Abr'ham praise,
Whose all sufficient grace
Shall guide me all my happy days, in all my ways.

[3.2]
He calls a worm His friend,
He calls Himself my God!
And He shall save me to the end, thro' Jesus' blood.

[4.1]
He by Himself has sworn;
I on His oath depend,
I shall, on eagle wings upborne, to Heav'n ascend.
I shall behold His face;

[4.2]
I shall His pow'r adore,
And sing the wonders of His grace forevermore.

[5.1]
Tho' nature's strength decay,
And earth and hell withstand,
To Canaan's bounds I urge my way, at His command.

[5.2]
The wat'ry deep I pass,
With Jesus in my view;
And thro' the howling wilderness my way pursue.

songs.title: The Gospel Shows The Father's Grace
songs.author: Matthias Loy (1828-1915)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
The Gospel shows the Father's grace,
Who sent his Son to save our race,
Proclaims how Jesus lived and died
That man might thus be justified.

[2]
It sets the Lamb before our eyes,
Who made th'atoning sacrifice,
And calls the souls with guilt oppressed
To come and find eternal rest.

[3]
It brings the Savior's righteousness
Our souls to robe in royal dress;
From all our guilt it brings release
And gives the troubled conscience peace.

[4]
It is the pow'r of God to save
From sin and Satan and the grave;
It works the faith, which firmly clings
To all the treasures which it brings.

[5]
It bears to all the tidings glad
And bids their hearts no more be sad;
The heavy laden souls it cheers
And banishes their guilty fears.

[6]
May we in faith its tidings learn
Nor thanklessly its blessings spurn;
May we in faith its truth confess
And praise the Lord our Righteousness!

songs.title: The King Shall Come
songs.author: unknown (trad. John Brownlie (1857-1925))
songs.lyrics:
[1]
The King shall come when morning dawns,
And light triumphant breaks;
When beauty gilds the eastern hills,
And life to joy awakes.

[2]
Not as of old a little child
To bear, and fight, and die,
But crowned with glory like the sun
That lights the morning sky.

[3]
O brighter than the rising morn
When He, victorious, rose,
And left the lonesome place of death,
Despite the rage of foes.

[4]
O brighter than that glorious morn
Shall this fair morning be,
When Christ, our King, in beauty comes,
And we His face shall see.

[5]
The King shall come when morning dawns,
And earth's dark night is past;
O haste the rising of that morn,
The day that aye shall last.

[6]
And let the endless bliss begin,
By weary saints foretold,
When right shall triumph over wrong,
And truth shall be extolled.

[7]
The King shall come when morning dawns,
And light and beauty brings:
Hail, Christ the Lord! Thy people pray,
Come quickly, King of kings.

songs.title: The Law Of God Is Good And Wise
songs.author: Matthias Loy (1828-1915)
songs.composer: Wittenberg, 1543 from Klug's Geistliche Lieder auffs new gebessert
songs.lyrics:
[1]
The law of God is good and wise,
And sets His will before our eyes,
Shows us the way of righteousness,
And dooms to death when we transgress.

[2]
Its light of holiness imparts
The knowledge of our sinful hearts,
That we may see our lost estate
And seek deliv'rance ere too late.

[3]
To those who help in Christ have found
And would in works of love abound
It shows what deeds are His delight
And should be done as good and right.

[4]
When men the offered help disdain
And willfully in sin remain,
Its terror in their ear resounds
And keeps their wickedness in bounds.

[5]
The law is good, but since the fall
Its holiness condemns us all;
It dooms us for our sin to die
And has no pow'r to justify.

songs.title: The Lily of the Valley
songs.author: Charles William Fry (1838-1882)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
I've found a friend in Jesus,
He's everything to me,
He's the fairest of ten thousand to my soul;

[1.2]
The Lily of the Valley, in Him alone
I see All I need to cleanse and
Make me fully whole.

[1.3]
In sorrow He's my comfort,
In sorrow He's my comfort, in trouble He's my stay;
He tells me every care on Him to roll.
He's the Lily in trouble He's my stay;

[1.4]
He tells me every care on Him to roll.
He's the Lily of the Valley, the Bright and Morning Star,
He's the fairest of ten thousand to my soul.

[2.1]
He all my grief has taken, and all my sorrows borne;
In temptation He's my strong and mighty tow'r;

[2.2]
I'll all for Him forsake now,
I'll all my idols tear From my heart
For now He keeps me by His pow'r.

[2.3]
Though all the world forsake me, and Satan tempt me sore,
Through Jesus I shall safely reach the goal.
He's the Lily

[3.1]
He'll never, never leave me, nor yet forsake me here,
So I live by faith and do His blessed will;

[3.2]
A wall of fire about me,
I've nothing now to fear,
With His manna He my hungry soul shall fill.

[3.3]
When crown'd at last in glory,
I'll see His blessed face,
Where rivers of delight shall ever roll.
He's the Lily

songs.title: The Lord's My Shepherd
songs.author: 1650 from the Scottish Psalter
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
The Lord's my shepherd I'll not want,
He makes me down to lie
In pastures green He leadeth me
The quiet waters by.

[1.2]
He leadeth me, He leadeth me,
The quiet waters by,
In pastures green He leadeth me
The quiet waters by.

[2.1]
My soul He doth restore again,
And me to walk doth make.
Within the paths of blessedness,
E'en for His Own Name's sake;

[2.2]
His Own Name's sake, His Own Name's sake,
E'en for His Own Name's sake;
Within the paths of blessedness,
E'en for His Own Name's sake.

[3.1]
Yea, though I walk in death's dark vale,
Yet will I fear no ill,
For Thou art with me, and Thy rod
And staff me comfort still;

[3.2]
I'll fear no ill, I'll fear no ill,
Yet will I fear no ill,
For Thou art with me, and Thy rod
And staff me comfort still.

[4.1]
My table Thou hast furnished well
In presence of my foes;
My head Thou dost with oil anoint,
And my cup overflows;

[4.2]
It overflows, It overflows,
And my cup overflows;
My head Thou dost with oil anoint,
And my cup overflows.

[5.1]
Goodness and mercy all my days
Will surely follow me:
And in my Father's heart always
My dwelling place shall be;

[5.2]
My dwelling place, My dwelling place,
My dwelling place shall be,
And in my Father's heart always
My dwelling place shall be.

songs.title: The Lord's Prayer (new)
songs.author: Brian L. Penney (1951-)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Father in heaven, Your name we confess,
High and exalted in bright holiness;
O may Your kingdom come, Your will be done,
And may the earth and heav'n be joined as one.

[2]
O Father, now our daily bread supply,
And grant forgiveness for iniquity;
May we forgive as we have been forgiv'n,
Our hearts with mercy filled, as Yours in heav'n.

[3]
O Father, lead us from temptation's pow'r;
May we find safety from sin's trying hour;
I Lord, deliver from the evil one,
All this we ask through Your beloved Son.

songs.title: The Love of God
songs.author: Frederick Martin Lehman (1868-1953)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
The love of God is greater far Than
Tongue or pen can ever tell,
It goes beyond the highest star,
And reaches to the lowest hell;

[1.2]
The guilty pair, bowed down with care,
God gave His Son to win;

[1.3]
His erring child,
He reconciled,
And pardoned from his sin.
Oh love of God, how rich and pure!

[1.4]
How measureless and strong!
It shall forevermore endure,
The saints' and angels' song.

[2.1]
When hoary time shall pass away,
And earthly thrones and kingdoms fall;
When men who here refuse to pray,
On rocks and hills and mountains call;

[2.2]
God's love, so sure, shall still endure,
All measureless and strong;
Redeeming grace to Adam's race- The saints' and angels' song.

[3.1]
Could we with ink the ocean fill,* And
Were the skies of parchment made,
Were every stalk on earth a quill And
Every man a scribe by trade;

[3.2]
To write the love of God above Would drain the ocean dry;
Nor could the scroll contain the whole,
Tho' stretched from sky to sky.

songs.title: The Mouth of Fools Doth God Confess
songs.author: Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. Richard Massie (1800-1887))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
The mouth of fools doth God confess,
But while their lips draw nigh Him,
Their heart is full of wickedness,
And all their deeds deny Him.

[1.2]
Corrupt are they, and every one
Abominable works hath done;
There is not one welldoer.

[2.1]
The Lord looked down from his high tow'r
On all mankind below Him,
To see if any owned His pow'r,
And truly sought to know Him;

[2.2]
Who all their understanding bent
To search His holy Word, intent
To do his will in earnest.

[3.1]
But none there was who walked with God,
For all aside had slidden,
Delusive paths of folly trod,
And followed lusts forbidden;

[3.2]
Not one there was who practiced good,
And yet they deemed, in haughty mood,
Their deeds must surely please Him.

[4.1]
How long, by folly blindly led,
Will ye oppress the needy,
And eat my people up like bread?
So fierce are ye, and greedy!

[4.2]
In God they put no trust at all,
Nor will on Him in trouble call,
But be their own providers.

[5.1]
Therefore their heart is never still,
A falling leaf dismays them;
God is with him who doth His will,
Who trusts him and obeys Him;

[5.2]
But ye the poor man's hope despise,
And laugh at him, e'en when he cries,
That God is his sure comfort.

[6]
Who shall to Israel's outcast race From Zion bring salvation?
God will himself at length show grace, And loose the captive nation;
That will he do by Christ their King; Let Jacob then be
Glad and sing, And Israel be joyful.

songs.title: The Old Rugged Cross
songs.author: George Bennard (1873-1958)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
On a hill far away stood an old rugged cross,
The emblem of suff'ring and shame;
And I love that old cross where the dearest and best
For a world of lost sinners was slain.

[1.2]
So I'll cherish the old rugged cross,
Till my trophies at last I lay down;
I will cling to the old rugged cross,
And exchange it some day for a crown.

[2]
O that old rugged cross, so despised by the world,
Has a wondrous attraction for me;
For the dear Lamb of God left His
Glory above To bear it to dark Calvary.

[3]
In that old rugged cross, stained with blood so divine,
A wondrous beauty I see,
For 'twas on that old cross Jesus suffered and died,
To pardon and sanctify me.

[4]
To the old rugged cross I will ever be true;
Its shame and reproach gladly bear;
Then He'll call me some day to my home far away,
Where His glory forever I'll share.

songs.title: The People That in Darkness Sat
songs.author: John Morison (1746-1798)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
The people that in darkness sat
A glorious light have seen;
The light has shined on them who long

[1.2]
In shades of death have been.
In shades of death have been.

[2.1]
To hail Thee, Sun of Righteousness,
The gath'ring nations come;
They joy as when the reapers bear

[2.2]
Their harvest treasures home.
Their harvest treasures home.

[3.1]
For Thou their burden dost remove
And break the tyrant's rod
As in the day when Midian fell

[3.2]
Before the sword of God.
Before the sword of God.

[4.1]
To us a Child of hope is born,
To us a Son is giv'n,
And on His shoulder ever rests

[4.2]
All pow'r in earth and heav'n.
All pow'r in earth and heav'n.

[5.1]
His name shall be the Prince of Peace,
The Everlasting Lord,
The Wonderful, the Counselor.

[5.2]
The God by all adored.
The God by all adored.

[6]
His righteous government and power
Shall over all extend;
On judgment and on justice based,
His reign shall have no end.

[7]
Lord Jesus, reign in us, we pray,
And make us Thine alone,
Who with the Father ever art
And Holy Spirit, one.

songs.title: The Star Proclaims the King is Here
songs.author: Coelius Sedulius (5th Century) (trad. John Mason Neale (1818-1866))
songs.lyrics:
[1]
The star proclaims the King is here;
But, Herod, why this senseless fear?
He takes no realms of earth away
Who gives the realms of heav'nly day.

[2]
The wiser Magi see from far
And follow on His guiding star;
And led by light, to light they press
And by their gifts their God confess.

[3]
Within the Jordan's crystal flood
In meekness stands the Lamb of God
And, sinless, sanctifies the wave,
Mankind from sin to cleanse and save.

[4]
At Cana first His pow'r is shown;
His might the blushing waters own
And, changing as He speaks the word,
Flow wine, obedient to their Lord.

[5]
All glory, Jesus, be to Thee
For this Thy glad epiphany;
Whom with the Father we adore
And Holy Ghost forevermore.

songs.title: The Strife Is O'er, The Battle Done
songs.author: K�ln, 1695 from Symphonia Sirenum Selectarum (trad. Francis Pott (1832-1909))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Alleluia,
Alleluia,
Alleluia.
The strife is o'er, the battle done;

[1.2]
The triumph of the Lord is won;
O Let the song of praise be sung:
Alleluia!

[1.3]
Alleluia,
Alleluia,
Alleluia.

[2]
The pow'rs of death have done their worst;
And Jesus hath His foes dispersed;
Let shouts of praise and joy outburst:
Alleluia!

[3]
On that third morn He rose again In glorious majesty to reign;
O let us swell the joyful strain.
Alleluia!

[4]
He closed the yawning gates of hell;
The bars from heav'ns high portals fell;
Let songs of joy His triumphs tell.
Alleluia!

[5]
Lord, by the stripes which wounded Thee,
From death's dread sting Thy servants free,
That we may live, and sing to Thee.
Alleluia!

songs.title: The Winds and Billows Loudly Roar
songs.author: Christopher Wordsworth (1807-1885) (trad. %%postscript /st { moveto -8 0 rmoveto 0 8 rlineto 4 0 rlineto stroke } def)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
The winds and billows loudly roar
We flounder in the deep
Our bark is frail, far off the shore,
And Jesus is asleep.

[2]
"Save us, we perish, Lord," they cry;
To Thee we fly for aid;
"Awake! awake!" they say; but why
So faithless and afraid?

[3]
His head is pillow'd on the stern,
As Man He is asleep;
As God He all things does discern,
And endless vigils keep.

[4]
He does the elements control;
By His Almighty Will.
The angry waves their surges roll;
And at His Word are still.

[5]
O ye, who in the Church's Bark
O'er life's rough ocean sail,
When all around is drear and dark,
And human efforts fail,

[6]
Touch not, with rude, irreverent hands,
And coward faithlessness,
Him, who the winds and waves commands;
But wait in quietness.

[7]
O never, never when distressed,
To doubtful means resort;
Christ's Bark, when on the billow's crest,
Is safe as in the port.

songs.title: There's a Great Day Coming
songs.author: Will Lamartine Thompson (1847-1909)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
There's a great day coming, A great day coming,
There's a great day coming by and by;
When the saints and the sinners shall be parted right and left,
Are you ready for that day to come? Are you ready?

[1.2]
Are you ready? Are you ready for the judgment day?
Are you ready? Are you ready? For the judgment day?

[2]
There's a bright day coming,
A bright day coming,
There's a bright day coming by and by;
But its brightness shall only come to them that love the Lord,

[3.1]
There's a sad day coming,
A sad day coming,
There's a sad day coming by and by;

[3.2]
When the sinner shall hear his doom, "Depart,
I know ye not,"

songs.title: Thine Arm, O Lord, in Days of Old
songs.author: Edward Hayes Plumptre (1821-1891)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Thine arm, O Lord, in days of old,
Was strong to heal and save;
It triumphed o'er disease and death,
O'er darkness and the grave.

[1.2]
To Thee they went, the blind, the dumb,
The palsied and the lame,
The leper with his tainted life,
The sick with fevered frame.

[2.1]
And lo! Thy touch brought life and health,
Gave speech, and strength and sight;
And youth renewed and fear relieved
Owned Thee, the Lord of light;

[2.2]
And now, O Lord, be near to bless,
Almighty as of yore,
In crowded street, by restless couch,
As by Gennesaret's shore.

[3.1]
Be Thou our great Deliverer still,
Thou Lord of life and death;
Restore and quicken, soothe and bless,
With Thine almighty breath.

[3.2]
To hands that work and eyes that see,
Give wisdom's heavenly lore,
That whole and sick, and weak and strong,
May praise Thee evermore.

songs.title: Thou, Who at Thy First Eucharist
songs.author: William H. Turton (1856-1938)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Thou, who at Thy first Eucharist didst pray
That all Thy Church might be forever one,
Grant us at ev'ry Eucharist to say
With longing heart and soul, "Thy will be done."

[1.2]
O may we all one bread, one body be,
Through this blest sacrament of unity.

[2.1]
For all Thy Church, O Lord, we intercede;
Make Thou our sad divisions soon to cease;
Draw us the nearer each to each, we plead,
By drawing all to Thee, O Prince of Peace;

[2.2]
Thus may we all one bread, one body be,
Through this blest sacrament of unity.

[3.1]
We pray Thee too for wand'rers from Thy fold;
O bring them back, good Shepherd of the sheep,
Back to the faith which saints believed of old,
Back to the Church which still that faith doth keep;

[3.2]
Soon may we all one bread, one body be,
Through this blest sacrament of unity.

[4.1]
So, Lord, at length when sacraments shall cease,
May we be one with all Thy Church above,
One with Thy saints in one unbroken peace,
One with Thy saints in one unbounded love;

[4.2]
More bless�d still, in peace and love to be
One with the Trinity in unity.

songs.title: Though in the Midst of Life We Be
songs.author: Medieval, Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. Richard Massie (1800-1887))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Though in midst of life we be,
Snares of death surround us;
Where shall we for succor flee,
Lest our foes confound us?

[1.2]
To Thee alone, our Savior.
We mourn our grievous sin which hath Stirr'd
The fire of Thy fierce wrath.
Holy and gracious God!

[1.3]
Holy and mighty God!
Holy and all- merciful Savior!
Thou eternal God!

[1.4]
Save us,
Lord, from sinking In the deep and bitter flood.
Kyrie eleison.

[2.1]
Whilst in midst of death we be,
Hell's grim jaws o'ertake us;
Who from such distress will free.
Who secure will make us?

[2.2]
Thou only,
Lord, canst do it!
It moves Thy tender heart to see Our great sin and misery.
Savior!

[2.3]
Thou eternal God!
Let not hell dismay us With its deep and burning flood.
Kyrie eleison.

[3.1]
Into hell's fierce agony Sin doth headlong drive us:
Where shall we for succor flee,
Who,
O, who will hide us?

[3.2]
Thou only, blessed Saviour.
Thy precious blood was shed to win Peace
And pardon for our sin.
Savior!

[3.3]
Let us not, we pray,
From the true faith's comfort Fall in our last need away.
Kyrie eleison.

songs.title: Through the Night of Doubt and Sorrow
songs.author: Bernhardt Severin Ingemann (1789-1862) (trad. Sabine Baring Gould (1834-1924))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Through the night of doubt and sorrow
Onward goes the pilgrim band,
Singing songs of expectation,
Marching to the Promised Land.

[1.2]
Clear before us through the darkness
Gleams and burns the guiding light:
Brother clasps the hand of brother,
Stepping fearless through the night.

[2.1]
One the light of God's own presence,
O'er His ransomed people shed,
Chasing far the gloom and terror,
Bright'ning all the path we tread:

[2.2]
One the object of our journey,
One the faith which never tires,
One the earnest looking forward,
One the hope our God inspires.

[3.1]
One the strain that lips of thousands
Lift as from the heart of one;
One the conflict, one the peril
One the march in God begun:

[3.2]
One the gladness of rejoicing
On the far eternal shore,
Where the One Almighty Father
Reigns in love for evermore.

[4.1]
Onward, therefore, pilgrim brothers,
Onward, with the cross our aid!
Bear its shame, and fight its battle,
Till we rest beneath its shade.

[4.2]
Soon shall come the great awaking,
Soon the rending of the tomb;
Then the scatt'ring of all shadows,
And the end of toil and gloom.

songs.title: Tis Good, Lord, To Be Here
songs.author: Joseph Armitage Robinson (1858-1933)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
'Tis good, Lord, to be here,
Thy glory fills the night;
Thy face and garments, like the sun,
Shine with unborrowed light.

[2]
'Tis good, Lord, to be here,
Thy beauty to behold
Where Moses and Elijah stand,
Thy messengers of old.

[3]
Fulfiller of the past,
Promise of things to be,
We hail Thy body glorified
And our redemption see.

[4]
Before we taste of death,
We see Thy Kingdom come;
We fain would hold the vision bright
And make this hill our home.

[5]
'Tis good, Lord, to be here.
Yet we may not remain;
But since Thou bidst us leave the mount,
Come with us to the plain.

songs.title: To Avert From Men God's Wrath
songs.author: John Hus (1369-1415) (trad. Christian Ignatius Latrobe (1758-1836))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
To avert from men God's wrath
Jesus suffered in our stead;
By an ignominious death
He a full atonement made;

[1.2]
And by His most precious blood,
Brought us, sinners, nigh to God.

[2.1]
That we never should forget
This great Love on us bestowed,
He gave us His flesh to eat,
And to drink His precious blood;

[2.2]
All who sick and needy are
May receive in Him a share.

[3.1]
Hither each afflicted soul
May repair, though filled with grief;
To the sick, not to the whole,
The Physician brings relief;

[3.2]
Fear not, therefore, but draw nigh,
Christ will all your wants supply.

[4.1]
He who in self- righteousness
Fixes any hope or stay,
Has not on a wedding dress,
And with shame is sent away;

[4.2]
To the hungry, weary heart,
He will food and rest impart.

[5.1]
But examine first your case,
Whether you be in the faith;
Do you long for pard'ning grace?
Is your only hope His death?

[5.2]
Then, howe'er your soul's oppressed,
Come, you are a worthy guest.

[6]
He who Jesus' mercy knows, Is from wrath and envy freed;
Love unto our neighbor shows That we are His flock indeed;
Thus we may in all our ways Show forth our Redeemer's praise.

songs.title: To God Be The Glory
songs.author: Fanny Jane Crosby (1820-1915)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
To God be the glory, great things He has done;
So loved He the world that He gave us His Son
Who yielded His life an atonement for sin,
And opened the life gate that all may go in.

[1.2]
Praise the Lord, praise the Lord, Let the earth hear His voice!
Praise the Lord, praise the Lord, Let the people rejoice!
O come to the Father, through Jesus the Son,
And give Him the glory, great things He has done.

[2]
O perfect redemption, the purchase of blood,
To every believer the promise of God;
The vilest offender who truly believes,
That moment from Jesus a pardon receives.

[3]
Great things He has taught us, great things He has done,
And great our rejoicing through Jesus the Son;
But purer, and higher, and greater will be
Our wonder, our transport, when Jesus we see.

songs.title: To Jordan Came Our Lord, The Christ
songs.author: Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. Richard Massie (1800-1887))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
To Jordan came our Lord the Christ,
To do God's pleasure willing,
And there was by Saint John baptized,
All righteousness fulfilling;

[1.2]
There did He consecrate a bath
To wash away transgression,
And quench the bitterness of death

[1.3]
By His own blood and passion;
He would a new life give us.

[2.1]
So hear ye all, and well perceive
What God doth call baptism,
And what a Christian should believe
Who error shuns and schism:

[2.2]
That we should water use, the Lord
Declareth it His pleasure;
Not simple water, but the Word

[2.3]
And Spirit without measure;
He is the true Baptizer.

[3.1]
To show us this, He hath His Word
With signs and symbols given;
On Jordan's banks was plainly heard
The Father's voice from Heaven:

[3.2]
"This is My well- beloved Son,
In whom My soul delighteth;

[3.3]
Hear Him." Yea, hear Him every one
Whom He Himself inviteth,
Hear and obey His teaching.

[4.1]
In tender manhood Jesus straight
To holy Jordan wendeth;
The Holy Ghost from Heaven's gate
In dovelike shape descendeth;

[4.2]
That thus the truth be not denied,
Nor should our faith e'er waver,
That the Three Persons all preside,

[4.3]
At baptism's holy laver,
And dwell with the believer.

[5.1]
Thus Jesus His disciples sent:
Go teach ye every nation,
That lost in sin they must repent;
And flee from condemnation:

[5.2]
He that believes and is baptized,
Obtains a mighty blessing;

[5.3]
A newborn man, no more he dies,
Eternal life possessing,
A joyful heir of Heaven.

songs.title: To Shepherds As They Watched By Night
songs.author: Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. Richard Massie (1800-1887))
songs.lyrics:
[1]
To shepherds as they watched by night
Appeared a host of angels bright;
Behold the tender Babe, they said,
In yonder lowly manger laid.

[2]
At Bethlehem, in David's town,
As Micah did of old make known;
'Tis Jesus Christ, your Lord and King,
Who doth to all salvation bring.

[3]
Oh, then rejoice that through His Son
God is with sinners now at one;
Made like yourselves of flesh and blood,
Your Brother is th'eternal God.

[4]
What harm can sin and death then do?
The true God now abides with you.
Let hell and Satan rage and chafe,
Christ is your Brother ye are safe.

[5]
Not one He will or can forsake
Who Him his confidence doth make.
Let all his wiles the Tempter try,
You may his utmost pow'rs defy.

[6]
Ye shall and must at last prevail;
God's own ye are, ye cannot fail.
To God forever sing your praise
With joy and patience all your days.

songs.title: Today Thy Mercy Calls Me
songs.author: Oswald Allen (1816-1878)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Today Thy mercy calls me
To wash away my sin;
However great my trespass,
Whate'er I may have been;

[1.2]
However long from mercy
I may have turned away,
Thy blood, O Christ, can wash me,
And make me clean today.

[2.1]
Today Thy gate is open,
And all who enter in
Shall find a Father's welcome,
And pardon for their sin;

[2.2]
The past shall be forgotten,
A present joy be given;
A future grace be promised,
A glorious crown in Heav'n.

[3.1]
Today the Father calls me,
The Holy Spirit waits,
The bless�d angels gather
Around the heav'nly gates;

[3.2]
No question will be asked me,
How often I have come;
Although I oft have wandered,
It is my Father's home.

[4.1]
O all embracing mercy,
Thou ever open door,
What shall I do without thee
When heart and eyes run o'er?

[4.2]
When all things seem against me,
To drive me to despair,
I know one gate is open,
One ear will hear my prayer.

songs.title: Twas In The Moon of Wintertime
songs.author: Jean de Br�beuf (1593-1649) (trad. Jesse Edgar Middleton (1872-1960))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
'Twas in the moon of wintertime,
When all the birds had fled,
That mighty Gitchi Manitou
Sent angel choirs instead;

[1.2]
Before their light the stars grew dim,
And wand'ring hunters heard the hymn:

[1.3]
Jesus your King is born,
Jesus is born,
In excelsis gloria.

[2]
Within a lodge of broken bark The tender babe was found,
A ragged robe of rabbit skin Enwrapped His beauty 'round;
But as the hunter braves drew nigh,
The angel song rang loud and high:

[3.1]
The earliest moon of wintertime Is not so
Round and fair As was the ring of
Glory on The helpless Infant there.

[3.2]
The chiefs from far before Him knelt With
Gifts of fox and beaver pelt.

[4.1]
Oh children of the forest free,
Oh sons of Manitou,
The holy Child of earth and Heav'n Is born today for you.

[4.2]
Come kneel before the radiant Boy,
Who brings you beauty, peace and joy.

songs.title: Under His Wings
songs.author: William Orcutt Cushing (1823-1902)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Under His wings I am safely abiding,
Though the night deepens and tempests are wild,
Still I can trust Him; I know He will keep me,
He has redeemed me, and I am His child.

[1.2]
Under His wings, under His wings,
Who from His love can sever?
Under His wings my soul shall abide,
Safely abide forever.

[2]
Under His wings, what a refuge in sorrow!
How the heart yearningly turns to His rest!
Often when earth has no balm for my healing,
There I find comfort, and there I am blessed.

[3.1]
Under His wings, oh, what precious enjoyment!
There will I hide till life's trials are o'er;

[3.2]
Sheltered, protected, no evil can harm me,
Resting in Jesus,
I'm safe evermore.

songs.title: Wake, Awake, for Night Is Flying
songs.author: Phillipp Nicolai (1556-1608) (trad. Catherine Winkworth (1827-1878))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Wake, awake, for night is flying;
The watchmen on the heights are crying:
Awake, Jerusalem, at last!

[1.2]
Midnight hears the welcome voices
And at the thrilling cry rejoices;
Come forth, ye virgins, night is past;
The Bridegroom comes, awake;

[1.3]
Your lamps with gladness take;
Alleluia!
And for His marriage feast prepare
For ye must go and meet Him there.

[2.1]
Zion hears the watchmen singing,
And all her heart with joy is springing;
She wakes, she rises from her gloom;

[2.2]
For her Lord comes down all glorious,
The strong in grace, in truth victorious.
Her Star is ris'n, her Light is come.

[2.3]
Ah come, Thou blessed One,
God's own beloved Son:
Alleluia!

[2.4]
We follow till the halls we see
Where Thou hast bid us sup with Thee

[3.1]
Now let all the heav'ns adore Thee,
And saints and angels sing before Thee,
With harp and cymbal's clearest tone;

[3.2]
Of one pearl each shining portal,
Where we are with the choir immortal
Of angels round Thy dazzling throne;

[3.3]
Nor eye hath seen, nor ear
Hath yet attained to hear
What there is ours,

[3.4]
But we rejoice and sing to Thee
Our hymn of joy eternally.

songs.title: We All Believe in One True God
songs.author: Medieval, Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. composite)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
We all believe in one true God,
Who created earth and heaven,
The Father, who to us in love
Hath the right of children given.

[1.2]
He both soul and body feedeth,
All we need He doth provide us;
He through snares and perils leadeth,
Watching that no harm betide us.

[1.3]
He careth for us day and night,
All things are governed by His might.

[2.1]
We all believe in Jesus Christ,
His own Son, our Lord, possessing
An equal Godhead, throne, and might,
Source of every grace and blessing.

[2.2]
Born of Mary, virgin mother,
By the power of the Spirit,
Made true man, our elder Brother,
That the lost might life inherit;

[2.3]
Was crucified for sinful men
And raised by God to life again.

[3.1]
We all confess the Holy Ghost,
Who sweet grace and comfort giveth
And with the Father and the Son
In eternal glory liveth;

[3.2]
Who the Church, His own creation,
Keeps in unity of spirit.
Here forgiveness and salvation
Daily come through Jesus' merit.

[3.3]
All flesh shall rise, and we shall be
In bliss with God eternally.

songs.title: We Gather Together
songs.author: unknown (trad. Theodore Baker (1851-1934))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
We gather together to ask the Lord's blessing;
He chastens and hastens His will to make known.
The wicked oppressing now cease from distressing.

[1.2]
Sing praises to His Name;
He forgets not His own.

[2.1]
Beside us to guide us,
Our God with us joining,
Ordaining, maintaining
His kingdom divine;

[2.2]
So from the beginning
The fight we were winning;
Thou, Lord, were at our side,
All glory be Thine!

[3.1]
We all do extol Thee,
Thou Leader triumphant,
And pray that Thou still our
Defender will be.

[3.2]
Let Thy congregation
Escape tribulation;
Thy Name be ever praised!
O Lord, make us free!

songs.title: We Give Thee But Thine Own
songs.author: William Walsham How (1823-1897)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
We give Thee but Thine own,
Whate'er the gift may be;
All that we have is Thine alone,
A trust, O Lord, from Thee.

[2]
May we Thy bounties thus
As stewards true receive,
And gladly, as Thou blessest us,
To Thee our firstfruits give.

[3]
O hearts are bruised and dead,
And homes are bare and cold,
And lambs for whom the Shepherd bled
Are straying from the fold.

[4]
To comfort and to bless,
To find a balm for woe,
To tend the lone and fatherless
Is angels' work below.

[5]
The captive to release,
To God the lost to bring,
To teach the way of life and peace?
It is a Christlike thing.

[6]
And we believe Thy Word,
Though dim our faith may be;
Whate'er for Thine we do, O Lord,
We do it unto Thee.

songs.title: We Know Thee Who Thou Art
songs.author: William Bright (1824-1901)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
We know Thee who Thou art,
Lord Jesus, Mary's Son;
We know the yearnings of Thy heart
To end Thy work begun.

[2]
That sacred fount of grace,
'Mid all the bliss of Heav'n,
Has joy whene'er we seek Thy face,
And kneel to be forgiv'n.

[3]
Brought home from ways perverse,
At peace Thine arms within,
We pray Thee, shield us from the curse
Of falling back to sin.

[4]
We dare not ask to live
Henceforth from trials free;
But oh! when next they tempt us, give
More strength to cling to Thee.

[5]
We know Thee who Thou art,
Our own redeeming Lord;
Be Thou by will, and mind, and heart,
Accepted, loved, adored.

songs.title: We Now Implore God the Holy Ghost
songs.author: German, Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. composite)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
We now implore God the Holy Ghost
For the true faith, which we need the most,
That in our last moments He may befriend us

[1.2]
And, as homeward we journey, attend us.
Lord, have mercy.

[2.1]
Shine in our hearts, O most precious Light,
That we Jesus Christ may know aright,
Clinging to our Savior, whose blood hath bought us.

[2.2]
Who again to our homeland hath brought us.
Lord, have mercy.

[3.1]
Thou sacred Love, grace on us bestow,
Set our hearts with heav'nly fire aglow
That with hearts united we love each other,

[3.2]
Of one mind, in peace with ev'ry brother.
Lord, have mercy!

[4.1]
Thou highest Comfort in ev'ry need,
Grant that neither shame nor death we heed,
That e'en then our courage may never fail us

[4.2]
When the Foe shall accuse and assail us.
Lord, have mercy!

songs.title: Were You There?
songs.author: African-American
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Were you there when they crucified my Lord?
Were you there when they crucified my Lord?
Sometimes it causes me to tremble, tremble, tremble.
Were you there when they crucified my Lord?

[2]
Were you there when they nailed Him to the tree?
Were you there when they nailed Him to the tree?
Were you there when they nailed Him to the tree?

[3]
Were you there when they pierced Him in the side?
Were you there when they pierced Him in the side?
Oh!
Were you there when they pierced Him in the side?

[4]
Were you there when the sun refused to shine?
Were you there when the sun refused to shine?
Were you there when the sun refused to shine?

[5]
Were you there when they laid Him in the tomb?
Were you there when they laid Him in the tomb?
Were you there when they laid Him in the tomb?

[6]
Were you there when God raised Him from the tomb?
Were you there when God raised Him from the tomb?
Oh! Sometimes it causes me to tremble, tremble, tremble.
Were you there when God raised Him from the tomb?

songs.title: What A Friend We Have In Jesus
songs.author: Joseph Medlicott Scriven (1819-1886)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
What a Friend we have in Jesus,
All our sins and griefs to bear!
What a privilege to carry
Everything to God in prayer!

[1.2]
O what peace we often forfeit,
O what needless pain we bear,
All because we do not carry
Everything to God in prayer.

[2.1]
Have we trials and temptations?
Is there trouble anywhere?
We should never be discouraged;
Take it to the Lord in prayer.

[2.2]
Can we find a friend so faithful
Who will all our sorrows share?
Jesus knows our every weakness;
Take it to the Lord in prayer.

[3.1]
Are we weak and heavy laden,
Cumbered with a load of care?
Precious Savior, still our refuge,
Take it to the Lord in prayer.

[3.2]
Do your friends despise, forsake you?
Take it to the Lord in prayer!
In His arms He'll take and shield you;
You will find a solace there.

[4.1]
Blessed Savior, Thou hast promised
Thou wilt all our burdens bear
May we ever, Lord, be bringing
All to Thee in earnest prayer.

[4.2]
Soon in glory bright unclouded
There will be no need for prayer
Rapture, praise and endless worship
Will be our sweet portion there.

songs.title: What Child Is This?
songs.author: William Chatterton Dix (1837-1865)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
What Child is this who, laid to rest
On Mary's lap is sleeping?
Whom angels greet with anthems sweet,
While shepherds watch are keeping?

[1.2]
This, this is Christ the King,
Whom shepherds guard and angels sing;
Haste, haste, to bring Him laud,
The Babe, the Son of Mary.

[2.1]
Why lies He in such mean estate,
Where ox and ass are feeding?
Good Christians, fear, for sinners here
The silent Word is pleading.

[2.2]
Nails, spear shall pierce Him through,
The cross be borne for me, for you.
Hail, hail the Word made flesh,
The Babe, the Son of Mary.

[3.1]
So bring Him incense, gold and myrrh,
Come peasant, king to own Him;
The King of kings salvation brings,
Let loving hearts enthrone Him.

[3.2]
Raise, raise a song on high,
The virgin sings her lullaby.
Joy, joy for Christ is born,
The Babe, the Son of Mary.

songs.title: When I Survey the Wondrous Cross
songs.author: Isaac Watts (1674-1748)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
When I survey the wondrous cross
On which the Prince of Glory died,
My richest gain I count but loss,
And pour contempt on all my pride.

[2]
Forbid it, Lord, that I should boast,
Save in the death of Christ my God!
All the vain things that charm me most,
I sacrifice them to His blood.

[3]
See from His head, His hands, His feet,
Sorrow and love flow mingled down!
Did e'er such love and sorrow meet,
Or thorns compose so rich a crown?

[4]
His dying crimson, like a robe,
Spreads o'er His body on the tree;
Then I am dead to all the globe,
And all the globe is dead to me.

[5]
Were the whole realm of nature mine,
That were a present far too small;
Love so amazing, so divine,
Demands my soul, my life, my all.

songs.title: When The Roll Is Called Up Yonder
songs.author: James Milton Black (1856-1938)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
When the trumpet of the Lord shall sound,
And time shall be no more,
And the morning breaks, eternal, bright and fair;

[1.2]
When the saved of earth shall gather over on the other shore,
And the roll is called up yonder,
I'll be there.

[1.3]
When the roll is called up yonder,
When the roll When the roll is called up yonder,
I'll be there,
When the roll is called up yonder,

[1.4]
When the roll is called up is called up yonder,
I'll be there,
When the roll is called up yonder,

[1.5]
When the roll is called up yonder,
I'll be there.

[2]
On that bright and cloudless morning when the
Dead in Christ shall rise,
And the glory of His resurrection share;
When His chosen ones shall gather to their home beyond the skies,

[3]
Let us labor for the Master from the dawn till setting sun,
Let us talk of all His wondrous love and care;
Then when all of life is over, and
Our work on earth is done,

songs.title: Where He Leads Me
songs.author: Edward William Blandy
songs.composer: John Samuel Norris (1844-1907), Philip Paul Bliss (1838-1876)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
I can hear my Savior calling,
I can hear my Savior calling,
I can hear my Savior calling,
"Take thy cross and follow, follow Me."

[1.2]
Where He leads me I will follow,
Where He leads me I will follow,
Where He leads me I will follow;
I'll go with Him, with Him, all the way.

[2]
I'll go with Him through the garden,
I'll go with Him through the garden,
I'll go with Him through the garden,
I'll go with Him, with Him all the way.

[3]
I'll go with Him through the judgment,
I'll go with Him through the judgment,
I'll go with Him through the judgment,
I'll go with Him, with Him all the way.

[4]
He will give me grace and glory,
He will give me grace and glory,
He will give me grace and glory,
And go with me, with me all the way.

songs.title: While O'er Our Guilty Land, O Lord
songs.author: Samuel Davies (1723-1761), Brian James Dumont (1971-)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
While o'er our guilty land, O Lord,
We view the terrors of Your sword,
O where can all the helpless fly?
To whom but You direct their cry?

[2]
On You, our guardian God, we call;
Before Your throne of grace we fall;
But is there no deliv'rance there?
And must we perish in despair?

[3]
See, we repent, we weep, we mourn;
To our forsaken God we turn;
O spare our guilty country, spare
The Church which You have planted there.

[4]
We are the old, the sick, the lame;
We blind and deaf cry Jesus' Name.
We plead Your mercy for His sake,
And trust that You will not forsake.

[5]
Christ is our only righteousness,
His death for us is our redress.
Your promise stronger than our sin;
Blot out O Lord what we have been.

[6]
We are your children after all,
Redeemed by Christ after the fall.
Marked with Your Name in Baptism,
Our home remains in Your Kingdom.

songs.title: Whiter Than Snow
songs.author: James L. Nicholson (1828-1876)
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Lord Jesus, I long to be perfectly whole;
I want Thee forever to live in my soul,
Break down ev'ry idol, cast out ev'ry foe;
Now wash me and I shall be whiter than snow.

[1.2]
Whiter than snow, yes, whiter than snow;
Now wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.

[2]
Lord Jesus, look down from Thy throne in the skies,
And help me to make a complete sacrifice;
I give up myself, and whatever I know,
Now wash me and I shall be whiter than snow.

[3.1]
Lord Jesus, for this I most humbly entreat,
I wait, blessed Lord, at Thy crucified feet,
By faith, for my cleansing,

[3.2]
I see Thy blood flow,
Now wash me and I shall be whiter than snow.

[4.1]
Lord Jesus,
Thou seest I patiently wait,
Come now, and within me a new heart create;

[4.2]
To those who have sought Thee,
Thou never said'st ``No,'' Now wash me and
I shall be whiter than snow.

songs.title: Wilt Thou, O Man, Live Happily
songs.author: Martin Luther (1483-1546) (trad. Richard Massie (1800-1887))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Wilt thou, O man, live happily,
And dwell with God eternally,
The ten commandments keep, for thus

[1.2]
Our God Himself biddeth us.
Kyr' eleison!

[2]
I am the Lord and God!
Take heed No other god doth thee mislead;
Thy heart shall trust alone in Me,
My kingdom then thou shalt be.

[3]
Honor My Name in word and deed,
And call on Me in time of need:
Hallow the Sabbath, that I may Work in
Thy heart on that day.

[4.1]
Obedient always, next to Me,
To father and to mother be;
Kill no man:

[4.2]
Even anger dread;
Keep sacred thy marriage bed.

[5]
Steal not, nor do thy neighbor wrong By
Bearing witness with false tongue;
Thy neighbor's wife desire thou not,
Nor grudge him aught he hath got.

songs.title: Within the Father's House
songs.author: James Russell Woodford (1820-1885)
songs.lyrics:
[1]
Within the Father's house
The Son hath found His home;
And to His temple suddenly
The Lord of Life hath come.

[2]
The doctors of the law
Gaze on the wondrous child,
And marvel at His gracious words
Of wisdom undefiled.

[3]
Yet not to them is giv'n
The mighty truth to know,
To lift the fleshly veil which hides
Incarnate God below.

[4]
The secret of the Lord
Escapes each human eye,
And faithful pond'ring hearts await
The full epiphany.

[5]
Lord, visit Thou our souls,
And teach us by Thy grace
Each dim revealing of Thyself
With loving awe to trace;

[6]
Till from our darkened sight
The cloud shall pass away,
And on the cleans�d soul shall burst
The everlasting day.

[7]
Till we behold Thy face,
And know, as we are known,
Thee, Father, Son, and Holy Ghost,
Co-equal Three in One.

songs.title: Yet Before We See Your Plans
songs.author: Brian James Dumont (1971-)
songs.composer: William Moore (19th Century), 1825 from Columbian Harmony
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
Yet before we see Your plans, Lord;
While the path is still unknown
Bless us Lord to shout Your praises,
May Your work through us be shown.

[1.2]
Give us faith to trust Your mercy,
Make us confident to be
Called and holy as Your Church who
Shout and sing Your victory.

[2]
Marching round the walls of Jer'cho Went Your trumpeted parade.
Celebrating Your great triumph E'en before it was displayed.

[3]
With four armies bearing on them King Jehoshaphat
Would send First the band to sing your
Praises,
Thus Your glory to extend.

[4]
On that night before He died The Lord
To You would raise a hymn He would
Sing Your praise and mercy E'en before the
Battle grim.

[5]
And we lowly helpless few harassed and fettered
By our sin More than conquerors in Christ
For He did our salvation win.

[6.1]
All around us Lord we see a
World that spins and spirals down.
While our hindered human eyes can't
See You turning us around.

[6.2]
Give us faith to trust Your mercy,
Make us confident to be
Called and holy as Your Church who
Shout and sing Your victory.

[7.1]
In our lives and times so broken
By our sin and willful pride
Or just with uncertainty, Your
Plans You often seem to hide,

[7.2]
Give us faith to trust Your mercy,
Make us confident to be
Called and holy as Your Church who
Shout and sing Your victory.

songs.title: You Parents Hear What Jesus Taught
songs.author: Ludwig Helmbold (1532-1598) (trad. William Martin Czamanske (1873-1964))
songs.lyrics:
[1]
You parents, hear what Jesus taught
When little ones to him were brought:
Forbid them not, but heed my plea
Permitting them to come to me.

[2]
Obey your Lord and let his truth
Be taught your children in their youth
That they in church and school may dwell
And learn their Savior's praise to tell.

[3]
For if you love them as you ought,
To Christ your children will be brought.
If thus you place them in his care,
All in your family well shall fare.

songs.title: You People Who Now Are Baptized
songs.author: Paul Gerhardt (1607-1676) (trad. Brian James Dumont (1971-))
songs.lyrics:
[1.1]
You people who now are baptized
God's gracious love surrounds you.
By Christ's Name you're now recognized;
Ponder what happened to you:

[1.2]
Whose work was it which fashioned you,
Whose inborn nature that He slew,
When you first gained His promise?

[2.1]
Before held in your mother's arm,
From your time of conception,
Quite hostile to the Law's alarms-
Let there be no deception.

[2.2]
A sinner born of sinner's seed;
Still God Himself for you would bleed,
He took on flesh to save you.

[3.1]
Your soul and body turned within,
Sin filled you like a poison.
Concern for neighbor paperthin;
God's love was simply foreign.

[3.2]
Then raised by God the Lord of Life
To glow in His eternal Light
Your robe of white is gleaming.

[4.1]
The majesty that terrifies
Was all God's presence brought you.
Your fault you could not rectify;
Anxiety consumed you.

[4.2]
A slave of sin and Satan held
Trapped in a prison bound for hell
Death was your only future.

[5.1]
Then washed clean in this holy flood,
The water of Baptism;

[5.2]
Instilled faith in Christ's holy blood
Brought to the Father's Kingdom,
Your heart rebuilt within your breast,

[5.3]
New nature filled with righteousness,
Your every sin forgiven!

[6.1]
It washes all your sins away
And makes you pure and holy.
Hell's hold on you was lost that day,
God's freedom for the lowly.

[6.2]
You are now truly God's dear child
An heir of heaven undefiled
With crown to cast before Him.

[7.1]
Your nature lost in Adam's fall,
Corrupt through generations,
Refreshed now in the waterfall-
A perfect new creation!

[7.2]
The death of death before your eyes:
God's power must be recognized.
Hell's demons lie defeated!

[8.1]
Now we can gladly draw to Christ
And boldly ask His blessing
Because of Jesus' sacrifice,
Our sins upon Him pressing.

[8.2]
The Father looks on us and sees
Christ's holiness and His good deeds:
White robes giv'n by His merit.

[9.1]
This holy bath ... What pow'r displays!
What wondrous grace-filled cleansing;
None on their own can e'er appraise
The value of their raising.

[9.2]
The Word of God in simple form
Can calm the tempest and the storm.
It brings peace to your spirit.

[10.1]
Plain water cannot wash our sin
Nor clean our inward spirit,
But water with God's promise can
Bring all the Father wills it.

[10.2]
The water that floods over you
From God's command has strength imbued.
His Name is placed upon you.

[11.1]
Too precious to repay somehow,
Just grateful thanks we offer.
Christ's work has been delivered now
To you through Word and water.

[11.2]
Nothing but Christ's atoning work
In you could kill death's ugly smirk
You're now refreshed and holy.

[12.1]
Now gladly live as God's dear child
Proclaim to all His Gospel
Shine to the world; be undefiled...
A beacon to all people.

[12.2]
Till called home to eternal joy
With new song that we'll all employ
To cast our crowns before Him.
